title: 威尼斯商人
author: William Shakespeare 威廉·莎士比亞
description: 《The Merchant of Venice》(約1596)。威尼斯商人安東尼奧為幫朋友巴薩尼奧追求貝爾蒙特嘅富家女鮑西婭,向猶太放貸人夏洛克借款,以「一磅肉」作抵押;商船失事後對簿公堂,鮑西婭女扮律師,以智慧破解契約。全劇五幕二十場,每段對白標示說話者,英文原文對照廣東話/普通話翻譯。

chapters.title: Act I, Scene I — Venice. A Street 第一幕第一場:威尼斯街道

passages.original: Enter Antonio, Salarino and Solanio.
passages.vernacular: [安東尼奧、薩萊里諾同索拉尼奧上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [安東尼奧、薩萊里諾與索拉尼奧上。]

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: In sooth I know not why I am so sad, It wearies me, you say it wearies you;
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,我唔知道我為何咁樣憂鬱,佢令我厭倦,你哋講佢都令你哋厭倦;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,我不知道我為何這樣憂鬱,它令我厭倦,你們說它也令你們厭倦;

passages.original: But how I caught it, found it, or came by it, What stuff ’tis made of, whereof it is born, I am to learn.
passages.vernacular: 但我係點樣染上、找到、得到佢嘅,佢係乜嘢質料做成嘅,從何而生,我仲得去學習。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我是怎樣染上、找到、得到它的,它是什麼質料做成的,從何而生,我還得去學習。

passages.original: And such a want-wit sadness makes of me, That I have much ado to know myself.
passages.vernacular: 呢種憂鬱把我變得咁樣糊塗,我連認識自己都費勁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這種憂鬱把我變得這樣糊塗,我連認識自己都費勁。

passages.title: Salarino 薩萊里諾
passages.original: Your mind is tossing on the ocean, There where your argosies, with portly sail Like signiors and rich burghers on the flood, Or as it were the pageants of the sea, Do overpeer the petty traffickers That curtsy to them, do them reverence, As they fly by them with their woven wings.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅心喺海洋上顛簸,喺嗰度,你嘅大商船,張住豐滿嘅帆,像海上嘅貴人同富有嘅市民,或像海上嘅遊行盛會,俯視嗰啲向佢哋行禮致敬嘅小商販,當佢哋用織成嘅翅膀飛馳而過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的心在海洋上顛簸,在那裡,你的大商船,張著豐滿的帆,像海上的貴人和富有的市民,或像海上的遊行盛會,俯視那些向它們行禮致敬的小商販,當它們用織成的翅膀飛馳而過。

passages.title: Solanio 索拉尼奧
passages.original: Believe me, sir, had I such venture forth, The better part of my affections would Be with my hopes abroad.
passages.vernacular: 相信我,先生,如果我有咁樣嘅冒險喺外,我大部分嘅心思會同我喺外嘅希望同喺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 相信我,先生,如果我有這樣的冒險在外,我大部分的心思會和我在外的希望同在。

passages.original: I should be still Plucking the grass to know where sits the wind, Peering in maps for ports, and piers and roads;
passages.vernacular: 我會一直拔草睇風向,喺地圖上找港口、碼頭同錨地;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會一直拔草看風向,在地圖上找港口、碼頭和錨地;

passages.original: And every object that might make me fear Misfortune to my ventures, out of doubt Would make me sad.
passages.vernacular: 每一樣可能使我擔心我嘅冒險遭遇不幸嘅嘢,無疑都會讓我憂傷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每一樣可能使我擔心我的冒險遭遇不幸的東西,無疑都會讓我憂傷。

passages.title: Salarino 薩萊里諾
passages.original: My wind cooling my broth Would blow me to an ague when I thought What harm a wind too great might do at sea.
passages.vernacular: 我吹涼肉湯嘅氣息,會讓我想到風太大喺海上可能造成嘅損害,而吹得我發冷發熱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我吹涼肉湯的氣息,會讓我想到風太大在海上可能造成的損害,而吹得我發冷發熱。

passages.original: I should not see the sandy hour-glass run But I should think of shallows and of flats, And see my wealthy Andrew dock’d in sand, Vailing her high top lower than her ribs To kiss her burial.
passages.vernacular: 我睇沙漏嘅沙流動,就會想到淺灘同沙洲,睇到我嗰富有嘅「安德魯號」擱淺喺沙裡,桅頂低垂得比船肋仲低,去親吻佢嘅墳墓。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看沙漏的沙流動,就會想到淺灘和沙洲,看到我那富有的「安德魯號」擱淺在沙裡,桅頂低垂得比船肋還低,去親吻她的墳墓。

passages.original: Should I go to church And see the holy edifice of stone And not bethink me straight of dangerous rocks, Which, touching but my gentle vessel’s side, Would scatter all her spices on the stream, Enrobe the roaring waters with my silks, And, in a word, but even now worth this, And now worth nothing?
passages.vernacular: 我若走進教堂,睇見嗰神聖嘅石頭建築,能不即刻想到危險嘅礁石,佢只要碰一下我嗰溫柔船隻嘅側面,就會把佢所有嘅香料撒喺水流上,用我嘅絲綢畀咆哮嘅水波披上華服,總之,頭先仲值咁多,而家卻一文不值?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我若走進教堂,看見那神聖的石頭建築,能不立刻想到危險的礁石,它只要碰一下我那溫柔船隻的側面,就會把她所有的香料撒在水流上,用我的絲綢給咆哮的水波披上華服,總之,剛才還值這麼多,現在卻一文不值?

passages.original: Shall I have the thought To think on this, and shall I lack the thought That such a thing bechanc’d would make me sad?
passages.vernacular: 我有呢想法去想呢啲,卻缺少咁樣嘅事發生會使我憂傷嘅想法嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有這想法去想這些,卻缺少這樣的事發生會使我憂傷的想法嗎?

passages.original: But tell not me, I know Antonio Is sad to think upon his merchandise.
passages.vernacular: 但別對我講,我知道安東尼奧係因為想到佢嘅貨物而憂傷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但別對我說,我知道安東尼奧是因為想到他的貨物而憂傷。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: Believe me, no.
passages.vernacular: 相信我,唔係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 相信我,不是。

passages.original: I thank my fortune for it, My ventures are not in one bottom trusted, Nor to one place;
passages.vernacular: 我感謝我嘅運氣,我嘅冒險唔係託付喺一條船上,都唔係一個地方;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我感謝我的運氣,我的冒險不是託付在一條船上,也不是一個地方;

passages.original: nor is my whole estate Upon the fortune of this present year.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅全部財產都不繫於今年嘅命運。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的全部財產也不繫於今年的命運。

passages.original: Therefore my merchandise makes me not sad.
passages.vernacular: 所以我嘅貨物不使我憂傷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以我的貨物不使我憂傷。

passages.title: Salarino 薩萊里諾
passages.original: Why then you are in love.
passages.vernacular: 咁你係戀愛喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼你是戀愛了。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: Fie, fie!
passages.vernacular: 呸,呸!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 呸,呸!

passages.title: Salarino 薩萊里諾
passages.original: Not in love neither?
passages.vernacular: 都唔係戀愛?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也不是戀愛?

passages.original: Then let us say you are sad Because you are not merry;
passages.vernacular: 咁讓我哋講你憂傷係因為你不快樂;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼讓我們說你憂傷是因為你不快樂;

passages.original: and ’twere as easy For you to laugh and leap and say you are merry Because you are not sad.
passages.vernacular: 你要笑、要跳、講你快樂,係因為你不憂傷,都一樣容易。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要笑、要跳、說你快樂,是因為你不憂傷,也一樣容易。

passages.original: Now, by two-headed Janus, Nature hath fram’d strange fellows in her time:
passages.vernacular: 而家,憑雙面神雅努斯,自然喺佢嘅時代造出咗奇怪嘅傢伙:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,憑雙面神雅努斯,自然在她的時代造出了奇怪的傢伙:

passages.original: Some that will evermore peep through their eyes, And laugh like parrots at a bagpiper.
passages.vernacular: 有些人總是瞇住眼睛,聽風笛手就像鸚鵡一樣大笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有些人總是瞇著眼睛,聽風笛手就像鸚鵡一樣大笑。

passages.original: And other of such vinegar aspect That they’ll not show their teeth in way of smile Though Nestor swear the jest be laughable.
passages.vernacular: 另啲人臉像醋一樣酸,即使涅斯托發誓呢個笑話好笑,佢哋都唔肯露齒微笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 另一些人臉像醋一樣酸,即使涅斯托發誓這個笑話好笑,他們也不肯露齒微笑。

passages.original: Enter Bassanio, Lorenzo and Gratiano.
passages.vernacular: [巴薩尼奧、羅倫佐同葛拉蒂安諾上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [巴薩尼奧、羅倫佐與葛拉蒂安諾上。]

passages.title: Solanio 索拉尼奧
passages.original: Here comes Bassanio, your most noble kinsman, Gratiano, and Lorenzo.
passages.vernacular: 你最高貴嘅親戚巴薩尼奧嚟喇,仲有葛拉蒂安諾同羅倫佐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你最高貴的親戚巴薩尼奧來了,還有葛拉蒂安諾和羅倫佐。

passages.original: Fare ye well.
passages.vernacular: 再會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再會。

passages.original: We leave you now with better company.
passages.vernacular: 我哋把你留畀更好嘅同伴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們把你留給更好的同伴。

passages.title: Salarino 薩萊里諾
passages.original: I would have stay’d till I had made you merry, If worthier friends had not prevented me.
passages.vernacular: 我本想留到使你快樂為止,如果更值得嘅朋友冇搶先。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我本想留到使你快樂為止,如果更值得的朋友沒有搶先。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: Your worth is very dear in my regard.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅價值喺我心目中好珍貴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的價值在我心目中非常珍貴。

passages.original: I take it your own business calls on you, And you embrace th’ occasion to depart.
passages.vernacular: 我想係你自己嘅事務喺召喚你,你趁機告辭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想是你自己的事務在召喚你,你趁機告辭。

passages.title: Salarino 薩萊里諾
passages.original: Good morrow, my good lords.
passages.vernacular: 早安,我嘅好大人哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早安,我的好大人們。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Good signiors both, when shall we laugh? Say, when?
passages.vernacular: 兩位好先生,我哋何時笑一場?講,何時?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩位好先生,我們何時笑一場?說,何時?

passages.original: You grow exceeding strange.
passages.vernacular: 你哋變得好生疏。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們變得非常生疏。

passages.original: Must it be so?
passages.vernacular: 非要咁樣嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 非要這樣嗎?

passages.title: Salarino 薩萊里諾
passages.original: We’ll make our leisures to attend on yours.
passages.vernacular: 我哋會騰出我哋嘅空閒嚟配合你哋嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們會騰出我們的空閒來配合你們的。

passages.original: [Exeunt Salarino and Solanio.]
passages.vernacular: [薩萊里諾同索拉尼奧下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [薩萊里諾與索拉尼奧下。]

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: My Lord Bassanio, since you have found Antonio, We two will leave you, but at dinner-time I pray you have in mind where we must meet.
passages.vernacular: 巴薩尼奧大人,既然你找到咗安東尼奧,我哋兩人要離開你,但請你記得晚飯時我哋喺邊度見面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴薩尼奧大人,既然你找到了安東尼奧,我們兩人要離開你,但請你記得晚飯時我們在哪裡見面。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: I will not fail you.
passages.vernacular: 我唔會誤你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不會誤你。

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: You look not well, Signior Antonio, You have too much respect upon the world.
passages.vernacular: 你睇起嚟不好,安東尼奧先生,你對世界太在意喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你看起來不好,安東尼奧先生,你對世界太在意了。

passages.original: They lose it that do buy it with much care.
passages.vernacular: 嗰啲用許多憂慮去買世界嘅人,反而失去佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那些用許多憂慮去買世界的人,反而失去它。

passages.original: Believe me, you are marvellously chang’d.
passages.vernacular: 相信我,你變得驚人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 相信我,你變得驚人。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: I hold the world but as the world, Gratiano, A stage, where every man must play a part, And mine a sad one.
passages.vernacular: 我視世界只係世界,葛拉蒂安諾,一座舞台,每人必須扮演一個角色,而我嘅係悲傷嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我視世界只是世界,葛拉蒂安諾,一座舞台,每人必須扮演一個角色,而我的是悲傷的。

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: Let me play the fool, With mirth and laughter let old wrinkles come, And let my liver rather heat with wine Than my heart cool with mortifying groans.
passages.vernacular: 讓我扮傻瓜,讓老皺紋喺歡笑中到來,讓我嘅肝臟寧可被酒加熱,都唔好我嘅心被致命嘅呻吟冷卻。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我扮傻瓜,讓老皺紋在歡笑中到來,讓我的肝臟寧可被酒加熱,也不要我的心被致命的呻吟冷卻。

passages.original: Why should a man whose blood is warm within Sit like his grandsire cut in alabaster?
passages.vernacular: 一個血液溫暖嘅人點解要像佢祖父嘅雪花石膏雕像嗰樣坐住?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個血液溫暖的人為什麼要像他祖父的雪花石膏雕像那樣坐著?

passages.original: Sleep when he wakes?
passages.vernacular: 醒住卻瞓住?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 醒著卻睡著?

passages.original: And creep into the jaundice By being peevish?
passages.vernacular: 因為鬱悶而得黃疸?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為鬱悶而得黃疸?

passages.original: I tell thee what, Antonio, (I love thee, and ’tis my love that speaks):
passages.vernacular: 我告訴你,安東尼奧,(我愛你,係我嘅愛喺講話):
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我告訴你,安東尼奧,(我愛你,是我的愛在說話):

passages.original: There are a sort of men whose visages Do cream and mantle like a standing pond, And do a wilful stillness entertain, With purpose to be dress’d in an opinion Of wisdom, gravity, profound conceit, As who should say, “I am Sir Oracle, And when I ope my lips, let no dog bark.”
passages.vernacular: 有一類人,佢哋嘅臉像死水池一樣結住皮,故意保持安靜,為了裝扮成智慧、莊重、深刻思想嘅名聲,好像喺講:「我係神諭先生,我一開口,不許狗吠。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有一類人,他們的臉像死水池一樣結著皮,故意保持安靜,為了裝扮成智慧、莊重、深刻思想的名聲,好像在說:「我是神諭先生,我一開口,不許狗吠。」

passages.original: O my Antonio, I do know of these That therefore only are reputed wise For saying nothing;
passages.vernacular: 啊我嘅安東尼奧,我知道呢類人,僅僅因為不講話而被認為聰明;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊我的安東尼奧,我知道這類人,僅僅因為不說話而被認為聰明;

passages.original: when, I am very sure, If they should speak, would almost damn those ears Which, hearing them, would call their brothers fools.
passages.vernacular: 而我好確定,如果佢哋講話,幾乎要使聽到佢哋卻稱佢哋嘅兄弟為傻瓜嘅嗰啲耳朵遭受詛咒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而我非常確定,如果他們說話,幾乎要使聽到他們卻稱他們的兄弟為傻瓜的那些耳朵遭受詛咒。

passages.original: I’ll tell thee more of this another time.
passages.vernacular: 呢件事我改天再告訴你更多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這件事我改天再告訴你更多。

passages.original: But fish not with this melancholy bait For this fool gudgeon, this opinion.
passages.vernacular: 但別用呢憂鬱嘅餌,去釣呢個傻小魚,呢種名聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但別用這憂鬱的餌,去釣這個傻小魚,這種名聲。

passages.original: Come, good Lorenzo.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,好羅倫佐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,好羅倫佐。

passages.original: Fare ye well a while.
passages.vernacular: 暫時再會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 暫時再會。

passages.original: I’ll end my exhortation after dinner.
passages.vernacular: 我會喺飯後結束我嘅勸誡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會在飯後結束我的勸誡。

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: Well, we will leave you then till dinner-time.
passages.vernacular: 好,嗰我哋留你到晚飯時間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,那我們留你到晚飯時間。

passages.original: I must be one of these same dumb wise men, For Gratiano never lets me speak.
passages.vernacular: 我得做呢啲啞巴智者之一,因為葛拉蒂安諾從不讓我講話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我得做這些啞巴智者之一,因為葛拉蒂安諾從不讓我說話。

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: Well, keep me company but two years moe, Thou shalt not know the sound of thine own tongue.
passages.vernacular: 好,再同我作伴兩年,你就不認得自己舌頭嘅聲音喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,再和我作伴兩年,你就不認得自己舌頭的聲音了。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: Fare you well.
passages.vernacular: 再會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再會。

passages.original: I’ll grow a talker for this gear.
passages.vernacular: 為了呢個,我要變成多話嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了這個,我要變成多話的人。

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: Thanks, i’ faith, for silence is only commendable In a neat’s tongue dried, and a maid not vendible.
passages.vernacular: 謝謝,講真嘅,因為沉默只值得稱讚於風乾嘅牛舌,同賣不出去嘅少女。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 謝謝,說真的,因為沉默只值得稱讚於風乾的牛舌,和賣不出去的少女。

passages.original: [Exeunt Gratiano and Lorenzo.]
passages.vernacular: [葛拉蒂安諾同羅倫佐下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [葛拉蒂安諾與羅倫佐下。]

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: Is that anything now?
passages.vernacular: 呢算乜嘢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這算什麼嗎?

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Gratiano speaks an infinite deal of nothing, more than any man in all Venice.
passages.vernacular: 葛拉蒂安諾講了無窮多嘅廢話,比威尼斯任何人都多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 葛拉蒂安諾說了無窮多的廢話,比威尼斯任何人都多。

passages.original: His reasons are as two grains of wheat hid in two bushels of chaff:
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅道理像兩粒麥子藏喺兩斗穀殼裡:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的道理像兩粒麥子藏在兩斗穀殼裡:

passages.original: you shall seek all day ere you find them, and when you have them they are not worth the search.
passages.vernacular: 你找一整天才找到,找到咗都不值得找。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你找一整天才找到,找到了也不值得找。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: Well, tell me now what lady is the same To whom you swore a secret pilgrimage, That you today promis’d to tell me of?
passages.vernacular: 好,而家告訴我,你發誓秘密朝聖嘅嗰位小姐係邊個,你今日答應要告訴我嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,現在告訴我,你發誓秘密朝聖的那位小姐是誰,你今天答應要告訴我的?

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: ’Tis not unknown to you, Antonio, How much I have disabled mine estate By something showing a more swelling port Than my faint means would grant continuance.
passages.vernacular: 你並唔係唔知道,安東尼奧,我為了炫耀啲比我微薄財力所能維持嘅更大嘅排場,把我嘅產業耗損咗多少。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你並不是不知道,安東尼奧,我為了炫耀一點比我微薄財力所能維持的更大的排場,把我的產業耗損了多少。

passages.original: Nor do I now make moan to be abridg’d From such a noble rate, but my chief care Is to come fairly off from the great debts Wherein my time, something too prodigal, Hath left me gag’d.
passages.vernacular: 我而家都並不為被削減咁樣高貴嘅排場而哀嘆,我主要嘅憂慮係如何體面地擺脫嗰啲巨債,我略嫌揮霍嘅歲月使我欠下嘅債。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我現在也並不為被削減這樣高貴的排場而哀嘆,我主要的憂慮是如何體面地擺脫那些巨債,我略嫌揮霍的歲月使我欠下的債。

passages.original: To you, Antonio, I owe the most in money and in love, And from your love I have a warranty To unburden all my plots and purposes How to get clear of all the debts I owe.
passages.vernacular: 對你,安東尼奧,我欠得最多,無論喺金錢定係情誼上,憑你嘅愛,我有保證向你傾吐我所有嘅計劃同意圖,關於點樣仲清我欠下嘅所有債務。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對你,安東尼奧,我欠得最多,無論在金錢還是情誼上,憑你的愛,我有保證向你傾吐我所有的計劃和意圖,關於怎樣還清我欠下的所有債務。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: I pray you, good Bassanio, let me know it; And if it stand, as you yourself still do, Within the eye of honour, be assur’d My purse, my person, my extremest means Lie all unlock’d to your occasions.
passages.vernacular: 請你,好巴薩尼奧,讓我知道;如果佢像你自己一向所做嘅,喺榮譽嘅眼光之內,就請放心,我嘅錢包、我嘅人、我極端嘅手段,都對你嘅需要毫無保留。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你,好巴薩尼奧,讓我知道;如果它像你自己一向所做的,在榮譽的眼光之內,就請放心,我的錢包、我的人、我極端的手段,都對你的需要毫無保留。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: In my school-days, when I had lost one shaft, I shot his fellow of the self-same flight The self-same way, with more advised watch To find the other forth;
passages.vernacular: 我上學嘅時候,丟咗一支箭,我就朝同一個方向射出同樣飛行嘅另一支,更仔細地觀察,把另一支找出嚟;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我上學的時候,丟了一支箭,我就朝同一個方向射出同樣飛行的另一支,更仔細地觀察,把另一支找出來;

passages.original: and by adventuring both I oft found both.
passages.vernacular: 兩支一起冒險,我常常兩支都找回。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩支一起冒險,我常常兩支都找回。

passages.original: I urge this childhood proof Because what follows is pure innocence.
passages.vernacular: 我提出呢童年嘅證明,因為接下嚟嘅完全係天真。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我提出這童年的證明,因為接下來的完全是天真。

passages.original: I owe you much, and, like a wilful youth, That which I owe is lost.
passages.vernacular: 我欠你好多,像任性嘅少年,我欠嘅已丟失。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我欠你很多,像任性的少年,我欠的已丟失。

passages.original: But if you please To shoot another arrow that self way Which you did shoot the first, I do not doubt, As I will watch the aim, or to find both, Or bring your latter hazard back again, And thankfully rest debtor for the first.
passages.vernacular: 但如果你願意朝同一個方向再射一支箭,就像你射第一支嗰樣,我不懷疑,由於我會留心瞄準,要麼兩支都找到,要麼把你後來嘅冒險帶回嚟,而感激地做第一筆嘅債務人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但如果你願意朝同一個方向再射一支箭,就像你射第一支那樣,我不懷疑,由於我會留心瞄準,要麼兩支都找到,要麼把你後來的冒險帶回來,而感激地做第一筆的債務人。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: You know me well, and herein spend but time To wind about my love with circumstance;
passages.vernacular: 你好了解我,喺此只係浪費時間用迂迴嚟繞我嘅愛;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你很了解我,在此只是浪費時間用迂迴來繞我的愛;

passages.original: And out of doubt you do me now more wrong In making question of my uttermost Than if you had made waste of all I have.
passages.vernacular: 無疑你而家質疑我最大嘅能力,比你把我所有嘅都浪費掉更冤枉我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無疑你現在質疑我最大的能力,比你把我所有的都浪費掉更冤枉我。

passages.original: Then do but say to me what I should do That in your knowledge may by me be done, And I am prest unto it.
passages.vernacular: 咁只要告訴我我該做乜嘢,只要喺你所知範圍內我能做到,我就準備好喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼只要告訴我我該做什麼,只要在你所知範圍內我能做到,我就準備好了。

passages.original: Therefore, speak.
passages.vernacular: 所以,講吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以,說吧。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: In Belmont is a lady richly left, And she is fair, and, fairer than that word, Of wondrous virtues.
passages.vernacular: 喺貝爾蒙特有一位繼承咗豐厚遺產嘅小姐,佢美麗,而且比呢個詞更美,具有驚人嘅美德。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在貝爾蒙特有一位繼承了豐厚遺產的小姐,她美麗,而且比這個詞更美,具有驚人的美德。

passages.original: Sometimes from her eyes I did receive fair speechless messages:
passages.vernacular: 有時從佢眼中我收到美麗無言嘅訊息:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有時從她眼中我收到美麗無言的訊息:

passages.original: Her name is Portia, nothing undervalu’d To Cato’s daughter, Brutus’ Portia.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅名字係鮑西婭,絲毫不遜於加圖嘅女兒,布魯圖嘅鮑西婭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的名字是鮑西婭,絲毫不遜於加圖的女兒,布魯圖的鮑西婭。

passages.original: Nor is the wide world ignorant of her worth, For the four winds blow in from every coast Renowned suitors, and her sunny locks Hang on her temples like a golden fleece, Which makes her seat of Belmont Colchos’ strond, And many Jasons come in quest of her.
passages.vernacular: 廣闊嘅世界都唔係唔知道佢嘅價值,因為四面嘅風從每個海岸吹嚟有名嘅求婚者,佢陽光般嘅金髮垂喺太陽穴上,像一張金羊毛,使佢嘅貝爾蒙特居所成為科爾基斯嘅海岸,許多伊阿宋為尋求佢而嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 廣闊的世界也不是不知道她的價值,因為四面的風從每個海岸吹來有名的求婚者,她陽光般的金髮垂在太陽穴上,像一張金羊毛,使她的貝爾蒙特居所成為科爾基斯的海岸,許多伊阿宋為尋求她而來。

passages.original: O my Antonio, had I but the means To hold a rival place with one of them, I have a mind presages me such thrift That I should questionless be fortunate.
passages.vernacular: 啊我嘅安東尼奧,如果我有辦法同其中一個保持對手嘅地位,我心中有一種預感告訴我咁樣嘅興旺,我無疑會幸運。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊我的安東尼奧,如果我有辦法與其中一個保持對手的地位,我心中有一種預感告訴我這樣的興旺,我無疑會幸運。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: Thou know’st that all my fortunes are at sea;
passages.vernacular: 你知道我所有嘅財富都喺海上;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道我所有的財富都在海上;

passages.original: Neither have I money nor commodity To raise a present sum, therefore go forth Try what my credit can in Venice do;
passages.vernacular: 我既冇錢都冇貨物可以籌集眼前嘅款額,所以去吧,試試我喺威尼斯嘅信用能做乜嘢;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我既沒有錢也沒有貨物可以籌集眼前的款額,所以去吧,試試我在威尼斯的信用能做什麼;

passages.original: That shall be rack’d even to the uttermost, To furnish thee to Belmont to fair Portia.
passages.vernacular: 佢會被榨到極限,去畀你備足前往貝爾蒙特見美麗鮑西婭嘅費用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它會被榨到極限,去給你備足前往貝爾蒙特見美麗鮑西婭的費用。

passages.original: Go presently inquire, and so will I, Where money is, and I no question make To have it of my trust or for my sake.
passages.vernacular: 即刻去打聽,我都去,邊度有錢,我毫不懷疑能憑我嘅信用或睇喺我嘅面上得到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 立刻去打聽,我也去,哪裡有錢,我毫不懷疑能憑我的信用或看在我的面上得到。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act I, Scene II — Belmont. A Room in Portia’s House 第一幕第二場:貝爾蒙特,鮑西婭家一室

passages.original: Enter Portia with her waiting-woman Nerissa.
passages.vernacular: [鮑西婭偕侍女尼莉莎上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [鮑西婭偕侍女尼莉莎上。]

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: By my troth, Nerissa, my little body is aweary of this great world.
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,尼莉莎,我呢小小嘅身體對呢偌大嘅世界感到厭倦喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,尼莉莎,我這小小的身體對這偌大的世界感到厭倦了。

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: You would be, sweet madam, if your miseries were in the same abundance as your good fortunes are.
passages.vernacular: 你會嘅,親愛嘅小姐,如果你嘅不幸同你嘅幸運一樣豐盛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你會的,親愛的小姐,如果你的不幸與你的幸運一樣豐盛。

passages.original: And yet, for aught I see, they are as sick that surfeit with too much as they that starve with nothing.
passages.vernacular: 然而依我睇,食撐咗嘅人同一無所有挨餓嘅人一樣係病人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而依我看,吃撐了的人和一無所有挨餓的人一樣是病人。

passages.original: It is no mean happiness, therefore, to be seated in the mean.
passages.vernacular: 所以,坐喺中庸之位係不小嘅幸福。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以,坐在中庸之位是不小的幸福。

passages.original: Superfluity come sooner by white hairs, but competency lives longer.
passages.vernacular: 過度更快迎嚟白髮,而適度活得長久。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 過度更快迎來白髮,而適度活得長久。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Good sentences, and well pronounc’d.
passages.vernacular: 好格言,講得好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好格言,說得好。

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: They would be better if well followed.
passages.vernacular: 如果好好遵行會更好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果好好遵行會更好。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: If to do were as easy as to know what were good to do, chapels had been churches, and poor men’s cottages princes’ palaces.
passages.vernacular: 如果做到同知道該做乜嘢一樣容易,小教堂早已成咗大教堂,窮人嘅茅舍早已成咗王子嘅宮殿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果做到和知道該做什麼一樣容易,小教堂早已成了大教堂,窮人的茅舍早已成了王子的宮殿。

passages.original: It is a good divine that follows his own instructions;
passages.vernacular: 能遵循自己教導嘅才係好傳道人;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 能遵循自己教導的才是好傳道人;

passages.original: I can easier teach twenty what were good to be done than to be one of the twenty to follow mine own teaching.
passages.vernacular: 我教二十個人乜嘢係該做嘅,比做嗰二十個人之一去遵循自己嘅教導容易。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我教二十個人什麼是該做的,比做那二十個人之一去遵循自己的教導容易。

passages.original: The brain may devise laws for the blood, but a hot temper leaps o’er a cold decree;
passages.vernacular: 頭腦可以為血氣立法,但熱情嘅脾氣會跳過冰冷嘅法令;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 頭腦可以為血氣立法,但熱情的脾氣會跳過冰冷的法令;

passages.original: such a hare is madness the youth, to skip o’er the meshes of good counsel the cripple.
passages.vernacular: 青春呢隻瘋兔,就係咁樣跳過好建議呢跛子所設嘅網。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 青春這隻瘋兔,就是這樣跳過好建議這跛子所設的網。

passages.original: But this reasoning is not in the fashion to choose me a husband.
passages.vernacular: 但呢番道理對替我挑選丈夫冇用處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但這番道理對替我挑選丈夫沒有用處。

passages.original: O me, the word “choose”!
passages.vernacular: 哎,「挑選」呢個詞!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎,「挑選」這個詞!

passages.original: I may neither choose who I would nor refuse who I dislike, so is the will of a living daughter curb’d by the will of a dead father.
passages.vernacular: 我既唔能夠選我想要嘅,都唔能夠拒絕我不鍾意嘅,活住嘅女兒嘅意志就係咁樣被死去嘅父親嘅意志所束縛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我既不能選我想要的,也不能拒絕我不喜歡的,活著的女兒的意志就是這樣被死去的父親的意志所束縛。

passages.original: Is it not hard, Nerissa, that I cannot choose one, nor refuse none?
passages.vernacular: 尼莉莎,我既唔能夠選一個,又唔能夠拒絕任何一個,呢唔係好難嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 尼莉莎,我既不能選一個,又不能拒絕任何一個,這不是很難嗎?

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: Your father was ever virtuous, and holy men at their death have good inspirations.
passages.vernacular: 你父親一向有德,聖人喺臨死時有好嘅靈感。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你父親一向有德,聖人在臨死時有好的靈感。

passages.original: Therefore the lott’ry that he hath devised in these three chests of gold, silver, and lead, whereof who chooses his meaning chooses you, will no doubt never be chosen by any rightly but one who you shall rightly love.
passages.vernacular: 所以佢喺金、銀、鉛呢三個匣子裡設計嘅抽籤,邊個選對佢嘅用意就選到你,無疑只有你真正所愛嘅人才會正確地選中。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以他在金、銀、鉛這三個匣子裡設計的抽籤,誰選對他的用意就選到你,無疑只有你真正所愛的人才會正確地選中。

passages.original: But what warmth is there in your affection towards any of these princely suitors that are already come?
passages.vernacular: 但你對已經嚟嘅呢啲王侯求婚者中嘅任何一個,有乜嘢暖意呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但你對已經來的這些王侯求婚者中的任何一個,有什麼暖意呢?

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: I pray thee over-name them, and as thou namest them, I will describe them, and according to my description level at my affection.
passages.vernacular: 我請你逐個講出佢哋嘅名字,你講一個,我就描述一個,按我嘅描述,你就能瞄準我嘅感情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我請你逐個說出他們的名字,你說一個,我就描述一個,按我的描述,你就能瞄準我的感情。

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: First, there is the Neapolitan prince.
passages.vernacular: 首先,有嗰位嗰不勒斯親王。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 首先,有那位那不勒斯親王。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Ay, that’s a colt indeed, for he doth nothing but talk of his horse, and he makes it a great appropriation to his own good parts that he can shoe him himself.
passages.vernacular: 對,嗰真係匹小馬駒,因為佢只談佢嘅馬,並把能親自畀馬釘蹄鐵視為自己好大嘅長處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,那真是匹小馬駒,因為他只談他的馬,並把能親自給馬釘蹄鐵視為自己很大的長處。

passages.original: I am much afeard my lady his mother play’d false with a smith.
passages.vernacular: 我好怕佢母親夫人跟鐵匠偷過情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很怕他母親夫人跟鐵匠偷過情。

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: Then is there the County Palatine.
passages.vernacular: 然後有巴拉丁伯爵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後有巴拉丁伯爵。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: He doth nothing but frown, as who should say “And you will not have me, choose.”
passages.vernacular: 佢只會皺眉,好像喺講「你若唔好我,就另選」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他只會皺眉,好像在說「你若不要我,就另選」。

passages.original: He hears merry tales and smiles not.
passages.vernacular: 佢聽有趣嘅故事都不笑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他聽有趣的故事也不笑。

passages.original: I fear he will prove the weeping philosopher when he grows old, being so full of unmannerly sadness in his youth.
passages.vernacular: 我怕佢年老時會變成哭泣嘅哲學家,既然年輕時就咁樣滿係無禮嘅憂鬱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我怕他年老時會變成哭泣的哲學家,既然年輕時就這樣滿是無禮的憂鬱。

passages.original: I had rather be married to a death’s-head with a bone in his mouth than to either of these.
passages.vernacular: 我寧可嫁畀口裡含住骨頭嘅骷髏,都不嫁畀呢兩個之一。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我寧可嫁給口裡含著骨頭的骷髏,也不嫁給這兩個之一。

passages.original: God defend me from these two!
passages.vernacular: 上帝保護我免於呢兩個!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上帝保護我免於這兩個!

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: How say you by the French lord, Monsieur Le Bon?
passages.vernacular: 你對法國貴族勒·邦先生點講?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你對法國貴族勒·邦先生怎麼說?

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: God made him, and therefore let him pass for a man.
passages.vernacular: 上帝造咗佢,所以就讓佢算係個人吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 上帝造了他,所以就讓他算是個人吧。

passages.original: In truth, I know it is a sin to be a mocker, but he!
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,我知道嘲笑人係罪,不過佢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,我知道嘲笑人是罪,可是他!

passages.original: why, he hath a horse better than the Neapolitan’s, a better bad habit of frowning than the Count Palatine.
passages.vernacular: 哎,佢嘅馬比嗰不勒斯人嘅好,皺眉嘅壞習慣都比巴拉丁伯爵嘅好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎,他的馬比那不勒斯人的好,皺眉的壞習慣也比巴拉丁伯爵的好。

passages.original: He is every man in no man.
passages.vernacular: 佢乜嘢人都係,又乜嘢人都唔係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他什麼人都是,又什麼人都不是。

passages.original: If a throstle sing, he falls straight a-cap’ring.
passages.vernacular: 鶇鳥一唱,佢即刻就蹦跳起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鶇鳥一唱,他立刻就蹦跳起來。

passages.original: He will fence with his own shadow.
passages.vernacular: 佢會跟自己嘅影子擊劍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他會跟自己的影子擊劍。

passages.original: If I should marry him, I should marry twenty husbands.
passages.vernacular: 如果我嫁畀佢,等於嫁畀二十個丈夫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我嫁給他,等於嫁給二十個丈夫。

passages.original: If he would despise me, I would forgive him, for if he love me to madness, I shall never requite him.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢鄙視我,我會原諒佢,因為如果佢瘋狂地愛我,我永遠無法回報佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他鄙視我,我會原諒他,因為如果他瘋狂地愛我,我永遠無法回報他。

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: What say you then to Falconbridge, the young baron of England?
passages.vernacular: 嗰你對英國嘅年輕男爵福肯橋點講?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那你對英國的年輕男爵福肯橋怎麼說?

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: You know I say nothing to him, for he understands not me, nor I him:
passages.vernacular: 你知道我對佢冇乜嘢可講,因為佢不懂我,我都不懂佢:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道我對他沒什麼可說,因為他不懂我,我也不懂他:

passages.original: he hath neither Latin, French, nor Italian, and you will come into the court and swear that I have a poor pennyworth in the English.
passages.vernacular: 佢不懂拉丁語、法語或意大利語,而你會去法庭發誓講我嘅英語好糟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不懂拉丁語、法語或意大利語,而你會去法庭發誓說我的英語很糟。

passages.original: He is a proper man’s picture; but alas, who can converse with a dumb-show?
passages.vernacular: 佢係個體面男人嘅畫像;但唉,邊個能同啞劇交談?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他是個體面男人的畫像;但唉,誰能和啞劇交談?

passages.original: How oddly he is suited!
passages.vernacular: 佢穿得多古怪!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他穿得多古怪!

passages.original: I think he bought his doublet in Italy, his round hose in France, his bonnet in Germany, and his behaviour everywhere.
passages.vernacular: 我想佢嘅短上衣係在意大利買嘅,圓褲喺法國買嘅,帽子喺德國買嘅,而佢嘅舉止係各處都買嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想他的短上衣是在意大利買的,圓褲在法國買的,帽子在德國買的,而他的舉止是各處都買的。

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: What think you of the Scottish lord, his neighbour?
passages.vernacular: 你認為佢嘅鄰居蘇格蘭貴族點樣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你認為他的鄰居蘇格蘭貴族怎樣?

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: That he hath a neighbourly charity in him, for he borrowed a box of the ear of the Englishman, and swore he would pay him again when he was able.
passages.vernacular: 佢有睦鄰嘅慈善,因為佢向英國人借咗一記耳光,並發誓等佢有能力時仲佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他有睦鄰的慈善,因為他向英國人借了一記耳光,並發誓等他有能力時還他。

passages.original: I think the Frenchman became his surety, and seal’d under for another.
passages.vernacular: 我想法國人替佢作咗擔保,又為另一記蓋章簽約。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想法國人替他作了擔保,又為另一記蓋章簽約。

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: How like you the young German, the Duke of Saxony’s nephew?
passages.vernacular: 你覺得年輕嘅德國人點樣,薩克森公爵嘅侄子?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你覺得年輕的德國人怎樣,薩克森公爵的侄子?

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Very vilely in the morning when he is sober, and most vilely in the afternoon when he is drunk:
passages.vernacular: 早晨清醒時好卑劣,下午醉酒時最卑劣:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 早晨清醒時非常卑劣,下午醉酒時最卑劣:

passages.original: when he is best, he is a little worse than a man, and when he is worst, he is little better than a beast.
passages.vernacular: 佢最好嘅時候,比人差啲;佢最壞嘅時候,比野獸好不咗多少。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他最好的時候,比人差一點;他最壞的時候,比野獸好不了多少。

passages.original: And the worst fall that ever fell, I hope I shall make shift to go without him.
passages.vernacular: 即使遭遇最壞嘅事,我希望我設法能冇佢都過得去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 即使遭遇最壞的事,我希望我設法能沒有他也過得去。

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: If he should offer to choose, and choose the right casket, you should refuse to perform your father’s will, if you should refuse to accept him.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢嚟選,而且選對咗匣子,你若拒絕接受佢,就係拒絕執行你父親嘅遺願。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他來選,而且選對了匣子,你若拒絕接受他,就是拒絕執行你父親的遺願。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Therefore, for fear of the worst, I pray thee set a deep glass of Rhenish wine on the contrary casket, for if the devil be within and that temptation without, I know he will choose it.
passages.vernacular: 所以,為防最壞嘅情況,請你喺錯誤嘅嗰個匣子上放一大杯萊茵葡萄酒,因為如果魔鬼喺裡面,而嗰個誘惑喺外面,我知道佢會選佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以,為防最壞的情況,請你在錯誤的那個匣子上放一大杯萊茵葡萄酒,因為如果魔鬼在裡面,而那個誘惑在外面,我知道他會選它。

passages.original: I will do anything, Nerissa, ere I will be married to a sponge.
passages.vernacular: 喺嫁畀海綿之前,尼莉莎,我乜嘢都肯做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在嫁給海綿之前,尼莉莎,我什麼都肯做。

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: You need not fear, lady, the having any of these lords.
passages.vernacular: 小姐,你唔使怕嫁畀呢啲貴人中嘅任何一位。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小姐,你不必怕嫁給這些貴人中的任何一位。

passages.original: They have acquainted me with their determinations, which is indeed to return to their home, and to trouble you with no more suit, unless you may be won by some other sort than your father’s imposition, depending on the caskets.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋已把佢哋嘅決定告訴咗我,就係回到佢哋家鄉,唔再用求婚打擾你,除非你能以你父親靠匣子規定之外嘅某種方式被贏得。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們已把他們的決定告訴了我,就是回到他們家鄉,不再用求婚打擾你,除非你能以你父親靠匣子規定之外的某種方式被贏得。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: If I live to be as old as Sibylla, I will die as chaste as Diana, unless I be obtained by the manner of my father’s will.
passages.vernacular: 如果我活到像西比拉一樣老,我都要像狄安娜一樣貞潔地死去,除非我係按我父親遺囑嘅方式得到嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我活到像西比拉一樣老,我也要像狄安娜一樣貞潔地死去,除非我是按我父親遺囑的方式得到的。

passages.original: I am glad this parcel of wooers are so reasonable, for there is not one among them but I dote on his very absence.
passages.vernacular: 我好高興呢一群求婚者咁樣通情達理,因為佢哋中冇一個我唔係對佢嘅缺席著迷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很高興這一群求婚者這樣通情達理,因為他們中沒有一個我不是對他的缺席著迷。

passages.original: And I pray God grant them a fair departure.
passages.vernacular: 願上帝讓佢哋順利離去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願上帝讓他們順利離去。

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: Do you not remember, lady, in your father’s time, a Venetian, a scholar and a soldier, that came hither in company of the Marquis of Montferrat?
passages.vernacular: 小姐,您仲記得您父親在世時,一位威尼斯人,既係學者又係軍人,同蒙費拉侯爵同嚟呢度嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小姐,您還記得您父親在世時,一位威尼斯人,既是學者又是軍人,與蒙費拉侯爵同來這裡嗎?

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Yes, yes, it was Bassanio, as I think, so was he call’d.
passages.vernacular: 記得,記得,係巴薩尼奧,我想佢係呢個名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 記得,記得,是巴薩尼奧,我想他是這個名字。

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: True, madam.
passages.vernacular: 對,小姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,小姐。

passages.original: He, of all the men that ever my foolish eyes look’d upon, was the best deserving a fair lady.
passages.vernacular: 喺我呢愚蠢嘅眼睛睇過嘅所有男人中,佢最配得上一位美麗嘅小姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在我這愚蠢的眼睛看過的所有男人中,他最配得上一位美麗的小姐。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: I remember him well, and I remember him worthy of thy praise.
passages.vernacular: 我記得佢,我記得佢值得你稱讚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我記得他,我記得他值得你稱讚。

passages.original: Enter a Servingman.
passages.vernacular: [一名僕人上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [一名僕人上。]

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: How now! what news?
passages.vernacular: 點樣!有乜嘢消息?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼樣!有什麼消息?

passages.title: Servingman 僕人
passages.original: The four strangers seek for you, madam, to take their leave.
passages.vernacular: 嗰四位外邦人找您,小姐,要嚟告辭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那四位外邦人找您,小姐,要來告辭。

passages.original: And there is a forerunner come from a fifth, the Prince of Morocco, who brings word the Prince his master will be here tonight.
passages.vernacular: 仲有一位先遣人員從第五位,摩洛哥親王嗰度嚟,帶信講親王佢主人今晚到呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有一位先遣人員從第五位,摩洛哥親王那裡來,帶信說親王他主人今晚到這裡。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: If I could bid the fifth welcome with so good heart as I can bid the other four farewell, I should be glad of his approach.
passages.vernacular: 如果我能以歡迎第五位嘅好心情,像向另外四位告別一樣,我會好高興佢嘅到來。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我能以歡迎第五位的好心情,像向另外四位告別一樣,我會很高興他的到來。

passages.original: If he have the condition of a saint and the complexion of a devil, I had rather he should shrive me than wive me.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢有聖人嘅性情同魔鬼嘅膚色,我寧願佢替我懺悔,而唔係娶我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他有聖人的性情和魔鬼的膚色,我寧願他替我懺悔,而不是娶我。

passages.original: Come, Nerissa.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,尼莉莎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,尼莉莎。

passages.original: Sirrah, go before.
passages.vernacular: 小子,你先去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小子,你先去。

passages.original: Whiles we shut the gate upon one wooer, another knocks at the door.
passages.vernacular: 我哋剛把門對一個求婚者關上,另一個又喺敲門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們剛把門對一個求婚者關上,另一個又在敲門。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act I, Scene III — Venice. A Public Place 第一幕第三場:威尼斯公共場所

passages.original: Enter Bassanio with Shylock the Jew.
passages.vernacular: [巴薩尼奧偕猶太人夏洛克上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [巴薩尼奧偕猶太人夏洛克上。]

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: Three thousand ducats, well.
passages.vernacular: 三千杜卡特,好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三千杜卡特,好。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Ay, sir, for three months.
passages.vernacular: 對,先生,三個月。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,先生,三個月。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: For three months, well.
passages.vernacular: 三個月,好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三個月,好。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: For the which, as I told you, Antonio shall be bound.
passages.vernacular: 為此,如我告訴你嘅,安東尼奧將作擔保。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為此,如我告訴你的,安東尼奧將作擔保。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: Antonio shall become bound, well.
passages.vernacular: 安東尼奧將作擔保,好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安東尼奧將作擔保,好。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: May you stead me?
passages.vernacular: 你能幫我嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你能幫我嗎?

passages.original: Will you pleasure me?
passages.vernacular: 你願意成全我嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你願意成全我嗎?

passages.original: Shall I know your answer?
passages.vernacular: 我能知道你嘅答覆嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我能知道你的答覆嗎?

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: Three thousand ducats for three months, and Antonio bound.
passages.vernacular: 三千杜卡特,三個月,安東尼奧擔保。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三千杜卡特,三個月,安東尼奧擔保。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Your answer to that.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅答覆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的答覆。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: Antonio is a good man.
passages.vernacular: 安東尼奧係個好人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安東尼奧是個好人。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Have you heard any imputation to the contrary?
passages.vernacular: 你聽到過任何相反嘅指責嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你聽到過任何相反的指責嗎?

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: Ho, no, no, no, no: my meaning in saying he is a good man is to have you understand me that he is sufficient.
passages.vernacular: 喔,不,不,不,不:我講佢係好人,意思係要你明白佢有償付能力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喔,不,不,不,不:我說他是好人,意思是要你明白他有償付能力。

passages.original: Yet his means are in supposition: he hath an argosy bound to Tripolis, another to the Indies.
passages.vernacular: 然而佢嘅財產只係假定嘅:佢有一艘大商船開往嘅黎波里,另一艘去印度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而他的財產只是假定的:他有一艘大商船開往的黎波里,另一艘去印度。

passages.original: I understand, moreover, upon the Rialto, he hath a third at Mexico, a fourth for England, and other ventures he hath squandered abroad.
passages.vernacular: 我仲聽講,喺雷雅托,佢有第三艘喺墨西哥,第四艘去英國,仲有其他散喺外面嘅冒險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我還聽說,在雷雅托,他有第三艘在墨西哥,第四艘去英國,還有其他散在外面的冒險。

passages.original: But ships are but boards, sailors but men; there be land-rats and water-rats, water-thieves and land-thieves—I mean pirates—and then there is the peril of waters, winds, and rocks.
passages.vernacular: 但船只係木板,水手只係人;有陸上嘅老鼠同水中嘅老鼠,水賊同陸賊——我係講海盜——仲有水、風、礁石嘅危險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但船只是木板,水手只是人;有陸上的老鼠和水中的老鼠,水賊和陸賊——我是說海盜——還有水、風、礁石的危險。

passages.original: The man is, notwithstanding, sufficient.
passages.vernacular: 儘管如此,呢個人仍係有償付能力嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 儘管如此,這個人仍是有償付能力的。

passages.original: Three thousand ducats.
passages.vernacular: 三千杜卡特。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三千杜卡特。

passages.original: I think I may take his bond.
passages.vernacular: 我想我可以接受佢嘅契約。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想我可以接受他的契約。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Be assured you may.
passages.vernacular: 請放心你可以。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請放心你可以。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: I will be assured I may.
passages.vernacular: 我要確定我可以。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要確定我可以。

passages.original: And that I may be assured, I will bethink me.
passages.vernacular: 為了確定,我要想一想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了確定,我要想一想。

passages.original: May I speak with Antonio?
passages.vernacular: 我可以同安東尼奧談談嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我可以和安東尼奧談談嗎?

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: If it please you to dine with us.
passages.vernacular: 如果你肯賞光同我哋共進晚餐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你肯賞光與我們共進晚餐。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: Yes, to smell pork, to eat of the habitation which your prophet, the Nazarite, conjured the devil into.
passages.vernacular: 係啊,去聞豬肉嘅氣味,去食你哋嘅先知攞撒勒人把魔鬼趕進去嘅嗰種住處嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是啊,去聞豬肉的氣味,去吃你們的先知拿撒勒人把魔鬼趕進去的那種住處的東西。

passages.original: I will buy with you, sell with you, talk with you, walk with you, and so following;
passages.vernacular: 我可以同你哋買賣,同你哋談話,同你哋散步,等等;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我可以和你們買賣,和你們談話,和你們散步,等等;

passages.original: but I will not eat with you, drink with you, nor pray with you.
passages.vernacular: 但我不同你哋一起食,一起飲,一起禱告。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我不和你們一起吃,一起喝,一起禱告。

passages.original: What news on the Rialto?
passages.vernacular: 雷雅托有乜嘢消息?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雷雅托有什麼消息?

passages.original: Who is he comes here?
passages.vernacular: 嚟嘅係邊個?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來的是誰?

passages.original: Enter Antonio.
passages.vernacular: [安東尼奧上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [安東尼奧上。]

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: This is Signior Antonio.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係安東尼奧先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是安東尼奧先生。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: [Aside.]
passages.vernacular: [旁白。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [旁白。]

passages.original: How like a fawning publican he looks!
passages.vernacular: 佢睇起嚟多像一個諂媚嘅稅吏!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他看起來多像一個諂媚的稅吏!

passages.original: I hate him for he is a Christian, But more for that in low simplicity He lends out money gratis, and brings down The rate of usance here with us in Venice.
passages.vernacular: 我恨佢,因為佢係基督徒,但更因為佢以卑賤嘅單純借出錢不收利息,壓低咗我哋威尼斯呢度嘅利率。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我恨他,因為他是基督徒,但更因為他以卑賤的單純借出錢不收利息,壓低了我們威尼斯這裡的利率。

passages.original: If I can catch him once upon the hip, I will feed fat the ancient grudge I bear him.
passages.vernacular: 如果我能一次抓住佢嘅把柄,我就要養肥我對佢嘅舊恨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我能一次抓住他的把柄,我就要養肥我對他的舊恨。

passages.original: He hates our sacred nation, and he rails, Even there where merchants most do congregate, On me, my bargains, and my well-won thrift, Which he calls interest.
passages.vernacular: 佢恨我哋神聖嘅民族,甚至喺商人最聚集嘅地方,佢都辱罵我、我嘅買賣同我正當賺嚟嘅利潤,佢稱之為利息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他恨我們神聖的民族,甚至在商人最聚集的地方,他也辱罵我、我的買賣和我正當賺來的利潤,他稱之為利息。

passages.original: Cursed be my tribe If I forgive him!
passages.vernacular: 如果我饒恕佢,就詛咒我嘅族人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我饒恕他,就詛咒我的族人!

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Shylock, do you hear?
passages.vernacular: 夏洛克,你聽見嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夏洛克,你聽見嗎?

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: I am debating of my present store, And by the near guess of my memory I cannot instantly raise up the gross Of full three thousand ducats.
passages.vernacular: 我喺盤算我現有嘅存款,憑我記憶嘅大致估計,我唔能夠即刻湊足整整三千杜卡特。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在盤算我現有的存款,憑我記憶的大致估計,我不能馬上湊足整整三千杜卡特。

passages.original: What of that?
passages.vernacular: 嗰又點樣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那又怎樣?

passages.original: Tubal, a wealthy Hebrew of my tribe, Will furnish me. But soft!
passages.vernacular: 圖巴爾,我同族嘅一位富有嘅希伯嚟人,會供應我。但慢住!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 圖巴爾,我同族的一位富有的希伯來人,會供應我。但慢著!

passages.original: how many months Do you desire?
passages.vernacular: 你想要幾個月?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你想要幾個月?

passages.original: [To Antonio.]
passages.vernacular: [對安東尼奧。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對安東尼奧。]

passages.original: Rest you fair, good signior, Your worship was the last man in our mouths.
passages.vernacular: 願你安好,好先生,閣下係我哋最後談起嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願你安好,好先生,閣下是我們最後談起的人。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: Shylock, albeit I neither lend nor borrow By taking nor by giving of excess, Yet to supply the ripe wants of my friend, I’ll break a custom.
passages.vernacular: 夏洛克,雖然我既不靠多取都不靠多畀嚟借貸,但為了供應我朋友迫切嘅需要,我要破一次例。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夏洛克,雖然我既不靠多取也不靠多給來借貸,但為了供應我朋友迫切的需要,我要破一次例。

passages.original: [To Bassanio.]
passages.vernacular: [對巴薩尼奧。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對巴薩尼奧。]

passages.original: Is he yet possess’d How much ye would?
passages.vernacular: 佢已經知道你要多少咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他已經知道你要多少了嗎?

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: Ay, ay, three thousand ducats.
passages.vernacular: 對,對,三千杜卡特。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,對,三千杜卡特。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: And for three months.
passages.vernacular: 三個月。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三個月。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: I had forgot, three months, you told me so.
passages.vernacular: 我忘喇,三個月,你告訴過我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我忘了,三個月,你告訴過我。

passages.original: Well then, your bond.
passages.vernacular: 好,咁你嘅契約。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,那麼你的契約。

passages.original: And let me see, but hear you, Methought you said you neither lend nor borrow Upon advantage.
passages.vernacular: 讓我想想,但聽住,我以為你講你既不借出都不借入要利息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我想想,但聽著,我以為你說你既不借出也不借入要利息。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: I do never use it.
passages.vernacular: 我從不咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從不這樣。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: When Jacob graz’d his uncle Laban’s sheep,— This Jacob from our holy Abram was As his wise mother wrought in his behalf, The third possessor; ay, he was the third.
passages.vernacular: 當雅各牧放佢舅舅拉班嘅羊時,——呢雅各係我哋神聖嘅亞伯拉罕嘅第三代繼承人,由佢聰明嘅母親為佢謀劃;對,佢係第三代。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當雅各牧放他舅舅拉班的羊時,——這雅各是我們神聖的亞伯拉罕的第三代繼承人,由他聰明的母親為他謀劃;對,他是第三代。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: And what of him?
passages.vernacular: 佢又點樣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他又怎樣?

passages.original: Did he take interest?
passages.vernacular: 佢收利息嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他收利息嗎?

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: No, not take interest, not, as you would say, Directly interest; mark what Jacob did.
passages.vernacular: 不,沒收利息,唔係,像你所講嘅,直接收利息;睇雅各做咗乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,沒有收利息,不是,像你所說的,直接收利息;看雅各做了什麼。

passages.original: When Laban and himself were compromis’d That all the eanlings which were streak’d and pied Should fall as Jacob’s hire, the ewes being rank In end of autumn turned to the rams, And when the work of generation was Between these woolly breeders in the act, The skilful shepherd pill’d me certain wands, And in the doing of the deed of kind, He stuck them up before the fulsome ewes, Who then conceiving did in eaning time Fall parti-colour’d lambs, and those were Jacob’s.
passages.vernacular: 當拉班同佢達成協議,所有帶條紋同斑點嘅羔羊都歸雅各作工價,母羊喺秋末發情,轉向公羊,當呢啲長毛嘅繁殖者正在交配,嗰機靈嘅牧人剝咗幾根樹枝,喺行呢天然之事時,把佢哋插喺發情嘅母羊面前,母羊於是懷孕,到產羔時生下雜色羊羔,嗰啲就係雅各嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當拉班和他達成協議,所有帶條紋和斑點的羔羊都歸雅各作工價,母羊在秋末發情,轉向公羊,當這些長毛的繁殖者正在交配,那機靈的牧人剝了幾根樹枝,在行這天然之事時,把它們插在發情的母羊面前,母羊於是懷孕,到產羔時生下雜色羊羔,那些就是雅各的。

passages.original: This was a way to thrive, and he was blest; And thrift is blessing if men steal it not.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係一條興旺嘅路,佢蒙咗福;而收穫係福氣,只要人唔係偷嚟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是一條興旺的路,他蒙了福;而收穫是福氣,只要人不是偷來的。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: This was a venture, sir, that Jacob serv’d for, A thing not in his power to bring to pass, But sway’d and fashion’d by the hand of heaven.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係雅各為之服務嘅一次冒險,一件不喺佢能力範圍內促成嘅事,而係由上天嘅手所支配同塑造嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是雅各為之服務的一次冒險,一件不在他能力範圍內促成的事,而是由上天的手所支配和塑造的。

passages.original: Was this inserted to make interest good?
passages.vernacular: 呢個係插進嚟證明收利息正當嘅嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是插進來證明收利息正當的嗎?

passages.original: Or is your gold and silver ewes and rams?
passages.vernacular: 定係你嘅金銀就係母羊同公羊?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還是你的金銀就是母羊和公羊?

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: I cannot tell; I make it breed as fast.
passages.vernacular: 我講不準;我讓佢繁殖得一樣快。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說不準;我讓它繁殖得一樣快。

passages.original: But note me, signior.
passages.vernacular: 但請注意我,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但請注意我,先生。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: Mark you this, Bassanio, The devil can cite Scripture for his purpose.
passages.vernacular: 注意呢個,巴薩尼奧,魔鬼都能為自己嘅目的引用聖經。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 注意這個,巴薩尼奧,魔鬼也能為自己的目的引用聖經。

passages.original: An evil soul producing holy witness Is like a villain with a smiling cheek, A goodly apple rotten at the heart.
passages.vernacular: 一個邪惡嘅靈魂引出神聖嘅見證,就像一個臉上帶笑嘅惡棍,一個外表漂亮、內心腐爛嘅蘋果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個邪惡的靈魂引出神聖的見證,就像一個臉上帶笑的惡棍,一個外表漂亮、內心腐爛的蘋果。

passages.original: O, what a goodly outside falsehood hath!
passages.vernacular: 啊,虛偽有多漂亮嘅外表!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,虛偽有多漂亮的外表!

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: Three thousand ducats, ’tis a good round sum.
passages.vernacular: 三千杜卡特,係個整數。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 三千杜卡特,是個整數。

passages.original: Three months from twelve, then let me see the rate.
passages.vernacular: 十二減三個月,讓我睇睇利率。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 十二減三個月,讓我看看利率。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: Well, Shylock, shall we be beholding to you?
passages.vernacular: 好,夏洛克,我哋能得到你嘅幫助嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,夏洛克,我們能得到你的幫助嗎?

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: Signior Antonio, many a time and oft In the Rialto you have rated me About my moneys and my usances.
passages.vernacular: 安東尼奧先生,許多次、多少次,喺雷雅托你責罵我,講我嘅錢同我嘅利息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安東尼奧先生,許多次、多少次,在雷雅托你責罵我,說我的錢和我的利息。

passages.original: Still have I borne it with a patient shrug, (For suff’rance is the badge of all our tribe.)
passages.vernacular: 我總是耐心地聳聳肩忍受,(因為忍耐係我哋全族嘅標記。)
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我總是耐心地聳聳肩忍受,(因為忍耐是我們全族的標記。)

passages.original: You call me misbeliever, cut-throat dog, And spet upon my Jewish gaberdine, And all for use of that which is mine own.
passages.vernacular: 你叫我異教徒、割喉狗,朝我猶太長袍吐唾沫,而呢一切就為了我使用屬於我自己嘅嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你叫我異教徒、割喉狗,朝我猶太長袍吐唾沫,而這一切就為了我使用屬於我自己的東西。

passages.original: Well then, it now appears you need my help.
passages.vernacular: 好,而家睇來你需要我嘅幫助喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,現在看來你需要我的幫助了。

passages.original: Go to, then, you come to me, and you say “Shylock, we would have moneys.”
passages.vernacular: 好,咁,你嚟找我,你講「夏洛克,我哋想要錢」。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,那麼,你來找我,你說「夏洛克,我們想要錢」。

passages.original: You say so: You that did void your rheum upon my beard, And foot me as you spurn a stranger cur Over your threshold, moneys is your suit.
passages.vernacular: 你咁講:你呢個曾喺我鬍子上吐痰,把我當陌生野狗一樣從你門檻上踢開嘅人,而家請求嘅係錢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你這麼說:你這個曾在我鬍子上吐痰,把我當陌生野狗一樣從你門檻上踢開的人,現在請求的是錢。

passages.original: What should I say to you?
passages.vernacular: 我該對你講乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我該對你說什麼?

passages.original: Should I not say “Hath a dog money?
passages.vernacular: 我唔係該講「一條狗有錢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不是該說「一條狗有錢嗎?

passages.original: Is it possible A cur can lend three thousand ducats?”
passages.vernacular: 一隻雜種狗可能借出三千杜卡特嗎?」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一隻雜種狗可能借出三千杜卡特嗎?」

passages.original: Or Shall I bend low and, in a bondman’s key, With bated breath and whisp’ring humbleness, Say this:
passages.vernacular: 或者我該彎下腰,用奴隸嘅腔調,屏住呼吸,低聲下氣地講:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 或者我該彎下腰,用奴隸的腔調,屏住呼吸,低聲下氣地說:

passages.original: “Fair sir, you spet on me on Wednesday last; You spurn’d me such a day;
passages.vernacular: 「好先生,你上星期三朝我吐咗唾沫;你某天踢咗我;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「好先生,你上星期三朝我吐了唾沫;你某天踢了我;

passages.original: another time You call’d me dog; and for these courtesies I’ll lend you thus much moneys”?
passages.vernacular: 另一次你叫我狗;為了呢啲禮貌,我就借畀你咁多錢」?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 另一次你叫我狗;為了這些禮貌,我就借給你這麼多錢」?

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: I am as like to call thee so again, To spet on thee again, to spurn thee too.
passages.vernacular: 我好可能仲會再咁樣叫你,再朝你吐唾沫,再踢你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很可能還會再這樣叫你,再朝你吐唾沫,再踢你。

passages.original: If thou wilt lend this money, lend it not As to thy friends, for when did friendship take A breed for barren metal of his friend?
passages.vernacular: 如果你要借呢錢,別當作借畀你嘅朋友,因點解時候友誼會為不生育嘅金屬向朋友收取孳息?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你要借這錢,別當作借給你的朋友,因為什麼時候友誼會為不生育的金屬向朋友收取孳息?

passages.original: But lend it rather to thine enemy, Who if he break, thou mayst with better face Exact the penalty.
passages.vernacular: 而係寧可借畀你嘅敵人,佢若違約,你更能理直氣壯地索取罰金。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而是寧可借給你的敵人,他若違約,你更能理直氣壯地索取罰金。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: Why, look you how you storm!
passages.vernacular: 哎,睇你點發火!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎,看你怎麼發火!

passages.original: I would be friends with you, and have your love, Forget the shames that you have stain’d me with, Supply your present wants, and take no doit Of usance for my moneys, and you’ll not hear me, This is kind I offer.
passages.vernacular: 我想同你做朋友,得到你嘅愛,忘記你加喺我身上嘅羞辱,供應你當前嘅需要,不收一個銅板嘅利息,你卻不聽我講,呢個係我提供嘅好意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想與你做朋友,得到你的愛,忘記你加在我身上的羞辱,供應你當前的需要,不收一個銅板的利息,你卻不聽我說,這是我提供的好意。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: This were kindness.
passages.vernacular: 呢將係好意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這將是好意。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: This kindness will I show.
passages.vernacular: 呢份好意我願意表示。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這份好意我願意表示。

passages.original: Go with me to a notary, seal me there Your single bond;
passages.vernacular: 跟我去見公證人,喺嗰度畀我蓋印你單獨嘅契約;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 跟我去見公證人,在那裡給我蓋印你單獨的契約;

passages.original: and in a merry sport, If you repay me not on such a day, In such a place, such sum or sums as are Express’d in the condition, let the forfeit Be nominated for an equal pound Of your fair flesh, to be cut off and taken In what part of your body pleaseth me.
passages.vernacular: 並且,作為一場好玩嘅遊戲,如果你不喺某天、某地,按條款中表明嘅款項仲我,就讓罰金訂為你美麗身上一磅肉,由我喺你身體任何鍾意嘅部位割下取走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 並且,作為一場好玩的遊戲,如果你不在某天、某地,按條款中表明的款項還我,就讓罰金訂為你美麗身上一磅肉,由我在你身體任何喜歡的部位割下取走。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: Content, in faith, I’ll seal to such a bond, And say there is much kindness in the Jew.
passages.vernacular: 同意,講真嘅,我願蓋印咁樣嘅契約,並講猶太人好有好意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同意,說真的,我願蓋印這樣的契約,並說猶太人很有好意。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: You shall not seal to such a bond for me, I’ll rather dwell in my necessity.
passages.vernacular: 你唔好為我蓋印咁樣嘅契約,我寧可繼續處於我嘅窘境。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不要為我蓋印這樣的契約,我寧可繼續處於我的窘境。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: Why, fear not, man, I will not forfeit it, Within these two months, that’s a month before This bond expires, I do expect return Of thrice three times the value of this bond.
passages.vernacular: 哎,別怕,老兄,我唔會違約,兩個月內,就係喺呢契約到期前一個月,我預計收回呢契約價值嘅三乘三倍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎,別怕,老兄,我不會違約,兩個月內,就是在這契約到期前一個月,我預計收回這契約價值的三乘三倍。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: O father Abram, what these Christians are, Whose own hard dealings teaches them suspect The thoughts of others.
passages.vernacular: 啊亞伯拉罕父親,呢啲基督徒係點樣嘅人,佢哋自己嘅嚴酷交易教會佢哋懷疑別人嘅心思。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊亞伯拉罕父親,這些基督徒是怎樣的人,他們自己的嚴酷交易教會他們懷疑別人的心思。

passages.original: Pray you, tell me this, If he should break his day, what should I gain By the exaction of the forfeiture?
passages.vernacular: 請你告訴我呢個,如果佢違約喇,我通過索取罰金能得到乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你告訴我這個,如果他違約了,我通過索取罰金能得到什麼?

passages.original: A pound of man’s flesh, taken from a man, Is not so estimable, profitable neither, As flesh of muttons, beefs, or goats.
passages.vernacular: 一磅人肉,從人身上取下,不像羊、牛或山羊嘅肉咁值錢,都冇咁有利。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一磅人肉,從人身上取下,不像羊、牛或山羊的肉那麼值錢,也沒那麼有利。

passages.original: I say, To buy his favour, I extend this friendship.
passages.vernacular: 我講,為了買得佢嘅好感,我才伸出呢份友誼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說,為了買得他的好感,我才伸出這份友誼。

passages.original: If he will take it, so.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢接受,就咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他接受,就這樣。

passages.original: If not, adieu, And for my love I pray you wrong me not.
passages.vernacular: 如果不接受,再會,為了我嘅愛,請你唔好冤枉我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果不接受,再會,為了我的愛,請你不要冤枉我。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: Yes, Shylock, I will seal unto this bond.
passages.vernacular: 好,夏洛克,我願意喺呢契約上蓋印。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,夏洛克,我願意在這契約上蓋印。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: Then meet me forthwith at the notary’s, Give him direction for this merry bond, And I will go and purse the ducats straight, See to my house left in the fearful guard Of an unthrifty knave, and presently I’ll be with you.
passages.vernacular: 咁即刻喺公證人處同我會面,畀佢指示寫呢份好玩嘅契約,我即刻去把杜卡特裝進錢袋,去睇我留喺一個不節儉嘅奴才膽怯睇守下嘅房子,然後即刻嚟見你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼立刻在公證人處與我會面,給他指示寫這份好玩的契約,我立刻去把杜卡特裝進錢袋,去看我留在一個不節儉的奴才膽怯看守下的房子,然後馬上來見你。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: Hie thee, gentle Jew.
passages.vernacular: 去吧,溫和嘅猶太人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去吧,溫和的猶太人。

passages.original: [Exit Shylock.]
passages.vernacular: [夏洛克下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [夏洛克下。]

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: This Hebrew will turn Christian; he grows kind.
passages.vernacular: 呢個希伯嚟人要變成基督徒喇;佢變得和善喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個希伯來人要變成基督徒了;他變得和善了。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: I like not fair terms and a villain’s mind.
passages.vernacular: 我不鍾意漂亮嘅條款配惡棍嘅心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不喜歡漂亮的條款配惡棍的心。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: Come on; in this there can be no dismay; My ships come home a month before the day.
passages.vernacular: 嚟吧;喺呢件事上唔使驚慌;我嘅船喺到期前一個月就會回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來吧;在這件事上不用驚慌;我的船在到期前一個月就會回來。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act II, Scene I — Belmont. A Room in Portia’s House 第二幕第一場:貝爾蒙特,鮑西婭家一室

passages.original: Flourish of cornets. Enter the Prince of Morocco, a tawny Moor all in white, and three or four followers accordingly, with Portia, Nerissa and their train.
passages.vernacular: [號角齊鳴。摩洛哥親王,一位全身白衣嘅黝黑摩爾人,偕三四名隨從,鮑西婭、尼莉莎及其侍從上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [號角齊鳴。摩洛哥親王,一位全身白衣的黝黑摩爾人,偕三四名隨從,鮑西婭、尼莉莎及其侍從上。]

passages.title: Prince of Morocco 摩洛哥親王
passages.original: Mislike me not for my complexion, The shadowed livery of the burnish’d sun, To whom I am a neighbour, and near bred.
passages.vernacular: 唔好因我嘅膚色而嫌棄我,嗰個係被烈日磨亮後投下陰影嘅制服,我同佢相鄰,離佢近。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要因我的膚色而嫌棄我,那是被烈日磨亮後投下陰影的制服,我與它相鄰,離它近。

passages.original: Bring me the fairest creature northward born, Where Phœbus’ fire scarce thaws the icicles, And let us make incision for your love To prove whose blood is reddest, his or mine.
passages.vernacular: 把北方生嘅最美嘅人帶嚟,喺嗰度太陽神嘅火幾乎融不咗冰柱,讓我哋為你嘅愛劃開皮膚,睇睇邊個嘅血更紅,佢嘅定係我嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把北方生的最美的人帶來,在那裡太陽神的火幾乎融不了冰柱,讓我們為你的愛劃開皮膚,看看誰的血更紅,他的還是我的。

passages.original: I tell thee, lady, this aspect of mine Hath fear’d the valiant;
passages.vernacular: 小姐,我告訴你,我呢副容貌曾使勇士害怕;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小姐,我告訴你,我這副容貌曾使勇士害怕;

passages.original: by my love I swear The best-regarded virgins of our clime Have lov’d it too.
passages.vernacular: 憑我嘅愛起誓,我哋嗰一帶最受重視嘅處女都愛過佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑我的愛起誓,我們那一帶最受重視的處女也愛過它。

passages.original: I would not change this hue, Except to steal your thoughts, my gentle queen.
passages.vernacular: 我唔願改變呢個膚色,除非係為了偷取你嘅心思,我溫柔嘅女王。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不願改變這個膚色,除非是為了偷取你的心思,我溫柔的女王。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: In terms of choice I am not solely led By nice direction of a maiden’s eyes;
passages.vernacular: 喺選擇上我並不單單被少女眼光嘅挑剔所引導;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在選擇上我並不單單被少女眼光的挑剔所引導;

passages.original: Besides, the lott’ry of my destiny Bars me the right of voluntary choosing.
passages.vernacular: 此外,我命運嘅抽籤剝奪咗我自願選擇嘅權利。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 此外,我命運的抽籤剝奪了我自願選擇的權利。

passages.original: But if my father had not scanted me And hedg’d me by his wit to yield myself His wife who wins me by that means I told you, Yourself, renowned Prince, then stood as fair As any comer I have look’d on yet For my affection.
passages.vernacular: 但如果我父親冇限制我、用佢嘅智慧圈住我,使我屈服於以我告訴你嘅嗰種方式贏得我嘅人,做佢嘅妻子,你,著名嘅親王,咁喺我至今睇過嘅所有嚟者中,你喺我嘅感情上都站得一樣好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但如果我父親沒有限制我、用他的智慧圈住我,使我屈服於以我告訴你的那種方式贏得我的人,做他的妻子,你,著名的親王,那麼在我至今看過的所有來者中,你在我的感情上也站得一樣好。

passages.title: Prince of Morocco 摩洛哥親王
passages.original: Even for that I thank you.
passages.vernacular: 即便為此我都謝謝你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 即便為此我也謝謝你。

passages.original: Therefore I pray you lead me to the caskets To try my fortune.
passages.vernacular: 所以請你領我到匣子嗰度去試我嘅運氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以請你領我到匣子那裡去試我的運氣。

passages.original: By this scimitar That slew the Sophy and a Persian prince, That won three fields of Sultan Solyman, I would o’erstare the sternest eyes that look, Outbrave the heart most daring on the earth, Pluck the young sucking cubs from the she-bear, Yea, mock the lion when he roars for prey, To win thee, lady.
passages.vernacular: 憑呢把彎刀,佢殺咗波斯國王同一位波斯親王,贏咗蘇丹蘇萊曼嘅三場戰役,我敢瞪視最嚴厲嘅目光,勝過世上最大膽嘅心,從母熊口中搶走食奶嘅小熊,對,嘲笑獅子為獵物吼叫時,為了贏得你,小姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑這把彎刀,它殺了波斯國王和一位波斯親王,贏了蘇丹蘇萊曼的三場戰役,我敢瞪視最嚴厲的目光,勝過世上最大膽的心,從母熊口中搶走吃奶的小熊,對,嘲笑獅子為獵物吼叫時,為了贏得你,小姐。

passages.original: But, alas the while!
passages.vernacular: 但係,唉!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但是,唉!

passages.original: If Hercules and Lichas play at dice Which is the better man, the greater throw May turn by fortune from the weaker hand:
passages.vernacular: 如果大力神赫拉克勒斯同利卡斯擲骰子比邊個更強,更大嘅點數可能憑運氣落到較弱嘅手裡:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果大力神赫拉克勒斯和利卡斯擲骰子比誰更強,更大的點數可能憑運氣落到較弱的手裡:

passages.original: So is Alcides beaten by his rage, And so may I, blind Fortune leading me, Miss that which one unworthier may attain, And die with grieving.
passages.vernacular: 所以赫拉克勒斯被佢自己嘅怒氣打敗,我都可能,盲目的命運領住我,錯過一個更不配嘅人能得到嘅嘢,悲傷而死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以赫拉克勒斯被他自己的怒氣打敗,我也可能,盲目的命運領著我,錯過一個更不配的人能得到的東西,悲傷而死。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: You must take your chance, And either not attempt to choose at all, Or swear before you choose, if you choose wrong Never to speak to lady afterward In way of marriage.
passages.vernacular: 你得碰你嘅運氣,要麼完全不去試住選,要麼喺選之前發誓,如果選錯喇,以後永遠不向任何小姐求婚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你得碰你的運氣,要麼完全不去試著選,要麼在選之前發誓,如果選錯了,以後永遠不向任何小姐求婚。

passages.original: Therefore be advis’d.
passages.vernacular: 所以要想清楚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以要想清楚。

passages.title: Prince of Morocco 摩洛哥親王
passages.original: Nor will not.
passages.vernacular: 我唔會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不會。

passages.original: Come, bring me unto my chance.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,帶我去碰我嘅運氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,帶我去碰我的運氣。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: First, forward to the temple.
passages.vernacular: 先往前去神殿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先往前去神殿。

passages.original: After dinner Your hazard shall be made.
passages.vernacular: 飯後你將冒險一試。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 飯後你將冒險一試。

passages.title: Prince of Morocco 摩洛哥親王
passages.original: Good fortune then, To make me blest or cursed’st among men!
passages.vernacular: 咁願好運使我成為人間最有福嘅,或最受詛咒嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼願好運使我成為人間最有福的,或最受詛咒的!

passages.original: [Cornets. Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [號角。同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [號角。同下。]

chapters.title: Act II, Scene II — Venice. A Street 第二幕第二場:威尼斯街道

passages.original: Enter Launcelet Gobbo, the clown, alone.
passages.vernacular: [小丑朗斯洛特·高波獨自上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [小丑朗斯洛特·高波獨自上。]

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: Certainly my conscience will serve me to run from this Jew my master.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅良心當然會允許我逃離呢個猶太人,我嘅主人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的良心當然會允許我逃離這個猶太人,我的主人。

passages.original: The fiend is at mine elbow and tempts me, saying to me “Gobbo, Launcelet Gobbo, good Launcelet” or “good Gobbo,” or “good Launcelet Gobbo, use your legs, take the start, run away.”
passages.vernacular: 魔鬼喺我手肘邊引誘我,對我講:「高波,朗斯洛特·高波,好朗斯洛特」,或「好高波」,或「好朗斯洛特·高波,用你嘅腿,搶先出發,逃跑。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 魔鬼在我手肘邊引誘我,對我說:「高波,朗斯洛特·高波,好朗斯洛特」,或「好高波」,或「好朗斯洛特·高波,用你的腿,搶先出發,逃跑。」

passages.original: My conscience says “No; take heed, honest Launcelet, take heed, honest Gobbo” or, as aforesaid, “honest Launcelet Gobbo, do not run, scorn running with thy heels.”
passages.vernacular: 我嘅良心講:「不;當心,誠實嘅朗斯洛特,當心,誠實嘅高波」,或如前所講,「誠實嘅朗斯洛特·高波,別跑,用腳跟鄙視逃跑。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的良心說:「不;當心,誠實的朗斯洛特,當心,誠實的高波」,或如前所說,「誠實的朗斯洛特·高波,別跑,用腳跟鄙視逃跑。」

passages.original: Well, the most courageous fiend bids me pack. “Fia!”
passages.vernacular: 好,最勇敢嘅魔鬼叫我收拾包袱。「快!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,最勇敢的魔鬼叫我收拾包袱。「快!」

passages.original: says the fiend, “away!”
passages.vernacular: 魔鬼講:「走!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 魔鬼說:「走!」

passages.original: says the fiend.
passages.vernacular: 魔鬼講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 魔鬼說。

passages.original: “For the heavens, rouse up a brave mind,” says the fiend, “and run.”
passages.vernacular: 「睇喺天嘅份上,鼓起勇敢嘅心,」魔鬼講,「跑吧。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「看在天的份上,鼓起勇敢的心,」魔鬼說,「跑吧。」

passages.original: Well, my conscience, hanging about the neck of my heart, says very wisely to me “My honest friend Launcelet, being an honest man’s son”—or rather an honest woman’s son, for indeed my father did something smack, something grow to, he had a kind of taste;—well, my conscience says “Launcelet, budge not.”
passages.vernacular: 好,我嘅良心掛喺我心嘅脖子上,好聰明地對我講:「我誠實嘅朋友朗斯洛特,你係誠實人嘅兒子」——或者講係誠實女人嘅兒子,因為其實我父親有點沾邊,有點偏向,佢有點口味;——好,我嘅良心講:「朗斯洛特,別動。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,我的良心掛在我心的脖子上,很聰明地對我說:「我誠實的朋友朗斯洛特,你是誠實人的兒子」——或者說是誠實女人的兒子,因為其實我父親有點沾邊,有點偏向,他有點口味;——好,我的良心說:「朗斯洛特,別動。」

passages.original: “Budge,” says the fiend.
passages.vernacular: 魔鬼講:「動。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 魔鬼說:「動。」

passages.original: “Budge not,” says my conscience.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅良心講:「別動。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的良心說:「別動。」

passages.original: “Conscience,” say I, “you counsel well.”
passages.vernacular: 我講:「良心,你勸得好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說:「良心,你勸得好。」

passages.original: “Fiend,” say I, “you counsel well.”
passages.vernacular: 我講:「魔鬼,你勸得好。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說:「魔鬼,你勸得好。」

passages.original: To be ruled by my conscience, I should stay with the Jew my master, who, (God bless the mark) is a kind of devil;
passages.vernacular: 聽從我嘅良心,我就該留喺猶太人我主人嗰度,佢(願上帝保佑)係一種魔鬼;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽從我的良心,我就該留在猶太人我主人那裡,他(願上帝保佑)是一種魔鬼;

passages.original: and, to run away from the Jew, I should be ruled by the fiend, who (saving your reverence) is the devil himself.
passages.vernacular: 而要從猶太人嗰度逃走,我就該聽從魔鬼,佢(恕我失禮)就係魔鬼本人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而要從猶太人那裡逃走,我就該聽從魔鬼,他(恕我失禮)就是魔鬼本人。

passages.original: Certainly the Jew is the very devil incarnation, and, in my conscience, my conscience is but a kind of hard conscience, to offer to counsel me to stay with the Jew.
passages.vernacular: 猶太人確實係魔鬼嘅化身,而依我嘅良心,我嘅良心只係一種冷酷嘅良心,竟然勸我留喺猶太人嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 猶太人確實是魔鬼的化身,而依我的良心,我的良心只是一種冷酷的良心,竟然勸我留在猶太人那裡。

passages.original: The fiend gives the more friendly counsel.
passages.vernacular: 魔鬼畀嘅勸告更友好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 魔鬼給的勸告更友好。

passages.original: I will run, fiend, my heels are at your commandment, I will run.
passages.vernacular: 我要跑,魔鬼,我嘅腳跟聽你吩咐,我要跑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要跑,魔鬼,我的腳跟聽你吩咐,我要跑。

passages.original: Enter Old Gobbo with a basket.
passages.vernacular: [老高波提住籃子上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [老高波提著籃子上。]

passages.title: Old Gobbo 老高波
passages.original: Master young man, you, I pray you; which is the way to Master Jew’s?
passages.vernacular: 年輕嘅先生,請問你,邊條路去猶太老爺家?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 年輕的先生,請問你,哪條路去猶太老爺家?

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: [Aside.]
passages.vernacular: [旁白。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [旁白。]

passages.original: O heavens, this is my true-begotten father, who being more than sand-blind, high-gravel blind, knows me not.
passages.vernacular: 啊天呀,呢個係我親生嘅父親,佢比沙盲更盲,盲到高石子嘅地步,認不出我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊天哪,這是我親生的父親,他比沙盲更盲,盲到高石子的地步,認不出我。

passages.original: I will try confusions with him.
passages.vernacular: 我要用混亂嚟試佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要用混亂來試他。

passages.title: Old Gobbo 老高波
passages.original: Master young gentleman, I pray you, which is the way to Master Jew’s?
passages.vernacular: 年輕嘅先生,請問你,邊條路去猶太老爺家?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 年輕的先生,請問你,哪條路去猶太老爺家?

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: Turn up on your right hand at the next turning, but at the next turning of all on your left;
passages.vernacular: 喺下一個轉彎向右拐,但喺最後一個轉彎向左;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在下一個轉彎向右拐,但在最後一個轉彎向左;

passages.original: marry, at the very next turning, turn of no hand, but turn down indirectly to the Jew’s house.
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,喺最近嘅轉彎,不往任何一邊拐,而係迂迴地向下拐到猶太人嘅房子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,在最近的轉彎,不往任何一邊拐,而是迂迴地向下拐到猶太人的房子。

passages.title: Old Gobbo 老高波
passages.original: Be God’s sonties, ’twill be a hard way to hit.
passages.vernacular: 憑上帝嘅聖徒,呢路難找。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑上帝的聖徒,這路難找。

passages.original: Can you tell me whether one Launcelet, that dwells with him, dwell with him or no?
passages.vernacular: 你能告訴我一個叫朗斯洛特嘅,住喺佢家嘅,係唔係仲住喺嗰度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你能告訴我一個叫朗斯洛特的,住在他家的,是不是還住在那裡?

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: Talk you of young Master Launcelet? [Aside.]
passages.vernacular: 你講嘅係年輕嘅朗斯洛特少爺?[旁白。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說的是年輕的朗斯洛特少爺?[旁白。]

passages.original: Mark me now, now will I raise the waters.
passages.vernacular: 注意我,而家我要興起水波。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 注意我,現在我要興起水波。

passages.original: Talk you of young Master Launcelet?
passages.vernacular: 你講嘅係年輕嘅朗斯洛特少爺?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說的是年輕的朗斯洛特少爺?

passages.title: Old Gobbo 老高波
passages.original: No master, sir, but a poor man’s son, his father, though I say’t, is an honest exceeding poor man, and, God be thanked, well to live.
passages.vernacular: 唔係少爺,先生,只係窮人嘅兒子,佢父親,雖然係我講嘅,係個誠實嘅好窮嘅人,感謝上帝,日子過得去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不是少爺,先生,只是窮人的兒子,他父親,雖然是我說的,是個誠實的非常窮的人,感謝上帝,日子過得去。

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: Well, let his father be what he will, we talk of young Master Launcelet.
passages.vernacular: 好,不管佢父親係乜嘢人,我哋講嘅係年輕嘅朗斯洛特少爺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,不管他父親是什麼人,我們說的是年輕的朗斯洛特少爺。

passages.title: Old Gobbo 老高波
passages.original: Your worship’s friend, and Launcelet, sir.
passages.vernacular: 係您閣下嘅朋友,朗斯洛特,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是您閣下的朋友,朗斯洛特,先生。

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: But I pray you, ergo, old man, ergo, I beseech you, talk you of young Master Launcelet?
passages.vernacular: 但請你,因此,老人家,因此,我懇求你,你講嘅係年輕嘅朗斯洛特少爺?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但請你,因此,老人家,因此,我懇求你,你說的是年輕的朗斯洛特少爺?

passages.title: Old Gobbo 老高波
passages.original: Of Launcelet, an’t please your mastership.
passages.vernacular: 係朗斯洛特,蒙您少爺恩准。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是朗斯洛特,蒙您少爺恩准。

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: Ergo, Master Launcelet.
passages.vernacular: 因此,朗斯洛特少爺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因此,朗斯洛特少爺。

passages.original: Talk not of Master Launcelet, father, for the young gentleman, according to Fates and Destinies, and such odd sayings, the Sisters Three and such branches of learning, is indeed deceased, or, as you would say in plain terms, gone to heaven.
passages.vernacular: 唔好講朗斯洛特少爺,父親,因為呢位年輕紳士,按命運同定數,同呢啲古怪嘅話,三姊妹同呢類學問分支,確實已死,或者像你講嘅簡單話,上天去喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別說朗斯洛特少爺,父親,因為這位年輕紳士,按命運和定數,和這些古怪的話,三姊妹和這類學問分支,確實已死,或者像你說的簡單話,上天去了。

passages.title: Old Gobbo 老高波
passages.original: Marry, God forbid!
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,上帝不許!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,上帝不許!

passages.original: The boy was the very staff of my age, my very prop.
passages.vernacular: 嗰細路係我老年嘅拐杖,係我真正嘅支柱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那孩子是我老年的拐杖,是我真正的支柱。

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: [Aside.]
passages.vernacular: [旁白。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [旁白。]

passages.original: Do I look like a cudgel or a hovel-post, a staff or a prop?
passages.vernacular: 我睇起嚟像棍子或棚柱,一根拐杖或支柱嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看起來像棍子或棚柱,一根拐杖或支柱嗎?

passages.original: Do you know me, father?
passages.vernacular: 你認得我嗎,父親?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你認得我嗎,父親?

passages.title: Old Gobbo 老高波
passages.original: Alack the day!
passages.vernacular: 哎呀,呢一天!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎呀,這一天!

passages.original: I know you not, young gentleman, but I pray you tell me, is my boy, God rest his soul, alive or dead?
passages.vernacular: 我不認得你,年輕嘅先生,但請你告訴我,我嘅細路,願上帝安息佢嘅靈魂,係活住定係死喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不認得你,年輕的先生,但請你告訴我,我的孩子,願上帝安息他的靈魂,是活著還是死了?

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: Do you not know me, father?
passages.vernacular: 你不認得我嗎,父親?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不認得我嗎,父親?

passages.title: Old Gobbo 老高波
passages.original: Alack, sir, I am sand-blind, I know you not.
passages.vernacular: 唉,先生,我係沙盲,我不認得你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 唉,先生,我是沙盲,我不認得你。

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: Nay, indeed, if you had your eyes, you might fail of the knowing me:
passages.vernacular: 不,確實,即使你有眼睛,你都可能認不出我:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,確實,即使你有眼睛,你也可能認不出我:

passages.original: it is a wise father that knows his own child.
passages.vernacular: 認得自己細路嘅父親才係聰明父親。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 認得自己孩子的父親才是聰明父親。

passages.original: Well, old man, I will tell you news of your son.
passages.vernacular: 好,老人家,我告訴你你兒子嘅消息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,老人家,我告訴你你兒子的消息。

passages.original: Give me your blessing, truth will come to light, murder cannot be hid long, a man’s son may, but in the end truth will out.
passages.vernacular: 畀我你嘅祝福,真相會暴露,謀殺唔能夠隱藏太久,一個人嘅兒子可以,但最終真相會講出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 給我你的祝福,真相會暴露,謀殺不能隱藏太久,一個人的兒子可以,但最終真相會說出來。

passages.title: Old Gobbo 老高波
passages.original: Pray you, sir, stand up, I am sure you are not Launcelet my boy.
passages.vernacular: 請你,先生,站起嚟,我確定你唔係我嘅細路朗斯洛特。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你,先生,站起來,我確定你不是我的孩子朗斯洛特。

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: Pray you, let’s have no more fooling about it, but give me your blessing.
passages.vernacular: 請你,唔好再為此開玩笑,畀我你嘅祝福。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你,別再為此開玩笑,給我你的祝福。

passages.original: I am Launcelet, your boy that was, your son that is, your child that shall be.
passages.vernacular: 我係朗斯洛特,你曾經嘅細路,你而家嘅兒子,你將來嘅細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是朗斯洛特,你曾經的孩子,你現在的兒子,你將來的孩子。

passages.title: Old Gobbo 老高波
passages.original: I cannot think you are my son.
passages.vernacular: 我唔能夠想像你係我兒子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不能想像你是我兒子。

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: I know not what I shall think of that; but I am Launcelet, the Jew’s man, and I am sure Margery your wife is my mother.
passages.vernacular: 我唔知道對此該點想;但我係猶太人嘅僕人朗斯洛特,我確定瑪格麗係我母親,你嘅妻子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不知道對此該怎麼想;但我是猶太人的僕人朗斯洛特,我確定瑪格麗是我母親,你的妻子。

passages.title: Old Gobbo 老高波
passages.original: Her name is Margery, indeed.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅名字確實係瑪格麗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她的名字確實是瑪格麗。

passages.original: I’ll be sworn if thou be Launcelet, thou art mine own flesh and blood.
passages.vernacular: 我願發誓,如果你係朗斯洛特,你就係我嘅親骨肉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我願發誓,如果你是朗斯洛特,你就是我的親骨肉。

passages.original: Lord worshipped might he be, what a beard hast thou got!
passages.vernacular: 主啊,願佢受崇拜,你長咗點樣嘅鬍子!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 主啊,願他受崇拜,你長了怎樣的鬍子!

passages.original: Thou hast got more hair on thy chin than Dobbin my fill-horse has on his tail.
passages.vernacular: 你下巴上嘅毛比我嘅拉車馬杜賓尾巴上嘅仲多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你下巴上的毛比我的拉車馬杜賓尾巴上的還多。

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: It should seem, then, that Dobbin’s tail grows backward.
passages.vernacular: 咁睇來,杜賓嘅尾巴係向後長嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼看來,杜賓的尾巴是向後長的。

passages.original: I am sure he had more hair on his tail than I have on my face when I last saw him.
passages.vernacular: 我確定,我上次見佢時,佢尾巴上嘅毛比我臉上嘅仲多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我確定,我上次見它時,它尾巴上的毛比我臉上的還多。

passages.title: Old Gobbo 老高波
passages.original: Lord, how art thou changed!
passages.vernacular: 主啊,你點變喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 主啊,你怎麼變了!

passages.original: How dost thou and thy master agree?
passages.vernacular: 你同你主人相處得點樣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你和你主人相處得怎樣?

passages.original: I have brought him a present.
passages.vernacular: 我畀佢帶咗禮物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我給他帶了禮物。

passages.original: How ’gree you now?
passages.vernacular: 你哋而家相處得如何?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們現在相處得如何?

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: Well, well.
passages.vernacular: 好,好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,好。

passages.original: But for mine own part, as I have set up my rest to run away, so I will not rest till I have run some ground.
passages.vernacular: 但就我自己而言,既然我已決心逃走,喺跑出一段路之前我唔會休息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但就我自己而言,既然我已決心逃走,在跑出一段路之前我不會休息。

passages.original: My master’s a very Jew.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅主人係徹頭徹尾嘅猶太人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的主人是徹頭徹尾的猶太人。

passages.original: Give him a present!
passages.vernacular: 畀佢禮物!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 給他禮物!

passages.original: Give him a halter.
passages.vernacular: 畀佢一條絞索。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 給他一條絞索。

passages.original: I am famished in his service.
passages.vernacular: 我喺佢手下服務餓得要命。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在他手下服務餓得要命。

passages.original: You may tell every finger I have with my ribs.
passages.vernacular: 你可以用我嘅肋骨數我每根手指。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你可以用我的肋骨數我每根手指。

passages.original: Father, I am glad you are come, give me your present to one Master Bassanio, who indeed gives rare new liveries.
passages.vernacular: 父親,我好高興你嚟喇,把你嘅禮物畀一位叫巴薩尼奧嘅先生,佢確實發好特別嘅新制服。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 父親,我很高興你來了,把你的禮物給一位叫巴薩尼奧的先生,他確實發很特別的新制服。

passages.original: If I serve not him, I will run as far as God has any ground.
passages.vernacular: 如果我不服侍佢,我就跑到上帝有地嘅最遠處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我不服侍他,我就跑到上帝有地的最遠處。

passages.original: O rare fortune, here comes the man!
passages.vernacular: 啊好運,嗰個人嚟喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊好運,那個人來了!

passages.original: To him, father; for I am a Jew, if I serve the Jew any longer.
passages.vernacular: 去找佢,父親;因為如果我再服侍猶太人,我就係猶太人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去找他,父親;因為如果我再服侍猶太人,我就是猶太人。

passages.original: Enter Bassanio with Leonardo and a follower or two.
passages.vernacular: [巴薩尼奧偕李奧納多及一兩名隨從上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [巴薩尼奧偕李奧納多及一兩名隨從上。]

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: You may do so, but let it be so hasted that supper be ready at the farthest by five of the clock.
passages.vernacular: 你可以咁樣,但要做得快,使晚飯最遲五點鐘準備好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你可以這樣,但要做得快,使晚飯最遲五點鐘準備好。

passages.original: See these letters delivered, put the liveries to making, and desire Gratiano to come anon to my lodging.
passages.vernacular: 把呢啲信送出去,叫人做制服,並請葛拉蒂安諾即刻嚟我嘅住處。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把這些信送出去,叫人做制服,並請葛拉蒂安諾馬上來我的住處。

passages.original: [Exit a Servant.]
passages.vernacular: [一名僕人下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [一名僕人下。]

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: To him, father.
passages.vernacular: 去找佢,父親。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去找他,父親。

passages.title: Old Gobbo 老高波
passages.original: God bless your worship!
passages.vernacular: 願上帝保佑閣下!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願上帝保佑閣下!

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Gramercy, wouldst thou aught with me?
passages.vernacular: 多謝,你要我做乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 多謝,你要我做什麼?

passages.title: Old Gobbo 老高波
passages.original: Here’s my son, sir, a poor boy.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係我嘅兒子,先生,一個可憐嘅細路。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是我的兒子,先生,一個可憐的孩子。

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: Not a poor boy, sir, but the rich Jew’s man, that would, sir, as my father shall specify.
passages.vernacular: 唔係可憐嘅細路,先生,而係富猶太人嘅僕人,佢想,先生,如我父親將講明嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不是可憐的孩子,先生,而是富猶太人的僕人,他想,先生,如我父親將說明的。

passages.title: Old Gobbo 老高波
passages.original: He hath a great infection, sir, as one would say, to serve.
passages.vernacular: 佢有好大嘅傳染,先生,就像講嘅,要服務。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他有很大的傳染,先生,就像說的,要服務。

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: Indeed the short and the long is, I serve the Jew, and have a desire, as my father shall specify.
