passages.original: Your daughter spent in Genoa, as I heard, one night, fourscore ducats.
passages.vernacular: 你女兒喺熱嗰亞,我聽講,一夜花咗八十杜卡特。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你女兒在熱那亞,我聽說,一夜花了八十杜卡特。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: Thou stick’st a dagger in me.
passages.vernacular: 你喺我身上插咗一把刀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你在我身上插了一把刀。

passages.original: I shall never see my gold again.
passages.vernacular: 我再都睇唔到我嘅金子喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我再也看不到我的金子了。

passages.original: Fourscore ducats at a sitting!
passages.vernacular: 一次就八十杜卡特!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一次就八十杜卡特!

passages.original: Fourscore ducats!
passages.vernacular: 八十杜卡特!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 八十杜卡特!

passages.title: Tubal 圖巴爾
passages.original: There came divers of Antonio’s creditors in my company to Venice that swear he cannot choose but break.
passages.vernacular: 有好幾位安東尼奧嘅債主同我同行嚟威尼斯,佢哋發誓佢唔可能不破產。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有好幾位安東尼奧的債主與我同行來威尼斯,他們發誓他不可能不破產。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: I am very glad of it.
passages.vernacular: 我好高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我非常高興。

passages.original: I’ll plague him, I’ll torture him.
passages.vernacular: 我要折磨佢,我要拷打佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要折磨他,我要拷打他。

passages.original: I am glad of it.
passages.vernacular: 我好高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很高興。

passages.title: Tubal 圖巴爾
passages.original: One of them showed me a ring that he had of your daughter for a monkey.
passages.vernacular: 其中一個畀我睇咗一枚戒指,係佢用一隻猴子從你女兒嗰度換嚟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其中一個給我看了一枚戒指,是他用一隻猴子從你女兒那裡換來的。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: Out upon her!
passages.vernacular: 去佢嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去她的!

passages.original: Thou torturest me, Tubal.
passages.vernacular: 你喺拷打我,圖巴爾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你在拷打我,圖巴爾。

passages.original: It was my turquoise, I had it of Leah when I was a bachelor.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係我嘅綠松石,我單身時從利亞嗰度得嚟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是我的綠松石,我單身時從利亞那裡得來的。

passages.original: I would not have given it for a wilderness of monkeys.
passages.vernacular: 就算畀我一整荒野嘅猴子我都唔會畀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就算給我一整荒野的猴子我也不會給。

passages.title: Tubal 圖巴爾
passages.original: But Antonio is certainly undone.
passages.vernacular: 但安東尼奧肯定完喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但安東尼奧肯定完了。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: Nay, that’s true, that’s very true.
passages.vernacular: 不,嗰個係真嘅,好真。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,那是真的,非常真。

passages.original: Go, Tubal, fee me an officer; bespeak him a fortnight before.
passages.vernacular: 去,圖巴爾,替我雇一個官差;提前兩星期預訂佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去,圖巴爾,替我雇一個官差;提前兩星期預訂他。

passages.original: I will have the heart of him if he forfeit, for were he out of Venice I can make what merchandise I will.
passages.vernacular: 如果佢違約,我要佢嘅心,因為佢若不喺威尼斯,我可以做任何買賣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果他違約,我要他的心,因為他若不在威尼斯,我可以做任何買賣。

passages.original: Go, Tubal, and meet me at our synagogue.
passages.vernacular: 去,圖巴爾,喺我哋嘅猶太會堂同我會面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去,圖巴爾,在我們的猶太會堂與我會面。

passages.original: Go, good Tubal, at our synagogue, Tubal.
passages.vernacular: 去,好圖巴爾,喺我哋嘅猶太會堂,圖巴爾。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去,好圖巴爾,在我們的猶太會堂,圖巴爾。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act III, Scene II — Belmont. A Room in Portia’s House 第三幕第二場:貝爾蒙特,鮑西婭家一室

passages.original: Enter Bassanio, Portia, Gratiano, Nerissa and all their trains.
passages.vernacular: [巴薩尼奧、鮑西婭、葛拉蒂安諾、尼莉莎及其侍從上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [巴薩尼奧、鮑西婭、葛拉蒂安諾、尼莉莎及其侍從上。]

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: I pray you tarry, pause a day or two Before you hazard, for in choosing wrong I lose your company;
passages.vernacular: 請你稍等,等一兩天再冒險,因為選錯咗我就失去你嘅陪伴;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你稍等,等一兩天再冒險,因為選錯了我就失去你的陪伴;

passages.original: therefore forbear a while.
passages.vernacular: 所以請暫時克制。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以請暫時克制。

passages.original: There’s something tells me (but it is not love) I would not lose you, and you know yourself Hate counsels not in such a quality.
passages.vernacular: 有個嘢告訴我(但嗰唔係愛),我唔願失去你,你自己都知道,恨唔會畀咁樣嘅勸告。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有個東西告訴我(但那不是愛),我不願失去你,你自己也知道,恨不會給這樣的勸告。

passages.original: But lest you should not understand me well,— And yet a maiden hath no tongue but thought,— I would detain you here some month or two Before you venture for me.
passages.vernacular: 但免得你不太明白我,——不過少女除咗思想冇舌頭,——我想把你留喺呢度一兩個月,再讓你為我冒險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但免得你不太明白我,——不過少女除了思想沒有舌頭,——我想把你留在這裡一兩個月,再讓你為我冒險。

passages.original: I could teach you How to choose right, but then I am forsworn.
passages.vernacular: 我可以教你點樣選對,但嗰樣我就違背誓言喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我可以教你怎樣選對,但那樣我就違背誓言了。

passages.original: So will I never be.
passages.vernacular: 我永遠唔會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我永遠不會。

passages.original: So may you miss me.
passages.vernacular: 咁你或者選不中我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼你也許選不中我。

passages.original: But if you do, you’ll make me wish a sin, That I had been forsworn.
passages.vernacular: 但如果你選不中,你會使我希望犯一樁罪,希望我已違背咗誓言。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但如果你選不中,你會使我希望犯一樁罪,希望我已違背了誓言。

passages.original: Beshrew your eyes, They have o’erlook’d me and divided me.
passages.vernacular: 該詛咒你嘅眼睛,佢哋睇過我,並把我分開喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 該詛咒你的眼睛,它們看過我,並把我分開了。

passages.original: One half of me is yours, the other half yours, Mine own, I would say;
passages.vernacular: 我一半屬於你,另一半都屬於你,係我自己嘅,我想講;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一半屬於你,另一半也屬於你,是我自己的,我想說;

passages.original: but if mine, then yours, And so all yours.
passages.vernacular: 但如果係我嘅,嗰個就係你嘅,所以全係你嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但如果是我的,那就是你的,所以全是你的。

passages.original: O these naughty times Puts bars between the owners and their rights!
passages.vernacular: 啊,呢啲邪惡嘅時代喺所有者同佢哋嘅權利之間設下阻隔!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,這些邪惡的時代在所有者與他們的權利之間設下阻隔!

passages.original: And so though yours, not yours.
passages.vernacular: 所以雖然係你嘅,卻唔係你嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以雖然是你的,卻不是你的。

passages.original: Prove it so, Let Fortune go to hell for it, not I.
passages.vernacular: 如果證明如此,就讓命運為此下地獄,唔係我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果證明如此,就讓命運為此下地獄,不是我。

passages.original: I speak too long, but ’tis to peise the time, To eche it, and to draw it out in length, To stay you from election.
passages.vernacular: 我講得太久喇,但呢個係為了衡量時間,拉長佢,延長佢,讓你延遲選擇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說得太久了,但這是為了衡量時間,拉長它,延長它,讓你延遲選擇。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Let me choose, For as I am, I live upon the rack.
passages.vernacular: 讓我選吧,因為我而家活喺拷問架上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我選吧,因為我現在活在拷問架上。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Upon the rack, Bassanio!
passages.vernacular: 喺拷問架上,巴薩尼奧!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在拷問架上,巴薩尼奧!

passages.original: Then confess What treason there is mingled with your love.
passages.vernacular: 咁坦白,你嘅愛裡摻雜住乜嘢叛逆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼坦白,你的愛裡摻雜著什麼叛逆。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: None but that ugly treason of mistrust, Which makes me fear th’ enjoying of my love.
passages.vernacular: 冇別嘅,只有嗰醜陋嘅不信任嘅叛逆,使我害怕享受我嘅愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有別的,只有那醜陋的不信任的叛逆,使我害怕享受我的愛。

passages.original: There may as well be amity and life ’Tween snow and fire as treason and my love.
passages.vernacular: 雪同火之間都可能有友誼同生命,正如叛逆同我嘅愛之間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雪與火之間也可能有友誼和生命,正如叛逆與我的愛之間。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Ay, but I fear you speak upon the rack Where men enforced do speak anything.
passages.vernacular: 對,不過我怕你係喺拷問架上講話,被逼嘅人乜嘢都講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,可是我怕你是在拷問架上說話,被逼的人什麼都說。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Promise me life, and I’ll confess the truth.
passages.vernacular: 答應畀我活命,我就坦白真相。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 答應給我活命,我就坦白真相。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Well then, confess and live.
passages.vernacular: 好,咁坦白並活命。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,那麼坦白並活命。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: “Confess and love” Had been the very sum of my confession:
passages.vernacular: 「坦白並愛」本係我坦白嘅全部要義:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「坦白並愛」本是我坦白的全部要義:

passages.original: O happy torment, when my torturer Doth teach me answers for deliverance!
passages.vernacular: 啊快樂嘅折磨,當我嘅拷問者教我得救嘅答案!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊快樂的折磨,當我的拷問者教我得救的答案!

passages.original: But let me to my fortune and the caskets.
passages.vernacular: 但讓我去我嘅命運同匣子嗰度吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但讓我去我的命運和匣子那裡吧。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Away, then!
passages.vernacular: 嗰就去吧!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那就去吧!

passages.original: I am lock’d in one of them.
passages.vernacular: 我被鎖喺其中一個裡面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我被鎖在其中一個裡面。

passages.original: If you do love me, you will find me out.
passages.vernacular: 如果你愛我,你會把我找出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你愛我,你會把我找出來。

passages.original: Nerissa and the rest, stand all aloof.
passages.vernacular: 尼莉莎同其餘嘅人,都站遠些。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 尼莉莎和其餘的人,都站遠些。

passages.original: Let music sound while he doth make his choice.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢作選擇時讓音樂奏響。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在他作選擇時讓音樂奏響。

passages.original: Then if he lose he makes a swan-like end, Fading in music.
passages.vernacular: 嗰樣,如果佢輸喇,佢像天鵝一樣結束,喺音樂中消逝。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那樣,如果他輸了,他像天鵝一樣結束,在音樂中消逝。

passages.original: That the comparison May stand more proper, my eye shall be the stream And wat’ry death-bed for him.
passages.vernacular: 為使比喻更恰當,我嘅眼睛將係為佢而設嘅溪流同水上嘅臨終之床。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為使比喻更恰當,我的眼睛將是為他而設的溪流和水上的臨終之床。

passages.original: He may win, And what is music then?
passages.vernacular: 佢或者會贏,嗰時音樂係乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他也許會贏,那時音樂是什麼?

passages.original: Then music is Even as the flourish when true subjects bow To a new-crowned monarch.
passages.vernacular: 嗰時音樂就像真正嘅臣民向新加冕嘅君主鞠躬時嘅號角齊鳴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那時音樂就像真正的臣民向新加冕的君主鞠躬時的號角齊鳴。

passages.original: Such it is As are those dulcet sounds in break of day That creep into the dreaming bridegroom’s ear And summon him to marriage.
passages.vernacular: 就像黎明時分嗰啲甜美嘅聲音,悄悄溜進做夢嘅新郎耳中,召喚佢去結婚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就像黎明時分那些甜美的聲音,悄悄溜進做夢的新郎耳中,召喚他去結婚。

passages.original: Now he goes, With no less presence, but with much more love Than young Alcides when he did redeem The virgin tribute paid by howling Troy To the sea-monster:
passages.vernacular: 而家佢去喇,風度不遜,卻愛得更深,勝過年輕嘅赫拉克勒斯當初贖回嚎哭嘅特洛伊獻畀海怪嘅處女貢品:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在他去了,風度不遜,卻愛得更深,勝過年輕的赫拉克勒斯當初贖回嚎哭的特洛伊獻給海怪的處女貢品:

passages.original: I stand for sacrifice; The rest aloof are the Dardanian wives, With bleared visages come forth to view The issue of th’ exploit.
passages.vernacular: 我站著作為祭品;其餘站遠嘅係達耳達尼亞嘅婦人,淚眼模糊地走出嚟,睇呢壯舉嘅結果。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我站著作為祭品;其餘站遠的是達耳達尼亞的婦人,淚眼模糊地走出來,看這壯舉的結果。

passages.original: Go, Hercules!
passages.vernacular: 去吧,赫拉克勒斯!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去吧,赫拉克勒斯!

passages.original: Live thou, I live.
passages.vernacular: 你活,我就活。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你活,我就活。

passages.original: With much much more dismay I view the fight than thou that mak’st the fray.
passages.vernacular: 我睇呢場戰鬥,比你呢製造戰鬥嘅人驚恐得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看這場戰鬥,比你這製造戰鬥的人驚恐得多。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: A song, whilst Bassanio comments on the caskets to himself.
passages.vernacular: 歌聲響起,同時巴薩尼奧獨自對匣子評論。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 歌聲響起,同時巴薩尼奧獨自對匣子評論。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Tell me where is fancy bred, Or in the heart or in the head?
passages.vernacular: 告訴我愛慕生於何處,係喺心裡定係喺頭裡?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 告訴我愛慕生於何處,是在心裡還是在頭裡?

passages.original: How begot, how nourished?
passages.vernacular: 如何生成,如何滋養?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如何生成,如何滋養?

passages.original: Reply, reply.
passages.vernacular: 回答,回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 回答,回答。

passages.original: It is engend’red in the eyes, With gazing fed, and fancy dies In the cradle where it lies.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺眼睛中孕育,靠凝視餵養,愛慕就喺佢躺住嘅搖籃中死去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它在眼睛中孕育,靠凝視餵養,愛慕就在它躺著的搖籃中死去。

passages.original: Let us all ring fancy’s knell: I’ll begin it.—Ding, dong, bell.
passages.vernacular: 讓我哋都為愛慕敲喪鐘:我嚟開頭。——叮,咚,鐘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我們都為愛慕敲喪鐘:我來開頭。——叮,咚,鐘。

passages.title: All 眾人
passages.original: Ding, dong, bell.
passages.vernacular: 叮,咚,鐘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叮,咚,鐘。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: So may the outward shows be least themselves.
passages.vernacular: 所以外表可能最不像本身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以外表可能最不像本身。

passages.original: The world is still deceiv’d with ornament.
passages.vernacular: 世界總是被裝飾所欺騙。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 世界總是被裝飾所欺騙。

passages.original: In law, what plea so tainted and corrupt But, being season’d with a gracious voice, Obscures the show of evil?
passages.vernacular: 喺法律上,乜嘢辯詞咁樣汙穢腐敗,只要用優美嘅聲音調味,就唔能夠掩蓋邪惡嘅外表?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在法律上,什麼辯詞這樣汙穢腐敗,只要用優美的聲音調味,就不能掩蓋邪惡的外表?

passages.original: In religion, What damned error but some sober brow Will bless it, and approve it with a text, Hiding the grossness with fair ornament?
passages.vernacular: 喺宗教上,乜嘢該死嘅謬誤,唔係某位嚴肅嘅臉孔祝福佢,並用經文贊同佢,用漂亮嘅裝飾掩蓋其粗劣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在宗教上,什麼該死的謬誤,不是某位嚴肅的臉孔祝福它,並用經文贊同它,用漂亮的裝飾掩蓋其粗劣?

passages.original: There is no vice so simple but assumes Some mark of virtue on his outward parts.
passages.vernacular: 冇一種惡習簡單到不喺外表上披上某種美德嘅標記。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有一種惡習簡單到不在外表上披上某種美德的標記。

passages.original: How many cowards, whose hearts are all as false As stairs of sand, wear yet upon their chins The beards of Hercules and frowning Mars, Who inward search’d, have livers white as milk, And these assume but valour’s excrement To render them redoubted.
passages.vernacular: 多少懦夫,佢哋嘅心像沙梯一樣虛假,下巴上卻戴住赫拉克勒斯同皺眉嘅馬爾斯嘅鬍子,內裡一查,肝臟白如奶,佢哋卻只係借勇敢嘅排泄物嚟使自己令人畏懼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 多少懦夫,他們的心像沙梯一樣虛假,下巴上卻戴著赫拉克勒斯和皺眉的馬爾斯的鬍子,內裡一查,肝臟白如奶,他們卻只是借勇敢的排泄物來使自己令人畏懼。

passages.original: Look on beauty, And you shall see ’tis purchas’d by the weight, Which therein works a miracle in nature, Making them lightest that wear most of it:
passages.vernacular: 睇睇美貌,你會睇到佢係按重量買嚟嘅,呢喺其中造成自然嘅奇蹟,戴得最多嘅人最輕:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看看美貌,你會看到它是按重量買來的,這在其中造成自然的奇蹟,戴得最多的人最輕:

passages.original: So are those crisped snaky golden locks Which make such wanton gambols with the wind Upon supposed fairness, often known To be the dowry of a second head, The skull that bred them in the sepulchre.
passages.vernacular: 嗰啲捲曲如蛇嘅金色髮絲都係如此,佢哋喺風中咁放蕩地嬉戲,喺所謂嘅美麗上,常被知道係第二個頭嘅嫁妝,就係喺墳墓中生出佢哋嘅頭骨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那些捲曲如蛇的金色髮絲也是如此,它們在風中那麼放蕩地嬉戲,在所謂的美麗上,常被知道是第二個頭的嫁妝,就是在墳墓中生出它們的頭骨。

passages.original: Thus ornament is but the guiled shore To a most dangerous sea;
passages.vernacular: 咁樣裝飾只係一個通向最危險大海嘅誘人海岸;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這樣裝飾只是一個通向最危險大海的誘人海岸;

passages.original: the beauteous scarf Veiling an Indian beauty;
passages.vernacular: 美麗嘅面紗遮住一個印度美人;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 美麗的面紗遮住一個印度美人;

passages.original: in a word, The seeming truth which cunning times put on To entrap the wisest.
passages.vernacular: 總之,係狡猾嘅時代披上嘅表面真理,嚟誘捕最聰明嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 總之,是狡猾的時代披上的表面真理,來誘捕最聰明的人。

passages.original: Therefore thou gaudy gold, Hard food for Midas, I will none of thee, Nor none of thee, thou pale and common drudge ’Tween man and man:
passages.vernacular: 所以你,金光閃閃嘅金子,米達斯嘅硬食,我唔好你,都唔好你,你呢蒼白嘅人同人之間嘅普通苦力:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以你,金光閃閃的金子,米達斯的硬食,我不要你,也不要你,你這蒼白的人與人之間的普通苦力:

passages.original: but thou, thou meagre lead, Which rather threaten’st than dost promise aught, Thy palenness moves me more than eloquence, And here choose I, joy be the consequence!
passages.vernacular: 而你,你呢瘦削嘅鉛,你同其承諾乜嘢不如講喺威脅,你嘅蒼白比雄辯更打動我,我就喺呢度選擇,願歡樂係結果!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而你,你這瘦削的鉛,你與其承諾什麼不如說在威脅,你的蒼白比雄辯更打動我,我就在這裡選擇,願歡樂是結果!

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: [Aside.]
passages.vernacular: [旁白。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [旁白。]

passages.original: How all the other passions fleet to air, As doubtful thoughts, and rash-embrac’d despair, And shudd’ring fear, and green-ey’d jealousy.
passages.vernacular: 其他一切激情係點樣化為空氣,像疑慮嘅念頭、魯莽擁抱嘅絕望、顫抖嘅恐懼、綠眼嘅嫉妒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其他一切激情是怎樣化為空氣,像疑慮的念頭、魯莽擁抱的絕望、顫抖的恐懼、綠眼的嫉妒。

passages.original: O love, be moderate; allay thy ecstasy, In measure rain thy joy; scant this excess!
passages.vernacular: 啊愛,請你節制;平息你嘅狂喜,適度地降下你嘅歡樂;減少呢過度!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊愛,請你節制;平息你的狂喜,適度地降下你的歡樂;減少這過度!

passages.original: I feel too much thy blessing, make it less, For fear I surfeit.
passages.vernacular: 我感受到你嘅祝福太多,讓佢少啲,免得我撐壞喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我感受到你的祝福太多,讓它少一些,免得我撐壞了。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: What find I here?
passages.vernacular: 我喺呢度發現咗乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在這裡發現了什麼?

passages.original: [Opening the leaden casket.]
passages.vernacular: [打開鉛匣。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [打開鉛匣。]

passages.original: Fair Portia’s counterfeit!
passages.vernacular: 美麗鮑西婭嘅肖像!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 美麗鮑西婭的肖像!

passages.original: What demi-god Hath come so near creation?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢半神咁樣接近創造?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼半神這樣接近創造?

passages.original: Move these eyes?
passages.vernacular: 呢雙眼睛會動嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這雙眼睛會動嗎?

passages.original: Or whether, riding on the balls of mine, Seem they in motion?
passages.vernacular: 定係騎喺我眼球上,睇起嚟喺動?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還是騎在我眼球上,看起來在動?

passages.original: Here are sever’d lips, Parted with sugar breath, so sweet a bar Should sunder such sweet friends.
passages.vernacular: 呢度有分開嘅嘴唇,吐住糖般嘅氣息,咁甜嘅屏障應該分開咁甜嘅朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡有分開的嘴唇,吐著糖般的氣息,這麼甜的屏障應該分開這麼甜的朋友。

passages.original: Here in her hairs The painter plays the spider, and hath woven A golden mesh t’entrap the hearts of men Faster than gnats in cobwebs.
passages.vernacular: 喺佢嘅頭髮裡,畫家扮演蜘蛛,織咗一張金網,捕捉人嘅心,比蚊蟲落喺蛛網上仲牢固。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在她的頭髮裡,畫家扮演蜘蛛,織了一張金網,捕捉人的心,比蚊蟲落在蛛網上還牢固。

passages.original: But her eyes!— How could he see to do them?
passages.vernacular: 但佢嘅眼睛!佢點睇得見去畫佢哋?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但她的眼睛!他怎麼看得見去畫它們?

passages.original: Having made one, Methinks it should have power to steal both his And leave itself unfurnish’d.
passages.vernacular: 畫成一隻後,我想佢應有力量偷走佢嘅雙眼,而使自己無從裝備。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 畫成一隻後,我想它應有力量偷走他的雙眼,而使自己無從裝備。

passages.original: Yet look how far The substance of my praise doth wrong this shadow In underprizing it, so far this shadow Doth limp behind the substance.
passages.vernacular: 然而睇,我讚美嘅實質喺多大程度上冤枉咗呢影子,低估咗佢,呢影子就喺多大程度上落後於實質。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而看,我讚美的實質在多大程度上冤枉了這影子,低估了它,這影子就在多大程度上落後於實質。

passages.original: Here’s the scroll, The continent and summary of my fortune.
passages.vernacular: 呢度係卷軸,我嘅命運嘅內容同摘要。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡是卷軸,我的命運的內容和摘要。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: You that choose not by the view Chance as fair and choose as true!
passages.vernacular: 你哋不憑外觀選擇,機運佳,選擇真!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們不憑外觀選擇,機運佳,選擇真!

passages.original: Since this fortune falls to you, Be content and seek no new.
passages.vernacular: 既然呢個運氣落到你,就請滿足,唔好再另尋新嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 既然這個運氣落到你,就請滿足,不要再另尋新的。

passages.original: If you be well pleas’d with this, And hold your fortune for your bliss, Turn to where your lady is, And claim her with a loving kiss.
passages.vernacular: 如果你對此滿意,並視你嘅運氣為幸福,就轉向你嘅小姐所在之處,用愛嘅一吻向佢認領。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你對此滿意,並視你的運氣為幸福,就轉向你的小姐所在之處,用愛的一吻向她認領。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: A gentle scroll.
passages.vernacular: 溫和嘅卷軸。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 溫和的卷軸。

passages.original: Fair lady, by your leave, [Kissing her.]
passages.vernacular: 美麗嘅小姐,恕我失禮,[吻佢。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: 美麗的小姐,恕我失禮,[吻她。]

passages.original: I come by note to give and to receive.
passages.vernacular: 我係按條文嚟畀予同領受嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是按條文來給予和領受的。

passages.original: Like one of two contending in a prize That thinks he hath done well in people’s eyes, Hearing applause and universal shout, Giddy in spirit, still gazing in a doubt Whether those peals of praise be his or no, So, thrice-fair lady, stand I even so, As doubtful whether what I see be true, Until confirm’d, sign’d, ratified by you.
passages.vernacular: 像兩個爭奪獎品嘅人之一,自認喺人哋眼中做得好,聽到掌聲同普遍嘅歡呼,精神暈眩,仍喺懷疑地凝望,唔知嗰陣陣讚美係咪屬於佢,三倍美麗嘅小姐,我都係如此站住,懷疑我所見嘅係咪真實,直到你確認、簽署、批准。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 像兩個爭奪獎品的人之一,自認在人們眼中做得好,聽到掌聲和普遍的歡呼,精神暈眩,仍在懷疑地凝望,不知那陣陣讚美是否屬於他,三倍美麗的小姐,我也是如此站著,懷疑我所見的是否真實,直到你確認、簽署、批准。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: You see me, Lord Bassanio, where I stand, Such as I am;
passages.vernacular: 你睇我,巴薩尼奧大人,我站喺呢度,就係我呢個樣子;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你看我,巴薩尼奧大人,我站在這裡,就是我這個樣子;

passages.original: though for myself alone I would not be ambitious in my wish To wish myself much better, yet for you I would be trebled twenty times myself, A thousand times more fair, ten thousand times More rich, That only to stand high in your account, I might in virtues, beauties, livings, friends, Exceed account.
passages.vernacular: 雖然為了我自己,我唔會野心勃勃地希望自己好得多,但為了你,我願比自己高二十倍,美一千倍,富一萬倍,只為喺你嘅賬上站得高,我願喺美德、美貌、產業、朋友上都超過計算。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 雖然為了我自己,我不會野心勃勃地希望自己好得多,但為了你,我願比自己高二十倍,美一千倍,富一萬倍,只為在你的賬上站得高,我願在美德、美貌、產業、朋友上都超過計算。

passages.original: But the full sum of me Is sum of something, which, to term in gross, Is an unlesson’d girl, unschool’d, unpractis’d;
passages.vernacular: 但我嘅全部總同,籠統地講,係個冇受過教導、冇上過學、冇經驗嘅女孩;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我的全部總和,籠統地說,是個沒受過教導、沒上過學、沒有經驗的女孩;

passages.original: Happy in this, she is not yet so old But she may learn;
passages.vernacular: 幸運嘅係,佢仲不太老,仍可學習;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 幸運的是,她還不太老,仍可學習;

passages.original: happier than this, She is not bred so dull but she can learn;
passages.vernacular: 更幸運嘅係,佢天生不太遲鈍,佢能學;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 更幸運的是,她天生不太遲鈍,她能學;

passages.original: Happiest of all, is that her gentle spirit Commits itself to yours to be directed, As from her lord, her governor, her king.
passages.vernacular: 最幸運嘅係,佢溫順嘅靈魂把自己託付畀你指引,就像交畀佢嘅夫君、佢嘅主人、佢嘅君王。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最幸運的是,她溫順的靈魂把自己託付給你指引,就像交給她的夫君、她的主人、她的君王。

passages.original: Myself, and what is mine, to you and yours Is now converted.
passages.vernacular: 我自己,同我所有嘅,而家都轉到你同你嘅名下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我自己,和我所有的,現在都轉到你和你的名下。

passages.original: But now I was the lord Of this fair mansion, master of my servants, Queen o’er myself;
passages.vernacular: 頭先我定係呢座美麗宅邸嘅主人、僕人嘅主人、自己嘅女王;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 剛才我還是這座美麗宅邸的主人、僕人的主人、自己的女王;

passages.original: and even now, but now, This house, these servants, and this same myself Are yours,—my lord’s.
passages.vernacular: 而就喺而家,就喺此刻,呢房子、呢啲僕人,同我自己,都係你嘅,——我嘅夫君嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而就在現在,就在此刻,這房子、這些僕人,和我自己,都是你的,——我的夫君的。

passages.original: I give them with this ring, Which when you part from, lose, or give away, Let it presage the ruin of your love, And be my vantage to exclaim on you.
passages.vernacular: 我把佢哋連同呢枚戒指一起畀你,你若同佢分離、丟失或送人,就讓佢預示你愛情嘅毀滅,並畀我責怪你嘅理由。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我把它們連同這枚戒指一起給你,你若與它分離、丟失或送人,就讓它預示你愛情的毀滅,並給我責怪你的理由。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Madam, you have bereft me of all words, Only my blood speaks to you in my veins, And there is such confusion in my powers As after some oration fairly spoke By a beloved prince, there doth appear Among the buzzing pleased multitude, Where every something being blent together, Turns to a wild of nothing, save of joy Express’d and not express’d.
passages.vernacular: 小姐,你奪走咗我所有嘅話,只有我血管中嘅血喺對你講話,我嘅力量咁樣混亂,就像一位受愛戴嘅君王發表咗一場精彩演講之後,喺嗡嗡作響嘅滿意人群中顯現嘅嗰樣,每啲混喺一起,變成一片荒野般嘅空白,除咗歡樂,講出嘅同講不出嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小姐,你奪走了我所有的話,只有我血管中的血在對你說話,我的力量這樣混亂,就像一位受愛戴的君王發表了一場精彩演說之後,在嗡嗡作響的滿意人群中顯現的那樣,每一點混在一起,變成一片荒野般的空白,除了歡樂,說出的和說不出的。

passages.original: But when this ring Parts from this finger, then parts life from hence.
passages.vernacular: 但當呢枚戒指離開呢根手指,生命都就離開呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但當這枚戒指離開這根手指,生命也就離開這裡。

passages.original: O then be bold to say Bassanio’s dead!
passages.vernacular: 啊嗰時就大膽地講巴薩尼奧死喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊那時就大膽地說巴薩尼奧死了!

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: My lord and lady, it is now our time, That have stood by and seen our wishes prosper, To cry, good joy.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅大人同夫人,而家輪到我哋,嗰啲站喺一旁睇住我哋嘅願望成功嘅人,喊一聲:祝福。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的大人和夫人,現在輪到我們,那些站在一旁看著我們的願望成功的人,喊一聲:祝福。

passages.original: Good joy, my lord and lady!
passages.vernacular: 祝福,我嘅大人同夫人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 祝福,我的大人和夫人!

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: My Lord Bassanio, and my gentle lady, I wish you all the joy that you can wish;
passages.vernacular: 巴薩尼奧大人,同我溫柔嘅夫人,我祝你哋能祝願嘅一切歡樂;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴薩尼奧大人,和我溫柔的夫人,我祝你們能祝願的一切歡樂;

passages.original: For I am sure you can wish none from me.
passages.vernacular: 因為我確信你哋唔會從我呢度祝願到任何歡樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為我確信你們不會從我這裡祝願到任何歡樂。

passages.original: And when your honours mean to solemnize The bargain of your faith, I do beseech you Even at that time I may be married too.
passages.vernacular: 當兩位大人打算舉行你哋信誓嘅婚禮時,我懇求就喺嗰時都讓我結婚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當兩位大人打算舉行你們信誓的婚禮時,我懇求就在那時也讓我結婚。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: With all my heart, so thou canst get a wife.
passages.vernacular: 衷心同意,只要你能找到妻子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 衷心同意,只要你能找到妻子。

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: I thank your lordship, you have got me one.
passages.vernacular: 感謝大人,您畀咗我一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 感謝大人,您給了我一個。

passages.original: My eyes, my lord, can look as swift as yours:
passages.vernacular: 我嘅眼睛,大人,能睇得同您嘅一樣快:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的眼睛,大人,能看得和您的一樣快:

passages.original: You saw the mistress, I beheld the maid.
passages.vernacular: 您睇見咗小姐,我睇見咗侍女。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您看見了小姐,我看見了侍女。

passages.original: You lov’d, I lov’d; for intermission No more pertains to me, my lord, than you.
passages.vernacular: 您愛,我愛;因為中斷同我無關,大人,同您無異。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您愛,我愛;因為中斷與我無關,大人,與您無異。

passages.original: Your fortune stood upon the caskets there, And so did mine too, as the matter falls.
passages.vernacular: 您嘅命運取決於嗰邊嘅匣子,我嘅都一樣,事情就係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您的命運取決於那邊的匣子,我的也一樣,事情就是這樣。

passages.original: For wooing here until I sweat again, And swearing till my very roof was dry With oaths of love, at last, (if promise last) I got a promise of this fair one here To have her love, provided that your fortune Achiev’d her mistress.
passages.vernacular: 因為喺呢度求愛直到汗流浹背,發誓直到屋頂都被愛嘅誓言晾乾,最後(如果承諾能持久),我得到咗呢位美人嘅承諾,獲得佢嘅愛,條件係你嘅運氣能贏得佢嘅小姐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為在這裡求愛直到汗流浹背,發誓直到屋頂都被愛的誓言晾乾,最後(如果承諾能持久),我得到了這位美人的承諾,獲得她的愛,條件是你的運氣能贏得她的小姐。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Is this true, Nerissa?
passages.vernacular: 呢個係真嘅嗎,尼莉莎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是真的嗎,尼莉莎?

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: Madam, it is, so you stand pleas’d withal.
passages.vernacular: 小姐,係嘅,只要您滿意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 小姐,是的,只要您滿意。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: And do you, Gratiano, mean good faith?
passages.vernacular: 葛拉蒂安諾,你係真心嘅嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 葛拉蒂安諾,你是真心的嗎?

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: Yes, faith, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 係,講真嘅,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是,說真的,大人。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Our feast shall be much honoured in your marriage.
passages.vernacular: 我哋嘅宴席因你哋嘅婚姻將大增光彩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們的宴席因你們的婚姻將大增光彩。

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: We’ll play with them the first boy for a thousand ducats.
passages.vernacular: 我哋同佢哋賭第一個生男孩,賭一千杜卡特。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們與他們賭第一個生男孩,賭一千杜卡特。

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: What!
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼!

passages.original: and stake down?
passages.vernacular: 而且係先下注?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且是先下注?

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: No, we shall ne’er win at that sport and stake down.
passages.vernacular: 不,先下注我哋永遠贏不咗呢個遊戲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,先下注我們永遠贏不了這個遊戲。

passages.original: But who comes here?
passages.vernacular: 但邊個嚟喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但誰來了?

passages.original: Lorenzo and his infidel?
passages.vernacular: 羅倫佐同佢嘅異教徒?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅倫佐和他的異教徒?

passages.original: What, and my old Venetian friend, Salerio!
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,仲有我嘅老威尼斯朋友,薩雷里奧!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,還有我的老威尼斯朋友,薩雷里奧!

passages.original: Enter Lorenzo, Jessica and Salerio.
passages.vernacular: [羅倫佐、潔西卡同薩雷里奧上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [羅倫佐、潔西卡與薩雷里奧上。]

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Lorenzo and Salerio, welcome hither, If that the youth of my new int’rest here Have power to bid you welcome.
passages.vernacular: 羅倫佐同薩雷里奧,歡迎嚟呢度,如果我喺呢度新獲得嘅權益,有資格講歡迎嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅倫佐和薩雷里奧,歡迎來這裡,如果我在這裡新獲得的權益,有資格說歡迎的話。

passages.original: By your leave, I bid my very friends and countrymen, Sweet Portia, welcome.
passages.vernacular: 恕我失禮,我邀請我真正嘅朋友同同胞,親愛嘅鮑西婭,歡迎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 恕我失禮,我邀請我真正的朋友和同胞,親愛的鮑西婭,歡迎。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: So do I, my lord, They are entirely welcome.
passages.vernacular: 我都咁樣,大人,佢哋完全受歡迎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也這樣,大人,他們完全受歡迎。

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: I thank your honour.
passages.vernacular: 感謝大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 感謝大人。

passages.original: For my part, my lord, My purpose was not to have seen you here, But meeting with Salerio by the way, He did entreat me, past all saying nay, To come with him along.
passages.vernacular: 至於我,大人,我本冇打算喺呢度見您,但喺路上遇到薩雷里奧,佢懇求我,唔容拒絕,同佢一同嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至於我,大人,我本沒打算在這裡見您,但在路上遇到薩雷里奧,他懇求我,不容拒絕,和他一同來。

passages.title: Salerio 薩雷里奧
passages.original: I did, my lord, And I have reason for it.
passages.vernacular: 我確實咁樣,大人,而且我有理由。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我確實這樣,大人,而且我有理由。

passages.original: Signior Antonio Commends him to you.
passages.vernacular: 安東尼奧先生向您致意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安東尼奧先生向您致意。

passages.original: [Gives Bassanio a letter.]
passages.vernacular: [把一封信交畀巴薩尼奧。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [把一封信交給巴薩尼奧。]

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Ere I ope his letter, I pray you tell me how my good friend doth.
passages.vernacular: 喺我拆開佢嘅信之前,請告訴我我嘅好朋友點樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在我拆開他的信之前,請告訴我我的好朋友怎樣。

passages.title: Salerio 薩雷里奧
passages.original: Not sick, my lord, unless it be in mind, Nor well, unless in mind.
passages.vernacular: 冇生病,大人,除非係喺心裡,都不算好,除非喺心裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有生病,大人,除非是在心裡,也不算好,除非在心裡。

passages.original: His letter there Will show you his estate.
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅信喺嗰度會向您顯示佢嘅處境。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的信在那裡會向您顯示他的處境。

passages.original: [Bassanio opens the letter.]
passages.vernacular: [巴薩尼奧拆開信。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [巴薩尼奧拆開信。]

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: Nerissa, cheer yond stranger, bid her welcome.
passages.vernacular: 尼莉莎,招待嗰位陌生人,歡迎佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 尼莉莎,招待那位陌生人,歡迎她。

passages.original: Your hand, Salerio.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅手,薩雷里奧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的手,薩雷里奧。

passages.original: What’s the news from Venice?
passages.vernacular: 威尼斯有乜嘢消息?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 威尼斯有什麼消息?

passages.original: How doth that royal merchant, good Antonio?
passages.vernacular: 嗰位皇家商人,好安東尼奧,點樣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那位皇家商人,好安東尼奧,怎樣?

passages.original: I know he will be glad of our success.
passages.vernacular: 我知道佢會為我哋嘅成功高興。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道他會為我們的成功高興。

passages.original: We are the Jasons, we have won the fleece.
passages.vernacular: 我哋係伊阿宋,我哋贏得咗金羊毛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們是伊阿宋,我們贏得了金羊毛。

passages.title: Salerio 薩雷里奧
passages.original: I would you had won the fleece that he hath lost.
passages.vernacular: 但願你哋贏得咗佢失去嘅羊毛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但願你們贏得了他失去的羊毛。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: There are some shrewd contents in yond same paper That steals the colour from Bassanio’s cheek.
passages.vernacular: 嗰張紙上有些嚴重嘅內容,使巴薩尼奧臉頰失去咗血色。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那張紙上有些嚴重的內容,使巴薩尼奧臉頰失去了血色。

passages.original: Some dear friend dead, else nothing in the world Could turn so much the constitution Of any constant man.
passages.vernacular: 除咗某個親愛嘅朋友死喇,世上冇別嘅能咁樣改變一個堅定嘅人嘅體質。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除了某個親愛的朋友死了,世上沒有別的能這樣改變一個堅定的人的體質。

passages.original: What, worse and worse?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,越嚟越糟?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,越來越糟?

passages.original: With leave, Bassanio, I am half yourself, And I must freely have the half of anything That this same paper brings you.
passages.vernacular: 失禮喇,巴薩尼奧,我係你嘅一半,凡呢張紙畀你帶嚟嘅,我必須自由地分得一半。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 失禮了,巴薩尼奧,我是你的一半,凡這張紙給你帶來的,我必須自由地分得一半。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: O sweet Portia, Here are a few of the unpleasant’st words That ever blotted paper.
passages.vernacular: 啊親愛嘅鮑西婭,呢度有幾句曾沾污紙張嘅最不愉快嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊親愛的鮑西婭,這裡有幾句曾沾污紙張的最不愉快的話。

passages.original: Gentle lady, When I did first impart my love to you, I freely told you all the wealth I had Ran in my veins, I was a gentleman.
passages.vernacular: 溫柔嘅小姐,當我第一次向你吐露我嘅愛時,我坦率地告訴你,我所有嘅財富都喺我血管裡流住,我係個紳士。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 溫柔的小姐,當我第一次向你吐露我的愛時,我坦率地告訴你,我所有的財富都在我血管裡流著,我是個紳士。

passages.original: And then I told you true.
passages.vernacular: 嗰時我告訴你嘅係真話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那時我告訴你的是真話。

passages.original: And yet, dear lady, Rating myself at nothing, you shall see How much I was a braggart.
passages.vernacular: 然而,親愛嘅小姐,把我自己估成零,你將睇到我幾咁係個吹牛者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然而,親愛的小姐,把我自己估成零,你將看到我多麼是個吹牛者。

passages.original: When I told you My state was nothing, I should then have told you That I was worse than nothing;
passages.vernacular: 當我告訴你我嘅家境係零時,我嗰時本該告訴你我比零仲糟;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當我告訴你我的家境是零時,我那時本該告訴你我比零還糟;

passages.original: for indeed I have engag’d myself to a dear friend, Engag’d my friend to his mere enemy, To feed my means.
passages.vernacular: 因為確實我把自己抵押畀一位好朋友,又把我嘅朋友抵押畀佢嘅死敵,嚟供養我嘅財力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為確實我把自己抵押給一位好朋友,又把我的朋友抵押給他的死敵,來供養我的財力。

passages.original: Here is a letter, lady, The paper as the body of my friend, And every word in it a gaping wound Issuing life-blood.
passages.vernacular: 呢度有一封信,小姐,嗰張紙就像我朋友嘅身體,上面每一個字都係裂開嘅傷口,流出生命嘅血。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡有一封信,小姐,那張紙就像我朋友的身體,上面每一個字都是裂開的傷口,流出生命的血。

passages.original: But is it true, Salerio?
passages.vernacular: 但呢個係真嘅嗎,薩雷里奧?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但這是真的嗎,薩雷里奧?

passages.original: Hath all his ventures fail’d?
passages.vernacular: 佢所有嘅冒險都失敗咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他所有的冒險都失敗了嗎?

passages.original: What, not one hit?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,一個都冇成功?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,一個都沒有成功?

passages.original: From Tripolis, from Mexico, and England, From Lisbon, Barbary, and India, And not one vessel scape the dreadful touch Of merchant-marring rocks?
passages.vernacular: 從嘅黎波里、墨西哥、英國,從里斯本、巴巴里同印度,冇一條船逃過摧毀商人嘅礁石嘅可怕觸碰?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 從的黎波里、墨西哥、英國,從里斯本、巴巴里和印度,沒有一條船逃過摧毀商人的礁石的可怕觸碰?

passages.title: Salerio 薩雷里奧
passages.original: Not one, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 一條都冇,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一條也沒有,大人。

passages.original: Besides, it should appear, that if he had The present money to discharge the Jew, He would not take it.
passages.vernacular: 此外,睇來,即使佢有現成嘅錢可以還畀猶太人,猶太人都唔肯收。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 此外,看來,即使他有現成的錢可以還給猶太人,猶太人也不肯收。

passages.original: Never did I know A creature that did bear the shape of man So keen and greedy to confound a man.
passages.vernacular: 我從冇見過一個長住人形嘅生物,咁樣急切貪婪地要毀滅一個人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從沒見過一個長著人形的生物,這樣急切貪婪地要毀滅一個人。

passages.original: He plies the Duke at morning and at night, And doth impeach the freedom of the state If they deny him justice.
passages.vernacular: 佢早晚逼迫公爵,並指控國家嘅自由,如果佢哋拒絕畀佢正義。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他早晚逼迫公爵,並指控國家的自由,如果他們拒絕給他正義。

passages.original: Twenty merchants, The Duke himself, and the magnificoes Of greatest port have all persuaded with him, But none can drive him from the envious plea Of forfeiture, of justice, and his bond.
passages.vernacular: 二十位商人、公爵本人、同最有地位嘅大人物哋都勸過佢,但冇一個人能使佢放棄嗰嫉恨嘅罰金要求、正義嘅要求同佢嘅契約。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 二十位商人、公爵本人、和最有地位的大人物們都勸過他,但沒有一個人能使他放棄那嫉恨的罰金要求、正義的要求和他的契約。

passages.title: Jessica 潔西卡
passages.original: When I was with him, I have heard him swear To Tubal and to Chus, his countrymen, That he would rather have Antonio’s flesh Than twenty times the value of the sum That he did owe him.
passages.vernacular: 我同佢喺一起時,聽過佢對佢嘅同族圖巴爾同丘斯發誓,佢寧願要安東尼奧嘅肉,都唔好所欠款項嘅二十倍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我和他在一起時,聽過他對他的同族圖巴爾和丘斯發誓,他寧願要安東尼奧的肉,也不要所欠款項的二十倍。

passages.original: And I know, my lord, If law, authority, and power deny not, It will go hard with poor Antonio.
passages.vernacular: 大人,我知道,如果法律、權威同權力不否決,可憐嘅安東尼奧會好難過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,我知道,如果法律、權威和權力不否決,可憐的安東尼奧會很難過。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Is it your dear friend that is thus in trouble?
passages.vernacular: 咁樣陷入麻煩嘅係你嘅好朋友嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這樣陷入麻煩的是你的好朋友嗎?

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: The dearest friend to me, the kindest man, The best condition’d and unwearied spirit In doing courtesies, and one in whom The ancient Roman honour more appears Than any that draws breath in Italy.
passages.vernacular: 對我最親愛嘅朋友,最仁厚嘅人,脾氣最好、行善時最不倦嘅靈魂,喺佢身上古羅馬嘅榮譽,比意大利任何呼吸嘅人更顯現。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對我最親愛的朋友,最仁厚的人,脾氣最好、行善時最不倦的靈魂,在他身上古羅馬的榮譽,比意大利任何呼吸的人更顯現。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: What sum owes he the Jew?
passages.vernacular: 佢欠猶太人多少錢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他欠猶太人多少錢?

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: For me three thousand ducats.
passages.vernacular: 為我三千杜卡特。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為我三千杜卡特。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: What, no more?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,冇更多?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,沒有更多?

passages.original: Pay him six thousand, and deface the bond.
passages.vernacular: 付佢六千,把契約毀掉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 付他六千,把契約毀掉。

passages.original: Double six thousand, and then treble that, Before a friend of this description Shall lose a hair through Bassanio’s fault.
passages.vernacular: 兩個六千,再三倍,都唔能夠讓咁樣嘅朋友因巴薩尼奧嘅過失損失一根頭髮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩個六千,再三倍,也不能讓這樣的朋友因巴薩尼奧的過失損失一根頭髮。

passages.original: First go with me to church and call me wife, And then away to Venice to your friend.
passages.vernacular: 先跟我去教堂,叫我妻子,然後再去威尼斯找你朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先跟我去教堂,叫我妻子,然後再去威尼斯找你朋友。

passages.original: For never shall you lie by Portia’s side With an unquiet soul.
passages.vernacular: 因為你絕不可帶住不安嘅靈魂躺喺鮑西婭身邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為你絕不可帶著不安的靈魂躺在鮑西婭身邊。

passages.original: You shall have gold To pay the petty debt twenty times over.
passages.vernacular: 你將有金子,把呢小債仲二十遍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你將有金子,把這小債還二十遍。

passages.original: When it is paid, bring your true friend along.
passages.vernacular: 付清後,把你嘅真摯朋友帶嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 付清後,把你的真摯朋友帶來。

passages.original: My maid Nerissa and myself meantime, Will live as maids and widows. Come, away!
passages.vernacular: 我嘅侍女尼莉莎同我同時將像少女同寡婦一樣生活。嚟,走!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的侍女尼莉莎和我同時將像少女和寡婦一樣生活。來,走!

passages.original: For you shall hence upon your wedding day.
passages.vernacular: 因為你要喺婚禮之日離開呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為你要在婚禮之日離開這裡。

passages.original: Bid your friends welcome, show a merry cheer;
passages.vernacular: 招待你嘅朋友,顯出快樂嘅神情;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 招待你的朋友,顯出快樂的神情;

passages.original: Since you are dear bought, I will love you dear.
passages.vernacular: 既然你係用高價買嚟嘅,我就會深深地愛你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 既然你是用高價買來的,我就會深深地愛你。

passages.original: But let me hear the letter of your friend.
passages.vernacular: 但讓我聽聽你朋友嘅信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但讓我聽聽你朋友的信。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Sweet Bassanio, my ships have all miscarried, my creditors grow cruel, my estate is very low, my bond to the Jew is forfeit, and since in paying it, it is impossible I should live, all debts are clear’d between you and I, if I might but see you at my death.
passages.vernacular: 「親愛嘅巴薩尼奧,我嘅船都失事喇,我嘅債主變得殘酷,我嘅家境好糟,我對猶太人嘅契約已違約,既然付清佢我唔可能活住,你我之間所有債務一筆勾銷,只要我臨死前能見你一面。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「親愛的巴薩尼奧,我的船都失事了,我的債主變得殘酷,我的家境很糟,我對猶太人的契約已違約,既然付清它我不可能活著,你我之間所有債務一筆勾銷,只要我臨死前能見你一面。

passages.original: Notwithstanding, use your pleasure.
passages.vernacular: 不過,隨你意願。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過,隨你意願。

passages.original: If your love do not persuade you to come, let not my letter.
passages.vernacular: 如果你嘅愛唔能夠講服你嚟,就唔好畀我嘅信講服你。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你的愛不能說服你來,就別讓我的信說服你。」

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: O love, dispatch all business and be gone!
passages.vernacular: 啊愛,快辦完所有事務然後走!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊愛,快辦完所有事務然後走!

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Since I have your good leave to go away, I will make haste;
passages.vernacular: 既然我得到你嘅允許離開,我會加緊;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 既然我得到你的允許離開,我會加緊;

passages.original: but, till I come again, No bed shall e’er be guilty of my stay, Nor rest be interposer ’twixt us twain.
passages.vernacular: 但喺我回嚟之前,冇一張床會因我逗留而有罪,都冇休息會介入我哋兩人之間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但在我回來之前,沒有一張床會因我逗留而有罪,也沒有休息會介入我們兩人之間。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act III, Scene III — Venice. A Street 第三幕第三場:威尼斯街道

passages.original: Enter Shylock, Salarino, Antonio and Gaoler.
passages.vernacular: [夏洛克、薩萊里諾、安東尼奧同獄卒上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [夏洛克、薩萊里諾、安東尼奧與獄卒上。]

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: Gaoler, look to him.
passages.vernacular: 獄卒,睇好佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 獄卒,看好他。

passages.original: Tell not me of mercy.
passages.vernacular: 別對我講憐憫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別對我說憐憫。

passages.original: This is the fool that lent out money gratis.
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係嗰個白白借出錢嘅傻瓜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是那個白白借出錢的傻瓜。

passages.original: Gaoler, look to him.
passages.vernacular: 獄卒,睇好佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 獄卒,看好他。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: Hear me yet, good Shylock.
passages.vernacular: 定係聽我講,好夏洛克。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還是聽我說,好夏洛克。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: I’ll have my bond, speak not against my bond.
passages.vernacular: 我要我嘅契約,別反對我嘅契約。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要我的契約,別反對我的契約。

passages.original: I have sworn an oath that I will have my bond.
passages.vernacular: 我已發誓,我要我嘅契約。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我已發誓,我要我的契約。

passages.original: Thou call’dst me dog before thou hadst a cause, But since I am a dog, beware my fangs;
passages.vernacular: 你喺我有理由之前就叫我狗,但既然我係狗,就當心我嘅尖牙;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你在我有理由之前就叫我狗,但既然我是狗,就當心我的尖牙;

passages.original: The Duke shall grant me justice.
passages.vernacular: 公爵會畀我正義。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 公爵會給我正義。

passages.original: I do wonder, Thou naughty gaoler, that thou art so fond To come abroad with him at his request.
passages.vernacular: 我好奇怪,你呢個壞獄卒,竟咁樣糊塗,應佢嘅請求陪佢出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很奇怪,你這個壞獄卒,竟這樣糊塗,應他的請求陪他出來。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: I pray thee hear me speak.
passages.vernacular: 我請你聽我講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我請你聽我說。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: I’ll have my bond.
passages.vernacular: 我要我嘅契約。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要我的契約。

passages.original: I will not hear thee speak.
passages.vernacular: 我不聽你講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不聽你說。

passages.original: I’ll have my bond, and therefore speak no more.
passages.vernacular: 我要我嘅契約,所以唔好再講喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要我的契約,所以不要再說了。

passages.original: I’ll not be made a soft and dull-eyed fool, To shake the head, relent, and sigh, and yield To Christian intercessors.
passages.vernacular: 我唔會被弄成一個軟弱、眼神呆滯嘅傻瓜,搖頭、心軟、嘆息、屈服於基督徒嘅講情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不會被弄成一個軟弱、眼神呆滯的傻瓜,搖頭、心軟、嘆息、屈服於基督徒的說情。

passages.original: Follow not, I’ll have no speaking, I will have my bond.
passages.vernacular: 唔好跟住我,我唔好講話,我要我嘅契約。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要跟著我,我不要說話,我要我的契約。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Salarino 薩萊里諾
passages.original: It is the most impenetrable cur That ever kept with men.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係最頑固不化嘅狗,曾同人為伍嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是最頑固不化的狗,曾與人為伍的。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: Let him alone.
passages.vernacular: 隨佢去吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 隨他去吧。

passages.original: I’ll follow him no more with bootless prayers.
passages.vernacular: 我再都唔使徒勞嘅懇求跟住佢喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我再也不用徒勞的懇求跟著他了。

passages.original: He seeks my life, his reason well I know: I oft deliver’d from his forfeitures Many that have at times made moan to me.
passages.vernacular: 佢要我嘅命,佢嘅理由我好清楚:我常常從佢嘅罰金中解救許多曾向我訴苦嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他要我的命,他的理由我很清楚:我常常從他的罰金中解救許多曾向我訴苦的人。

passages.original: Therefore he hates me.
passages.vernacular: 所以佢恨我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以他恨我。

passages.title: Salarino 薩萊里諾
passages.original: I am sure the Duke Will never grant this forfeiture to hold.
passages.vernacular: 我確信公爵絕唔會准許呢項罰金成立。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我確信公爵絕不會准許這項罰金成立。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: The Duke cannot deny the course of law, For the commodity that strangers have With us in Venice, if it be denied, ’Twill much impeach the justice of the state, Since that the trade and profit of the city Consisteth of all nations.
passages.vernacular: 公爵唔能夠否定法律嘅程序,因為外邦人喺威尼斯同我哋享有嘅便利,若被否定,就會嚴重指控國家嘅公正,因為呢城市嘅貿易同利益由各國人組成。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 公爵不能否定法律的程序,因為外邦人在威尼斯與我們享有的便利,若被否定,就會嚴重指控國家的公正,因為這城市的貿易和利益由各國人組成。

passages.original: Therefore, go.
passages.vernacular: 所以,去吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以,去吧。

passages.original: These griefs and losses have so bated me That I shall hardly spare a pound of flesh Tomorrow to my bloody creditor.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲悲傷同損失使我消瘦,聽日我恐怕難以畀我嘅血腥債主割下一磅肉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些悲傷和損失使我消瘦,明天我恐怕難以給我的血腥債主割下一磅肉。

passages.original: Well, gaoler, on, pray God Bassanio come To see me pay his debt, and then I care not.
passages.vernacular: 好,獄卒,走吧,但願上帝讓巴薩尼奧嚟,睇我仲清佢嘅債,然後我就無所謂喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,獄卒,走吧,但願上帝讓巴薩尼奧來,看我還清他的債,然後我就無所謂了。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act III, Scene IV — Belmont. A Room in Portia’s House 第三幕第四場:貝爾蒙特,鮑西婭家一室

passages.original: Enter Portia, Nerissa, Lorenzo, Jessica and Balthazar.
passages.vernacular: [鮑西婭、尼莉莎、羅倫佐、潔西卡同巴爾薩澤上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [鮑西婭、尼莉莎、羅倫佐、潔西卡與巴爾薩澤上。]

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: Madam, although I speak it in your presence, You have a noble and a true conceit Of godlike amity, which appears most strongly In bearing thus the absence of your lord.
passages.vernacular: 夫人,雖然我當面講呢話,你對神一般嘅友誼有崇高而真切嘅理解,呢喺你咁樣忍受你夫君嘅缺席時最顯而易見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夫人,雖然我當面說這話,你對神一般的友誼有崇高而真切的理解,這在你這樣忍受你夫君的缺席時最顯而易見。

passages.original: But if you knew to whom you show this honour, How true a gentleman you send relief, How dear a lover of my lord your husband, I know you would be prouder of the work Than customary bounty can enforce you.
passages.vernacular: 但如果你知道你向邊個顯示呢份尊榮,你派去救助嘅係點樣真誠嘅紳士,係我主人你丈夫點樣親愛嘅朋友,我知道你會比平常嘅慷慨所能迫使你嘅,更為呢件事驕傲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但如果你知道你向誰顯示這份尊榮,你派去救助的是怎樣真誠的紳士,是我主人你丈夫怎樣親愛的朋友,我知道你會比平常的慷慨所能迫使你的,更為這件事驕傲。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: I never did repent for doing good, Nor shall not now;
passages.vernacular: 我從未為行善後悔,而家都唔會;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我從未為行善後悔,現在也不會;

passages.original: for in companions That do converse and waste the time together, Whose souls do bear an equal yoke of love, There must be needs a like proportion Of lineaments, of manners, and of spirit;
passages.vernacular: 因為喺嗰啲相處交談、一起消磨時光嘅伴侶之間,佢哋嘅靈魂擔住相等嘅愛嘅軛,必然有相似比例嘅面容、舉止同精神;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為在那些相處交談、一起消磨時光的伴侶之間,他們的靈魂擔著相等的愛的軛,必然有相似比例的面容、舉止和精神;

passages.original: Which makes me think that this Antonio, Being the bosom lover of my lord, Must needs be like my lord.
passages.vernacular: 呢使我想到呢位安東尼奧,既係我夫君嘅知心友人,必然像我夫君。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這使我想到這位安東尼奧,既是我夫君的知心友人,必然像我夫君。

passages.original: If it be so, How little is the cost I have bestowed In purchasing the semblance of my soul From out the state of hellish cruelty!
passages.vernacular: 如果係咁樣,我為了從地獄般殘酷嘅境地救出同我靈魂相似嘅人而花嘅費用係幾咁少!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果是這樣,我為了從地獄般殘酷的境地救出與我靈魂相似的人而花的費用是多麼少!

passages.original: This comes too near the praising of myself; Therefore no more of it.
passages.vernacular: 呢太接近自我稱讚喇;所以唔再講呢個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這太接近自我稱讚了;所以不再說這個。

passages.original: Hear other things.
passages.vernacular: 聽別嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽別的事。

passages.original: Lorenzo, I commit into your hands The husbandry and manage of my house Until my lord’s return.
passages.vernacular: 羅倫佐,我把我家嘅管理同經營託付喺你手裡,直到我夫君回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅倫佐,我把我家的管理與經營託付在你手裡,直到我夫君回來。

passages.original: For mine own part, I have toward heaven breath’d a secret vow To live in prayer and contemplation, Only attended by Nerissa here, Until her husband and my lord’s return.
passages.vernacular: 至於我自己,我已向天暗暗發咗誓,要喺祈禱同默想中生活,只有呢度嘅尼莉莎陪伴,直到佢丈夫同我夫君回嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至於我自己,我已向天暗暗發了誓,要在祈禱和默想中生活,只有這裡的尼莉莎陪伴,直到她丈夫和我夫君回來。

passages.original: There is a monastery two miles off, And there we will abide.
passages.vernacular: 兩英里外有一座修道院,我哋將住喺嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩英里外有一座修道院,我們將住在那裡。

passages.original: I do desire you Not to deny this imposition, The which my love and some necessity Now lays upon you.
passages.vernacular: 我希望你唔好拒絕呢個託付,佢係我嘅愛同某種需要而家加喺你身上嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望你不要拒絕這個託付,它是我的愛和某種需要現在加在你身上的。

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: Madam, with all my heart I shall obey you in all fair commands.
passages.vernacular: 夫人,我衷心樂意喺一切正當嘅命令上服從你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夫人,我衷心樂意在一切正當的命令上服從你。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: My people do already know my mind, And will acknowledge you and Jessica In place of Lord Bassanio and myself.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅人已知道我嘅心意,會承認你同潔西卡代替巴薩尼奧大人同我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的人已知道我的心意,會承認你和潔西卡代替巴薩尼奧大人和我。

passages.original: So fare you well till we shall meet again.
passages.vernacular: 咁再會,直到我哋再見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼再會,直到我們再見。

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: Fair thoughts and happy hours attend on you!
passages.vernacular: 願美好嘅思想同快樂嘅時光伴隨你哋!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願美好的思想與快樂的時光伴隨你們!

passages.title: Jessica 潔西卡
passages.original: I wish your ladyship all heart’s content.
passages.vernacular: 我祝夫人您一切稱心如意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我祝夫人您一切稱心如意。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: I thank you for your wish, and am well pleas’d To wish it back on you.
passages.vernacular: 我感謝你嘅祝願,並樂意把佢回祝畀你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我感謝你的祝願,並樂意把它回祝給你。

passages.original: Fare you well, Jessica.
passages.vernacular: 再會,潔西卡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再會,潔西卡。

passages.original: [Exeunt Jessica and Lorenzo.]
passages.vernacular: [潔西卡同羅倫佐下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [潔西卡與羅倫佐下。]

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Now, Balthazar, As I have ever found thee honest-true, So let me find thee still.
passages.vernacular: 而家,巴爾薩澤,正如我一向發現你誠實可靠,就讓我繼續咁樣發現你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,巴爾薩澤,正如我一向發現你誠實可靠,就讓我繼續這樣發現你。

passages.original: Take this same letter, And use thou all th’ endeavour of a man In speed to Padua, see thou render this Into my cousin’s hands, Doctor Bellario;
passages.vernacular: 攞住呢封信,盡一個人所有嘅努力,火速趕往帕多瓦,務必把佢交到我表兄手裡,貝拉里奧博士;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿著這封信,盡一個人所有的努力,火速趕往帕多瓦,務必把它交到我表兄手裡,貝拉里奧博士;

passages.original: And look what notes and garments he doth give thee, Bring them, I pray thee, with imagin’d speed Unto the traject, to the common ferry Which trades to Venice.
passages.vernacular: 佢畀你乜嘢筆記同衣服,你要想像中嘅快速帶到渡口,到往嚟威尼斯嘅公共渡船嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他給你什麼筆記和衣服,你要想像中的快速帶到渡口,到往來威尼斯的公共渡船那裡。

passages.original: Waste no time in words, But get thee gone.
passages.vernacular: 別浪費時間講話,走吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別浪費時間說話,走吧。

passages.original: I shall be there before thee.
passages.vernacular: 我會比你先到嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會比你先到那裡。

passages.title: Balthazar 巴爾薩澤
passages.original: Madam, I go with all convenient speed.
passages.vernacular: 夫人,我以一切方便嘅速度前往。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夫人,我以一切方便的速度前往。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Come on, Nerissa, I have work in hand That you yet know not of;
passages.vernacular: 嚟吧,尼莉莎,我有一件你仲唔知道嘅事要做;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來吧,尼莉莎,我有一件你還不知道的事要做;

passages.original: we’ll see our husbands Before they think of us.
passages.vernacular: 我哋要喺我哋嘅丈夫想到我哋之前見到佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們要在我們的丈夫想到我們之前見到他們。

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: Shall they see us?
passages.vernacular: 佢哋會睇到我哋嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們會看到我們嗎?

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: They shall, Nerissa, but in such a habit That they shall think we are accomplished With that we lack.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋會嘅,尼莉莎,但我哋將穿住咁樣嘅服裝,讓佢哋以為我哋具備我哋所缺少嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們會的,尼莉莎,但我們將穿著這樣的服裝,讓他們以為我們具備我們所缺少的。

passages.original: I’ll hold thee any wager, When we are both accoutered like young men, I’ll prove the prettier fellow of the two, And wear my dagger with the braver grace, And speak between the change of man and boy With a reed voice;
passages.vernacular: 我跟你賭任何賭注,當我哋都打扮成年輕人時,我會證明自己係兩人中更俊俏嘅,佩劍更有風度,喺男孩變成男人嘅變聲之間,用蘆笛般嘅嗓音講話;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我跟你賭任何賭注,當我們都打扮成年輕人時,我會證明自己是兩人中更俊俏的,佩劍更有風度,在男孩變成男人的變聲之間,用蘆笛般的嗓音說話;

passages.original: and turn two mincing steps Into a manly stride;
passages.vernacular: 把兩步小碎步變成男子漢大步;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把兩步小碎步變成男子漢大步;

passages.original: and speak of frays Like a fine bragging youth;
passages.vernacular: 像一個漂亮嘅吹牛少年一樣談論爭鬥;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 像一個漂亮的吹牛少年一樣談論爭鬥;

passages.original: and tell quaint lies How honourable ladies sought my love, Which I denying, they fell sick and died; I could not do withal.
passages.vernacular: 編造稀奇嘅謊話,講高貴嘅小姐哋點樣追求我嘅愛,我拒絕喇,佢哋就生病死去;我實在冇辦法。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 編造稀奇的謊話,說高貴的小姐們怎樣追求我的愛,我拒絕了,她們就生病死去;我實在沒辦法。

passages.original: Then I’ll repent, And wish for all that, that I had not kill’d them.
passages.vernacular: 然後我會後悔,並為呢一切希望我冇害死佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後我會後悔,並為這一切希望我沒有害死她們。

passages.original: And twenty of these puny lies I’ll tell, That men shall swear I have discontinued school About a twelvemonth.
passages.vernacular: 我會編二十個咁樣嘅小謊,讓人發誓我已輟學大約一年。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會編二十個這樣的小謊,讓人發誓我已輟學大約一年。

passages.original: I have within my mind A thousand raw tricks of these bragging Jacks, Which I will practise.
passages.vernacular: 我心裡有一千個呢啲吹牛小子嘅生硬把戲,我要實踐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我心裡有一千個這些吹牛小子的生硬把戲,我要實踐。

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: Why, shall we turn to men?
passages.vernacular: 哎,我哋要變成男人嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎,我們要變成男人嗎?

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Fie, what a question’s that, If thou wert near a lewd interpreter!
passages.vernacular: 呸,呢個係乜嘢問題,如果你靠近一個下流嘅解釋者!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 呸,這是什麼問題,如果你靠近一個下流的解釋者!

passages.original: But come, I’ll tell thee all my whole device When I am in my coach, which stays for us At the park gate;
passages.vernacular: 嚟吧,等我坐進喺公園門口等我哋嘅馬車裡,我會告訴你我全部嘅計劃;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來吧,等我坐進在公園門口等我們的馬車裡,我會告訴你我全部的計劃;

passages.original: and therefore haste away, For we must measure twenty miles today.
passages.vernacular: 所以快走,因為我哋今日要走二十英里。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以快走,因為我們今天要走二十英里。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act III, Scene V — A Garden 第三幕第五場:花園

passages.original: Enter Launcelet and Jessica.
passages.vernacular: [朗斯洛特同潔西卡上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [朗斯洛特與潔西卡上。]

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: Yes, truly, for look you, the sins of the father are to be laid upon the children, therefore, I promise you, I fear you.
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,真嘅,你睇,父親嘅罪要加喺細路身上,所以我向你保證,我怕你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,真的,你看,父親的罪要加在孩子身上,所以我向你保證,我怕你。

passages.original: I was always plain with you, and so now I speak my agitation of the matter.
passages.vernacular: 我對你一向直話直講,所以而家我講出我對呢件事嘅憂慮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我對你一向直話直說,所以現在我說出我對這件事的憂慮。

passages.original: Therefore be of good cheer, for truly I think you are damn’d.
passages.vernacular: 所以高興些,因為老實講我想你要被詛咒喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以高興些,因為老實說我想你要被詛咒了。

passages.original: There is but one hope in it that can do you any good, and that is but a kind of bastard hope neither.
passages.vernacular: 其中只有一個希望能對你有點好處,而且嗰都只係一種私生子嘅希望。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 其中只有一個希望能對你有點好處,而且那也只是一種私生子的希望。

passages.title: Jessica 潔西卡
passages.original: And what hope is that, I pray thee?
passages.vernacular: 請問嗰個係乜嘢希望?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請問那是什麼希望?

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: Marry, you may partly hope that your father got you not, that you are not the Jew’s daughter.
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅,你可以部分地希望你父親冇生你,你唔係猶太人嘅女兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的,你可以部分地希望你父親沒有生你,你不是猶太人的女兒。

passages.title: Jessica 潔西卡
passages.original: That were a kind of bastard hope indeed; so the sins of my mother should be visited upon me.
passages.vernacular: 嗰確實係一種私生子嘅希望;咁樣我母親嘅罪就要報應喺我身上喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那確實是一種私生子的希望;這樣我母親的罪就要報應在我身上了。

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: Truly then I fear you are damn’d both by father and mother;
passages.vernacular: 咁講真嘅,我怕你被父親同母親雙雙詛咒;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼說真的,我怕你被父親和母親雙雙詛咒;

passages.original: thus when I shun Scylla your father, I fall into Charybdis your mother.
passages.vernacular: 咁樣當我躲開斯庫拉你父親時,我就落入卡律布狄斯你母親。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這樣當我躲開斯庫拉你父親時,我就落入卡律布狄斯你母親。

passages.original: Well, you are gone both ways.
passages.vernacular: 好,你兩邊都完喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,你兩邊都完了。

passages.title: Jessica 潔西卡
passages.original: I shall be saved by my husband.
passages.vernacular: 我將被我丈夫拯救。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我將被我丈夫拯救。

passages.original: He hath made me a Christian.
passages.vernacular: 佢使我成為基督徒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他使我成為基督徒。

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: Truly the more to blame he, we were Christians enow before, e’en as many as could well live one by another.
passages.vernacular: 講真嘅佢更該受責備,我哋以前嘅基督徒已經夠多喇,正好夠彼此相處過日子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說真的他更該受責備,我們以前的基督徒已經夠多了,正好夠彼此相處過日子。

passages.original: This making of Christians will raise the price of hogs;
passages.vernacular: 咁樣造基督徒會提高豬肉嘅價格;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這樣造基督徒會提高豬肉的價格;

passages.original: if we grow all to be pork-eaters, we shall not shortly have a rasher on the coals for money.
passages.vernacular: 如果我哋全都食豬肉,不久我哋就冇一片肉能花錢放到炭火上烤。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我們全都吃豬肉,不久我們就沒有一片肉能花錢放到炭火上烤。

passages.original: Enter Lorenzo.
passages.vernacular: [羅倫佐上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [羅倫佐上。]

passages.title: Jessica 潔西卡
passages.original: I’ll tell my husband, Launcelet, what you say.
passages.vernacular: 朗斯洛特,我要把你講嘅告訴我丈夫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 朗斯洛特,我要把你說的告訴我丈夫。

passages.original: Here he comes.
passages.vernacular: 佢嚟喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他來了。

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: I shall grow jealous of you shortly, Launcelet, if you thus get my wife into corners!
passages.vernacular: 朗斯洛特,如果你咁樣把我妻子拉到角落裡,我不久就要對你食醋喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 朗斯洛特,如果你這樣把我妻子拉到角落裡,我不久就要對你吃醋了!

passages.title: Jessica 潔西卡
passages.original: Nay, you need not fear us, Lorenzo.
passages.vernacular: 不,你唔使怕我哋,羅倫佐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,你不必怕我們,羅倫佐。

passages.original: Launcelet and I are out.
passages.vernacular: 朗斯洛特同我鬧翻喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 朗斯洛特和我鬧翻了。

passages.original: He tells me flatly there’s no mercy for me in heaven, because I am a Jew’s daughter;
passages.vernacular: 佢直白地告訴我,天上冇憐憫畀我,因為我係猶太人嘅女兒;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他直白地告訴我,天上沒有憐憫給我,因為我是猶太人的女兒;

passages.original: and he says you are no good member of the commonwealth, for in converting Jews to Christians you raise the price of pork.
passages.vernacular: 佢講你唔係國家嘅好成員,因為你把猶太人變成基督徒,抬高咗豬肉嘅價格。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他說你不是國家的好成員,因為你把猶太人變成基督徒,抬高了豬肉的價格。

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: I shall answer that better to the commonwealth than you can the getting up of the negro’s belly!
passages.vernacular: 我向國家交代呢個,會比你交代使嗰黑人肚子大起嚟更好!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我向國家交代這個,會比你交代使那黑人肚子大起來更好!

passages.original: The Moor is with child by you, Launcelet.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個摩爾女人被你搞大咗肚子,朗斯洛特。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那個摩爾女人被你搞大了肚子,朗斯洛特。

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: It is much that the Moor should be more than reason;
passages.vernacular: 摩爾女人比理性所容許嘅仲多,呢個係常有嘅事;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 摩爾女人比理性所容許的還多,這是常有的事;

passages.original: but if she be less than an honest woman, she is indeed more than I took her for.
passages.vernacular: 但如果佢唔係個誠實嘅女人,嗰佢確實比我所以為嘅仲多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但如果她不是個誠實的女人,那她確實比我所以為的還多。

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: How every fool can play upon the word!
passages.vernacular: 每個傻瓜點都能玩弄字眼!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每個傻瓜怎麼都能玩弄字眼!

passages.original: I think the best grace of wit will shortly turn into silence, and discourse grow commendable in none only but parrots.
passages.vernacular: 我想最好嘅機智風度不久就要變成沉默,而言談只有鸚鵡才值得稱讚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想最好的機智風度不久就要變成沉默,而言談只有鸚鵡才值得稱讚。

passages.original: Go in, sirrah; bid them prepare for dinner.
passages.vernacular: 進去,小子;叫佢哋準備晚飯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 進去,小子;叫他們準備晚飯。

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: That is done, sir, they have all stomachs.
passages.vernacular: 已經做好喇,先生,佢哋都有胃口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 已經做好了,先生,他們都有胃口。

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: Goodly Lord, what a wit-snapper are you!
passages.vernacular: 好主啊,你真係個口舌尖利嘅人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好主啊,你真是個口舌尖利的人!

passages.original: Then bid them prepare dinner.
passages.vernacular: 嗰就叫佢哋準備晚飯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那就叫他們準備晚飯。

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: That is done too, sir, only “cover” is the word.
passages.vernacular: 呢都做好喇,先生,只係「蓋上」呢個詞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這也做好了,先生,只是「蓋上」這個詞。

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: Will you cover, then, sir?
passages.vernacular: 嗰你要蓋上嗎,先生?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那你要蓋上嗎,先生?

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: Not so, sir, neither.
passages.vernacular: 都唔係,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也不是,先生。

passages.original: I know my duty.
passages.vernacular: 我知道我嘅本分。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我知道我的本分。

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: Yet more quarrelling with occasion!
passages.vernacular: 又攞場合嚟吵!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 又拿場合來吵!

passages.original: Wilt thou show the whole wealth of thy wit in an instant?
passages.vernacular: 你要一下子展示你全部嘅機智財富嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你要一下子展示你全部的機智財富嗎?

passages.original: I pray thee understand a plain man in his plain meaning:
passages.vernacular: 請你明白一個直人嘅直意:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你明白一個直人的直意:

passages.original: go to thy fellows, bid them cover the table, serve in the meat, and we will come in to dinner.
passages.vernacular: 去你嘅同伴嗰度,叫佢哋蓋桌(擺桌),端上肉,我哋就進嚟食晚飯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去你的同伴那裡,叫他們蓋桌(擺桌),端上肉,我們就進來吃晚飯。

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: For the table, sir, it shall be served in; for the meat, sir, it shall be covered;
passages.vernacular: 講到桌子,先生,佢會被端上;講到肉,先生,佢會被蓋上;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說到桌子,先生,它會被端上;說到肉,先生,它會被蓋上;

passages.original: for your coming in to dinner, sir, why, let it be as humours and conceits shall govern.
passages.vernacular: 講到您進嚟食晚飯,先生,哎,就讓佢由情緒同心思決定。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說到您進來吃晚飯,先生,哎,就讓它由情緒和心思決定。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: O dear discretion, how his words are suited!
passages.vernacular: 啊親愛嘅審慎,佢嘅話配得多巧!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊親愛的審慎,他的話配得多巧!

passages.original: The fool hath planted in his memory An army of good words, and I do know A many fools that stand in better place, Garnish’d like him, that for a tricksy word Defy the matter.
passages.vernacular: 呢傻瓜喺記憶裡種咗一支好詞嘅軍隊,我知道許多地位更好嘅傻瓜,都像佢一樣打扮,為一個狡猾嘅詞而不顧事理。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這傻瓜在記憶裡種了一支好詞的軍隊,我知道許多地位更好的傻瓜,也像他一樣打扮,為一個狡猾的詞而不顧事理。

passages.original: How cheer’st thou, Jessica?
passages.vernacular: 你點樣,潔西卡?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你怎麼樣,潔西卡?

passages.original: And now, good sweet, say thy opinion, How dost thou like the Lord Bassanio’s wife?
passages.vernacular: 而家,好親愛嘅,講講你嘅意見,你覺得巴薩尼奧大人嘅妻子點樣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,好親愛的,說說你的意見,你覺得巴薩尼奧大人的妻子怎樣?

passages.title: Jessica 潔西卡
passages.original: Past all expressing.
passages.vernacular: 無法形容。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 無法形容。

passages.original: It is very meet The Lord Bassanio live an upright life, For having such a blessing in his lady, He finds the joys of heaven here on earth, And if on earth he do not merit it, In reason he should never come to heaven.
passages.vernacular: 巴薩尼奧大人理應過正直嘅生活,因為有咁樣嘅福氣喺佢夫人身上,佢喺人間找到天堂嘅歡樂,如果佢喺人間配不上,按理佢永遠上不咗天堂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴薩尼奧大人理應過正直的生活,因為有這樣的福氣在他夫人身上,他在人間找到天堂的歡樂,如果他在人間配不上,按理他永遠上不了天堂。

passages.original: Why, if two gods should play some heavenly match, And on the wager lay two earthly women, And Portia one, there must be something else Pawn’d with the other, for the poor rude world Hath not her fellow.
passages.vernacular: 哎,如果兩位神要下一場天上嘅賭局,把兩個人間女人作賭注,其中一個係鮑西婭,咁另一個必須押上別嘅嘢,因為可憐粗魯嘅世界冇佢嘅同類。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎,如果兩位神要下一場天上的賭局,把兩個人間女人作賭注,其中一個是鮑西婭,那麼另一個必須押上別的東西,因為可憐粗魯的世界沒有她的同類。

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: Even such a husband Hast thou of me as she is for a wife.
passages.vernacular: 你從我呢度得到嘅丈夫,正像佢作為妻子一樣好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你從我這裡得到的丈夫,正像她作為妻子一樣好。

passages.title: Jessica 潔西卡
passages.original: Nay, but ask my opinion too of that.
passages.vernacular: 不,都問問我對此嘅意見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,也問問我對此的意見。

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: I will anon.
passages.vernacular: 我即刻問。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我馬上問。

passages.original: First let us go to dinner.
passages.vernacular: 先去食飯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先去吃飯。

passages.title: Jessica 潔西卡
passages.original: Nay, let me praise you while I have a stomach.
passages.vernacular: 不,讓我趁我有胃口時讚美你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,讓我趁我有胃口時讚美你。

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: No pray thee, let it serve for table-talk.
passages.vernacular: 不,請你,留作餐桌上嘅談話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,請你,留作餐桌上的談話。

passages.original: Then howsome’er thou speak’st, ’mong other things I shall digest it.
passages.vernacular: 咁無論你點講,我都會連同其他嘢一起消化佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼無論你怎麼說,我都會連同其他東西一起消化它。

passages.title: Jessica 潔西卡
passages.original: Well, I’ll set you forth.
passages.vernacular: 好,我嚟誇你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,我來誇你。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act IV, Scene I — Venice. A Court of Justice 第四幕第一場:威尼斯法庭

passages.original: Enter the Duke, the Magnificoes, Antonio, Bassanio, Gratiano, Salerio and others.
passages.vernacular: [公爵、顯貴哋、安東尼奧、巴薩尼奧、葛拉蒂安諾、薩雷里奧及其他人上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [公爵、顯貴們、安東尼奧、巴薩尼奧、葛拉蒂安諾、薩雷里奧及其他人上。]

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: What, is Antonio here?
passages.vernacular: 點,安東尼奧喺呢度嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼,安東尼奧在這裡嗎?

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: Ready, so please your Grace.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢度,請公爵大人吩咐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這裡,請公爵大人吩咐。

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: I am sorry for thee, thou art come to answer A stony adversary, an inhuman wretch, Uncapable of pity, void and empty From any dram of mercy.
passages.vernacular: 我為你難過,你嚟回答嘅係一個鐵石般嘅對手,一個無人性嘅可憐蟲,唔能夠憐憫,冇一分一毫嘅慈悲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我為你難過,你來回答的是一個鐵石般的對手,一個無人性的可憐蟲,不能憐憫,沒有一分一毫的慈悲。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: I have heard Your Grace hath ta’en great pains to qualify His rigorous course;
passages.vernacular: 我聽講大人費咗好大力氣去緩和佢嘅嚴酷做法;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽說大人費了很大力氣去緩和他的嚴酷做法;

passages.original: but since he stands obdurate, And that no lawful means can carry me Out of his envy’s reach, I do oppose My patience to his fury, and am arm’d To suffer with a quietness of spirit The very tyranny and rage of his.
passages.vernacular: 但既然佢頑固不化,而且冇任何合法手段能把我帶出佢怨恨嘅範圍,我就以我嘅耐心對抗佢嘅狂怒,並武裝自己,以平靜嘅心靈承受佢嘅暴虐同憤怒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但既然他頑固不化,而且沒有任何合法手段能把我帶出他怨恨的範圍,我就以我的耐心對抗他的狂怒,並武裝自己,以平靜的心靈承受他的暴虐和憤怒。

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: Go one and call the Jew into the court.
passages.vernacular: 派個人去把猶太人叫到法庭嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 派個人去把猶太人叫到法庭來。

passages.title: Salarino 薩萊里諾
passages.original: He is ready at the door.
passages.vernacular: 佢已喺門口候住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他已在門口候著。

passages.original: He comes, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 佢嚟喇,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他來了,大人。

passages.original: Enter Shylock.
passages.vernacular: [夏洛克上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [夏洛克上。]

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: Make room, and let him stand before our face.
passages.vernacular: 讓開地方,讓佢站喺我哋面前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓開地方,讓他站在我們面前。

passages.original: Shylock, the world thinks, and I think so too, That thou but leadest this fashion of thy malice To the last hour of act, and then, ’tis thought, Thou’lt show thy mercy and remorse more strange Than is thy strange apparent cruelty;
passages.vernacular: 夏洛克,世人咁樣想,我都咁樣想,你只係把你惡意嘅呢種表演帶到行動嘅最後一刻,然後,人哋以為,你會顯示出比你奇怪嘅明顯殘忍更奇怪嘅憐憫同悔恨;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夏洛克,世人這樣想,我也這樣想,你只是把你惡意的這種表演帶到行動的最後一刻,然後,人們以為,你會顯示出比你奇怪的明顯殘忍更奇怪的憐憫和悔恨;

passages.original: And where thou now exacts the penalty, Which is a pound of this poor merchant’s flesh, Thou wilt not only loose the forfeiture, But, touch’d with human gentleness and love, Forgive a moiety of the principal, Glancing an eye of pity on his losses That have of late so huddled on his back, Enow to press a royal merchant down, And pluck commiseration of his state From brassy bosoms and rough hearts of flint, From stubborn Turks and Tartars never train’d To offices of tender courtesy.
passages.vernacular: 而你而家索取嘅罰金,係呢可憐商人身上嘅一磅肉,你不僅會放棄呢罰金,而且被人性嘅溫柔和愛所觸動,寬免一半本金,對佢近來堆喺背上嘅損失投以憐憫嘅一瞥,嗰啲損失足以壓垮一位皇家商人,並從銅鑄嘅胸膛同燧石般嘅硬心、從從未受過溫柔禮貌訓練嘅頑固土耳其人同韃靼人嗰度,激起對佢處境嘅同情。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而你現在索取的罰金,是這可憐商人身上的一磅肉,你不僅會放棄這罰金,而且被人性的溫柔和愛所觸動,寬免一半本金,對他近來堆在背上的損失投以憐憫的一瞥,那些損失足以壓垮一位皇家商人,並從銅鑄的胸膛和燧石般的硬心、從從未受過溫柔禮貌訓練的頑固土耳其人和韃靼人那裡,激起對他處境的同情。

passages.original: We all expect a gentle answer, Jew.
passages.vernacular: 我哋都期待一個溫和嘅答覆,猶太人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們都期待一個溫和的答覆,猶太人。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: I have possess’d your Grace of what I purpose, And by our holy Sabbath have I sworn To have the due and forfeit of my bond.
passages.vernacular: 我已向大人稟明我嘅意圖,並憑我哋神聖嘅安息日發誓,要得到我契約上應得嘅罰金。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我已向大人稟明我的意圖,並憑我們神聖的安息日發誓,要得到我契約上應得的罰金。

passages.original: If you deny it, let the danger light Upon your charter and your city’s freedom!
passages.vernacular: 如果你哋否決,就讓危險落喺你哋嘅特許狀同你哋城市嘅自由上!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你們否決,就讓危險落在你們的特許狀和你們城市的自由上!

passages.original: You’ll ask me why I rather choose to have A weight of carrion flesh than to receive Three thousand ducats.
passages.vernacular: 你哋會問我點解寧願要一磅腐肉,都唔好三千杜卡特。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們會問我為什麼寧願要一磅腐肉,也不要三千杜卡特。

passages.original: I’ll not answer that, But say it is my humour.
passages.vernacular: 我不回答呢個,只講呢個係我嘅脾氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不回答這個,只說這是我的脾氣。

passages.original: Is it answer’d?
passages.vernacular: 呢回答咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這回答了嗎?

passages.original: What if my house be troubled with a rat, And I be pleas’d to give ten thousand ducats To have it ban’d?
passages.vernacular: 如果我嘅房子被老鼠困擾,我樂意付一萬杜卡特把佢毒死呢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我的房子被老鼠困擾,我樂意付一萬杜卡特把它毒死呢?

passages.original: What, are you answer’d yet?
passages.vernacular: 點,你哋得到答覆咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼,你們得到答覆了嗎?

passages.original: Some men there are love not a gaping pig; Some that are mad if they behold a cat;
passages.vernacular: 有些人不愛張口嘅豬;有些人見到貓就發瘋;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有些人不愛張口的豬;有些人見到貓就發瘋;

passages.original: And others, when the bagpipe sings i’ the nose, Cannot contain their urine;
passages.vernacular: 仲有些人,聽到風笛從鼻子裡唱歌,就忍不住尿;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有些人,聽到風笛從鼻子裡唱歌,就忍不住尿;

passages.original: for affection Mistress of passion, sways it to the mood Of what it likes or loathes.
passages.vernacular: 因為感情,激情嘅主人,按佢所喜或所惡,支配激情嘅情緒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為感情,激情的主人,按它所喜或所惡,支配激情的情緒。

passages.original: Now, for your answer: As there is no firm reason to be render’d Why he cannot abide a gaping pig, Why he a harmless necessary cat, Why he a woollen bagpipe, but of force Must yield to such inevitable shame As to offend, himself being offended, So can I give no reason, nor I will not, More than a lodg’d hate and a certain loathing I bear Antonio, that I follow thus A losing suit against him.
passages.vernacular: 而家,關於你哋嘅回答:既然冇確定嘅理由可以畀出,點解佢受不了張口嘅豬,點解佢受不了無害而有用嘅貓,點解佢受不了羊毛風笛,而必然屈服於咁樣不可避免嘅羞辱,以致喺自己被冒犯時冒犯別人,同樣,我都無法畀出理由,都唔願畀,只有我對安東尼奧懷有嘅根深蒂固嘅恨同某種厭惡,所以我咁樣對佢提起一場註定失敗嘅訴訟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,關於你們的回答:既然沒有確定的理由可以給出,為什麼他受不了張口的豬,為什麼他受不了無害而有用的貓,為什麼他受不了羊毛風笛,而必然屈服於這樣不可避免的羞辱,以致在自己被冒犯時冒犯別人,同樣,我也無法給出理由,也不願給,只有我對安東尼奧懷有的根深蒂固的恨和某種厭惡,所以我這樣對他提起一場註定失敗的訴訟。

passages.original: Are you answered?
passages.vernacular: 你哋得到答覆咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們得到答覆了嗎?

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: This is no answer, thou unfeeling man, To excuse the current of thy cruelty.
passages.vernacular: 呢唔係答覆,你呢無情嘅人,唔能夠為你殘忍嘅潮流作辯解。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不是答覆,你這無情的人,不能為你殘忍的潮流作辯解。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: I am not bound to please thee with my answer.
passages.vernacular: 我冇義務用我嘅回答取悅你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沒有義務用我的回答取悅你。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Do all men kill the things they do not love?
passages.vernacular: 係唔係所有人都殺佢哋不愛嘅嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是不是所有人都殺他們不愛的東西?

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: Hates any man the thing he would not kill?
passages.vernacular: 有人會恨佢唔想殺嘅嘢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有人會恨他不想殺的東西嗎?

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Every offence is not a hate at first.
passages.vernacular: 每一次冒犯起初並不都係恨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 每一次冒犯起初並不都是恨。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: What, wouldst thou have a serpent sting thee twice?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,你想要毒蛇咬你兩次嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,你想要毒蛇咬你兩次嗎?

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: I pray you, think you question with the Jew.
passages.vernacular: 請你想想你係喺同猶太人辯論。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你想想你是在同猶太人辯論。

passages.original: You may as well go stand upon the beach And bid the main flood bate his usual height;
passages.vernacular: 你不妨去站喺海灘上,命令大潮降低佢平常嘅高度;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不妨去站在海灘上,命令大潮降低它平常的高度;

passages.original: You may as well use question with the wolf, Why he hath made the ewe bleat for the lamb;
passages.vernacular: 你不妨跟狼辯論,點解讓母羊為羔羊咩叫;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不妨跟狼辯論,為什麼讓母羊為羔羊咩叫;

passages.original: You may as well forbid the mountain pines To wag their high tops and to make no noise When they are fretten with the gusts of heaven;
passages.vernacular: 你不妨禁止山上嘅松樹,喺天上嘅狂風吹打佢哋時,不搖動佢哋高高嘅樹梢、不發出聲響;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不妨禁止山上的松樹,在天上的狂風吹打它們時,不搖動它們高高的樹梢、不發出聲響;

passages.original: You may as well do anything most hard As seek to soften that—than which what’s harder?— His Jewish heart.
passages.vernacular: 你不妨做任何最難嘅事,比如試圖軟化嗰——仲有乜嘢比嗰更硬嘅?——佢猶太人嘅心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不妨做任何最難的事,比如試圖軟化那——還有什麼比那更硬的?——他猶太人的心。

passages.original: Therefore, I do beseech you, Make no moe offers, use no farther means, But with all brief and plain conveniency.
passages.vernacular: 所以,我懇求你哋,唔好再提出條件,唔好再用任何手段,只要簡短、直截咗當地辦。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以,我懇求你們,不要再提出條件,不要再用任何手段,只要簡短、直截了當地辦。

passages.original: Let me have judgment, and the Jew his will.
passages.vernacular: 讓我得到判決,讓猶太人如願。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我得到判決,讓猶太人如願。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: For thy three thousand ducats here is six.
passages.vernacular: 為了你嘅三千杜卡特,呢度係六千。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了你的三千杜卡特,這裡是六千。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: If every ducat in six thousand ducats Were in six parts, and every part a ducat, I would not draw them, I would have my bond.
passages.vernacular: 如果六千杜卡特裡每一個杜卡特都分成六份,每份都係一個杜卡特,我都不收,我只要我嘅契約。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果六千杜卡特裡每一個杜卡特都分成六份,每份都是一個杜卡特,我也不收,我只要我的契約。

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: How shalt thou hope for mercy, rend’ring none?
passages.vernacular: 你不施憐憫,怎能指望得到憐憫?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不施憐憫,怎能指望得到憐憫?

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: What judgment shall I dread, doing no wrong?
passages.vernacular: 我不做錯事,有乜嘢判決可怕?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不做錯事,有什麼判決可怕?

passages.original: You have among you many a purchas’d slave, Which, like your asses and your dogs and mules, You use in abject and in slavish parts, Because you bought them.
passages.vernacular: 你哋中間有許多買嚟嘅奴隸,你哋像對待驢、狗同騾子一樣,讓佢哋做卑賤、奴隸般嘅活,因為你哋買咗佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們中間有許多買來的奴隸,你們像對待驢、狗和騾子一樣,讓他們做卑賤、奴隸般的活,因為你們買了他們。

passages.original: Shall I say to you “Let them be free, marry them to your heirs?
passages.vernacular: 我該對你哋講:「讓佢哋自由,把佢哋嫁畀你哋嘅繼承人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我該對你們說:「讓他們自由,把他們嫁給你們的繼承人?

passages.original: Why sweat they under burdens?
passages.vernacular: 點解讓佢哋喺重擔下流汗?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為什麼讓他們在重擔下流汗?

passages.original: Let their beds Be made as soft as yours, and let their palates Be season’d with such viands”?
passages.vernacular: 讓佢哋嘅床鋪得像你哋嘅一樣軟,讓佢哋嘅口味用同樣嘅佳餚調味」嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓他們的床鋪得像你們的一樣軟,讓他們的口味用同樣的佳餚調味」嗎?

passages.original: You will answer “The slaves are ours.”
passages.vernacular: 你哋會回答:「奴隸係我哋嘅。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們會回答:「奴隸是我們的。」

passages.original: So do I answer you: The pound of flesh which I demand of him Is dearly bought;
passages.vernacular: 我都咁樣回答你哋:我向佢索取嘅嗰一磅肉係用高價買嚟嘅;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也這樣回答你們:我向他索取的那一磅肉是用高價買來的;

passages.original: ’tis mine and I will have it.
passages.vernacular: 佢係我嘅,我要得到佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它是我的,我要得到它。

passages.original: If you deny me, fie upon your law!
passages.vernacular: 如果你哋拒絕我,呸你哋嘅法律!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你們拒絕我,呸你們的法律!

passages.original: There is no force in the decrees of Venice.
passages.vernacular: 威尼斯嘅法令冇任何力量。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 威尼斯的法令沒有任何力量。

passages.original: I stand for judgment.
passages.vernacular: 我等待判決。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我等待判決。

passages.original: Answer; shall I have it?
passages.vernacular: 回答;我能得到嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 回答;我能得到嗎?

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: Upon my power I may dismiss this court, Unless Bellario, a learned doctor, Whom I have sent for to determine this, Come here today.
passages.vernacular: 憑我嘅權力,我可以解散呢個法庭,除非我派人去請嚟決定此案嘅貝拉里奧博士今日到達。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑我的權力,我可以解散這個法庭,除非我派人去請來決定此案的貝拉里奧博士今天到達。

passages.title: Salarino 薩萊里諾
passages.original: My lord, here stays without A messenger with letters from the doctor, New come from Padua.
passages.vernacular: 大人,外面有一位信使等住,帶住博士嘅信,剛從帕多瓦嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,外面有一位信使等著,帶著博士的信,剛從帕多瓦來。

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: Bring us the letters.
passages.vernacular: 把信攞嚟畀我哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把信拿來給我們。

passages.original: Call the messenger.
passages.vernacular: 叫信使進嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 叫信使進來。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Good cheer, Antonio!
passages.vernacular: 振作,安東尼奧!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 振作,安東尼奧!

passages.original: What, man, courage yet!
passages.vernacular: 點,老兄,仲要有勇氣!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼,老兄,還要有勇氣!

passages.original: The Jew shall have my flesh, blood, bones, and all, Ere thou shalt lose for me one drop of blood.
passages.vernacular: 猶太人可以得到我嘅肉、血、骨頭同一切,都唔能夠讓你為我失去一滴血。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 猶太人可以得到我的肉、血、骨頭和一切,也不能讓你為我失去一滴血。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: I am a tainted wether of the flock, Meetest for death, the weakest kind of fruit Drops earliest to the ground, and so let me.
passages.vernacular: 我係羊群中一隻有病嘅閹羊,最適合死亡,最軟弱嘅果子最早落地,就讓我咁樣吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是羊群中一隻有病的閹羊,最適合死亡,最軟弱的果子最早落地,就讓我這樣吧。
