passages.original: You cannot better be employ’d, Bassanio, Than to live still, and write mine epitaph.
passages.vernacular: 你最好嘅用處,巴薩尼奧,就係繼續活住,為我寫墓誌銘。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你最好的用處,巴薩尼奧,就是繼續活著,為我寫墓誌銘。

passages.original: Enter Nerissa dressed like a lawyer’s clerk.
passages.vernacular: [尼莉莎扮作律師嘅書記上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [尼莉莎扮作律師的書記上。]

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: Came you from Padua, from Bellario?
passages.vernacular: 你係從帕多瓦,從貝拉里奧嗰度嚟嘅嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是從帕多瓦,從貝拉里奧那裡來的嗎?

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: From both, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 兩處都係,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 兩處都是,大人。

passages.original: Bellario greets your Grace.
passages.vernacular: 貝拉里奧向大人致意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貝拉里奧向大人致意。

passages.original: [Presents a letter.]
passages.vernacular: [呈上一封信。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [呈上一封信。]

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Why dost thou whet thy knife so earnestly?
passages.vernacular: 你點解咁樣熱切地磨你嘅刀?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為什麼這樣熱切地磨你的刀?

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: To cut the forfeiture from that bankrupt there.
passages.vernacular: 為了從嗰邊嗰個破產者身上割下罰金。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了從那邊那個破產者身上割下罰金。

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: Not on thy sole but on thy soul, harsh Jew, Thou mak’st thy knife keen.
passages.vernacular: 你磨利你嘅刀,唔係磨喺鞋底上,而係磨喺你嘅靈魂上,冷酷嘅猶太人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你磨利你的刀,不是磨在鞋底上,而是磨在你的靈魂上,冷酷的猶太人。

passages.original: But no metal can, No, not the hangman’s axe, bear half the keenness Of thy sharp envy.
passages.vernacular: 但冇任何金屬,連劊子手嘅斧頭都唔能夠,承受你尖銳怨恨嘅一半鋒利。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但沒有任何金屬,連劊子手的斧頭也不能,承受你尖銳怨恨的一半鋒利。

passages.original: Can no prayers pierce thee?
passages.vernacular: 難道冇祈禱能刺穿你嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 難道沒有祈禱能刺穿你嗎?

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: No, none that thou hast wit enough to make.
passages.vernacular: 冇,冇你能想出嚟嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有,沒有你能想出來的。

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: O, be thou damn’d, inexecrable dog!
passages.vernacular: 啊,該詛咒你,你呢可憎嘅狗!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,該詛咒你,你這可憎的狗!

passages.original: And for thy life let justice be accus’d; Thou almost mak’st me waver in my faith, To hold opinion with Pythagoras That souls of animals infuse themselves Into the trunks of men.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅生命該使正義受控訴;你幾乎使我動搖信仰,去同意畢達哥拉斯嘅睇法,認為動物嘅靈魂會注入人嘅軀幹。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的生命該使正義受控訴;你幾乎使我動搖信仰,去同意畢達哥拉斯的看法,認為動物的靈魂會注入人的軀幹。

passages.original: Thy currish spirit Govern’d a wolf who, hang’d for human slaughter, Even from the gallows did his fell soul fleet, And whilst thou layest in thy unhallowed dam, Infus’d itself in thee;
passages.vernacular: 你狗一樣嘅靈魂曾支配一隻狼,嗰狼因殺人被吊死,從絞架上把佢兇殘嘅靈魂逃出,而當你躺喺你不神聖嘅母親子宮裡時,佢注入咗你;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你狗一樣的靈魂曾支配一隻狼,那狼因殺人被吊死,從絞架上把它兇殘的靈魂逃出,而當你躺在你不神聖的母親子宮裡時,它注入了你;

passages.original: for thy desires Are wolfish, bloody, starv’d and ravenous.
passages.vernacular: 因為你嘅慾望係狼一樣嘅、嗜血嘅、飢餓而貪婪嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為你的慾望是狼一樣的、嗜血的、飢餓而貪婪的。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: Till thou canst rail the seal from off my bond, Thou but offend’st thy lungs to speak so loud.
passages.vernacular: 除非你能用叫罵把我契約上嘅封印罵掉,否則你咁樣大聲講話,只係傷咗你嘅肺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除非你能用叫罵把我契約上的封印罵掉,否則你這樣大聲說話,只是傷了你的肺。

passages.original: Repair thy wit, good youth, or it will fall To cureless ruin.
passages.vernacular: 修補你嘅智慧吧,好青年,否則佢要落入無藥可救嘅毀滅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 修補你的智慧吧,好青年,否則它要落入無藥可救的毀滅。

passages.original: I stand here for law.
passages.vernacular: 我喺呢度堅持嘅係法律。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在這裡堅持的是法律。

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: This letter from Bellario doth commend A young and learned doctor to our court.
passages.vernacular: 貝拉里奧嘅呢封信向我哋法庭推薦一位年輕博學嘅博士。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 貝拉里奧的這封信向我們法庭推薦一位年輕博學的博士。

passages.original: Where is he?
passages.vernacular: 佢喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他在哪裡?

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: He attendeth here hard by, To know your answer, whether you’ll admit him.
passages.vernacular: 佢就喺附近等住,想知道您嘅答覆,係咪准許佢進嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他就在附近等著,想知道您的答覆,是否准許他進來。

passages.title: Duke of Venice 威尼斯公爵
passages.original: With all my heart: some three or four of you Go give him courteous conduct to this place.
passages.vernacular: 衷心准許:你哋三四個人去,禮貌地引佢到呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 衷心准許:你們三四個人去,禮貌地引他到這裡。

passages.original: Meantime, the court shall hear Bellario’s letter.
passages.vernacular: 同時,法庭將聽貝拉里奧嘅信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 同時,法庭將聽貝拉里奧的信。

passages.original: [Reads.] Your Grace shall understand that at the receipt of your letter I am very sick, but in the instant that your messenger came, in loving visitation was with me a young doctor of Rome. His name is Balthazar. I acquainted him with the cause in controversy between the Jew and Antonio the merchant. We turn’d o’er many books together. He is furnished with my opinion, which, bettered with his own learning (the greatness whereof I cannot enough commend), comes with him at my importunity to fill up your Grace’s request in my stead. I beseech you let his lack of years be no impediment to let him lack a reverend estimation, for I never knew so young a body with so old a head. I leave him to your gracious acceptance, whose trial shall better publish his commendation.
passages.vernacular: [讀。]「大人明鑒:收到大人嚟信時,我病得好重,但喺您嘅信使到來嘅嗰一刻,有一位羅馬嘅年輕博士,懷住好意嚟探望我。佢名叫巴爾薩澤。我向佢講明了猶太人同商人安東尼奧之間爭議嘅原委。我哋一起翻閱咗許多書。佢已具備我嘅意見,又加上佢自己嘅學識(其偉大我稱讚不盡),應我嘅懇求同佢同嚟,代我滿足大人嘅要求。我懇請唔好因佢年歲不足而使佢缺少應得嘅尊敬,因為我從未見過咁年輕嘅身體裝住咁老嘅頭腦。我把佢交畀大人嘅恩准,佢嘅考驗會更好地宣揚對佢嘅推薦。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: [讀。]「大人明鑒:收到大人來信時,我病得很重,但在您的信使到來的那一刻,有一位羅馬的年輕博士,懷著好意來探望我。他名叫巴爾薩澤。我向他說明了猶太人與商人安東尼奧之間爭議的原委。我們一起翻閱了許多書。他已具備我的意見,又加上他自己的學識(其偉大我稱讚不盡),應我的懇求與他同來,代我滿足大人的要求。我懇請不要因他年歲不足而使他缺少應得的尊敬,因為我從未見過這麼年輕的身體裝著這麼老的頭腦。我把他交給大人的恩准,他的考驗會更好地宣揚對他的推薦。」

passages.title: Duke of Venice 威尼斯公爵
passages.original: You hear the learn’d Bellario what he writes, And here, I take it, is the doctor come.
passages.vernacular: 你哋聽到博學嘅貝拉里奧寫嘅喇,我想,醫生到喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們聽到博學的貝拉里奧寫的了,我想,醫生到了。

passages.original: Enter Portia dressed like a doctor of laws.
passages.vernacular: [鮑西婭扮作法學博士上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [鮑西婭扮作法學博士上。]

passages.title: Duke of Venice 威尼斯公爵
passages.original: Give me your hand.
passages.vernacular: 把你嘅手畀我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把你的手給我。

passages.original: Come you from old Bellario?
passages.vernacular: 你係從老貝拉里奧嗰度嚟嘅嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是從老貝拉里奧那裡來的嗎?

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: I did, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,大人。

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: You are welcome.
passages.vernacular: 歡迎你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 歡迎你。

passages.original: Take your place.
passages.vernacular: 請就座。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請就座。

passages.original: Are you acquainted with the difference That holds this present question in the court?
passages.vernacular: 你知道喺呢法庭上引起而家呢場爭議嘅分歧嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道在這法庭上引起現在這場爭議的分歧嗎?

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: I am informed throughly of the cause.
passages.vernacular: 我已完全了解呢案件嘅原委。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我已完全了解這案件的原委。

passages.original: Which is the merchant here?
passages.vernacular: 呢度邊位係商人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡哪位是商人?

passages.original: And which the Jew?
passages.vernacular: 邊位係猶太人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哪位是猶太人?

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: Antonio and old Shylock, both stand forth.
passages.vernacular: 安東尼奧同老夏洛克,都上前。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安東尼奧和老夏洛克,都上前。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Is your name Shylock?
passages.vernacular: 你名叫夏洛克嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你名叫夏洛克嗎?

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: Shylock is my name.
passages.vernacular: 夏洛克係我嘅名字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夏洛克是我的名字。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Of a strange nature is the suit you follow, Yet in such rule that the Venetian law Cannot impugn you as you do proceed.
passages.vernacular: 你提起嘅訴訟性質奇特,然而按你進行嘅規則,威尼斯法律唔能夠反駁你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你提起的訴訟性質奇特,然而按你進行的規則,威尼斯法律不能反駁你。

passages.original: [To Antonio.]
passages.vernacular: [對安東尼奧。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對安東尼奧。]

passages.original: You stand within his danger, do you not?
passages.vernacular: 你處喺佢嘅危險之中,唔係嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你處在他的危險之中,不是嗎?

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: Ay, so he says.
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,佢咁講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,他這麼說。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Do you confess the bond?
passages.vernacular: 你承認契約嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你承認契約嗎?

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: I do.
passages.vernacular: 我承認。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我承認。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Then must the Jew be merciful.
passages.vernacular: 咁猶太人必須慈悲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼猶太人必須慈悲。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: On what compulsion must I?
passages.vernacular: 憑乜嘢強制我必須?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑什麼強制我必須?

passages.original: Tell me that.
passages.vernacular: 告訴我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 告訴我。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: The quality of mercy is not strain’d, It droppeth as the gentle rain from heaven Upon the place beneath.
passages.vernacular: 慈悲嘅品質係不受強迫嘅,佢像溫柔嘅雨從天上降下,落喺下面嘅地方。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 慈悲的品質是不受強迫的,它像溫柔的雨從天上降下,落在下面的地方。

passages.original: It is twice blest, It blesseth him that gives and him that takes.
passages.vernacular: 佢受雙重祝福,祝福施予嘅人,都祝福接受嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它受雙重祝福,祝福施予的人,也祝福接受的人。

passages.original: ’Tis mightiest in the mightiest; it becomes The throned monarch better than his crown.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺最有權勢者身上最有力量;佢比王冠更適合坐喺寶座上嘅君王。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它在最有權勢者身上最有力量;它比王冠更適合坐在寶座上的君王。

passages.original: His sceptre shows the force of temporal power, The attribute to awe and majesty, Wherein doth sit the dread and fear of kings;
passages.vernacular: 佢嘅權杖顯示世俗權力嘅力量,係令人敬畏同威嚴嘅屬性,國王嘅恐怖同畏懼就坐落其中;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他的權杖顯示世俗權力的力量,是令人敬畏和威嚴的屬性,國王的恐怖和畏懼就坐落其中;

passages.original: But mercy is above this sceptred sway, It is enthroned in the hearts of kings, It is an attribute to God himself;
passages.vernacular: 但慈悲高於呢權杖嘅統治,佢坐喺國王嘅心中,佢係上帝自己嘅屬性;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但慈悲高於這權杖的統治,它坐在國王的心中,它是上帝自己的屬性;

passages.original: And earthly power doth then show likest God’s When mercy seasons justice.
passages.vernacular: 當慈悲調和咗公正,人間嘅權力就最像上帝嘅權力。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 當慈悲調和了公正,人間的權力就最像上帝的權力。

passages.original: Therefore, Jew, Though justice be thy plea, consider this, That in the course of justice none of us Should see salvation.
passages.vernacular: 所以,猶太人,雖然你嘅訴求係公正,請考慮呢個:喺公正嘅過程中,我哋中冇一個人能得到救恩。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以,猶太人,雖然你的訴求是公正,請考慮這個:在公正的過程中,我們中沒有一個人能得到救恩。

passages.original: We do pray for mercy, And that same prayer doth teach us all to render The deeds of mercy.
passages.vernacular: 我哋祈求慈悲,而嗰同一個祈禱教導我哋所有人施行慈悲嘅行為。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們祈求慈悲,而那同一個祈禱教導我們所有人施行慈悲的行為。

passages.original: I have spoke thus much To mitigate the justice of thy plea, Which if thou follow, this strict court of Venice Must needs give sentence ’gainst the merchant there.
passages.vernacular: 我講咁多,係為了緩和你訴求嘅公正,如果你堅持,威尼斯呢個嚴格嘅法庭必然要判商人敗訴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說這麼多,是為了緩和你訴求的公正,如果你堅持,威尼斯這個嚴格的法庭必然要判商人敗訴。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: My deeds upon my head!
passages.vernacular: 我嘅行為由我自己承擔!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的行為由我自己承擔!

passages.original: I crave the law, The penalty and forfeit of my bond.
passages.vernacular: 我要求法律,我契約上嘅刑罰同罰金。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我要求法律,我契約上的刑罰和罰金。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Is he not able to discharge the money?
passages.vernacular: 佢冇能力償還呢筆錢嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他沒有能力償還這筆錢嗎?

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Yes, here I tender it for him in the court, Yea, twice the sum, if that will not suffice, I will be bound to pay it ten times o’er On forfeit of my hands, my head, my heart.
passages.vernacular: 有,我喺法庭上為佢提出,對,兩倍嘅數目,如果呢唔夠,我願意保證十倍償還,以我嘅手、我嘅頭、我嘅心作抵押。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有,我在法庭上為他提出,對,兩倍的數目,如果這不夠,我願意保證十倍償還,以我的手、我的頭、我的心作抵押。

passages.original: If this will not suffice, it must appear That malice bears down truth.
passages.vernacular: 如果呢仲唔夠,就必定顯示惡意壓倒咗真相。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果這還不夠,就必定顯示惡意壓倒了真相。

passages.original: And I beseech you, Wrest once the law to your authority.
passages.vernacular: 我懇求您,一次把法律扭轉到您嘅權威之下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我懇求您,一次把法律扭轉到您的權威之下。

passages.original: To do a great right, do a little wrong, And curb this cruel devil of his will.
passages.vernacular: 為了做一件大嘅正確,做啲小嘅錯誤,制住呢殘酷魔鬼嘅意志。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了做一件大的正確,做一點小的錯誤,制住這殘酷魔鬼的意志。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: It must not be, there is no power in Venice Can alter a decree established;
passages.vernacular: 不行,威尼斯冇任何權力能改變已確立嘅法令;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不行,威尼斯沒有任何權力能改變已確立的法令;

passages.original: ’Twill be recorded for a precedent, And many an error by the same example Will rush into the state.
passages.vernacular: 呢會被記錄作為先例,許多錯誤將同樣嘅榜樣湧入國家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這會被記錄作為先例,許多錯誤將同樣的榜樣湧入國家。

passages.original: It cannot be.
passages.vernacular: 唔可能。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不可能。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: A Daniel come to judgment!
passages.vernacular: 一位但以理嚟審判喇!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一位但以理來審判了!

passages.original: Yea, a Daniel!
passages.vernacular: 對,一位但以理!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,一位但以理!

passages.original: O wise young judge, how I do honour thee!
passages.vernacular: 啊聰明嘅年輕法官,我幾咁尊敬你!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊聰明的年輕法官,我多麼尊敬你!

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: I pray you let me look upon the bond.
passages.vernacular: 請讓我睇睇嗰契約。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請讓我看看那契約。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: Here ’tis, most reverend doctor, here it is.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢度,最可敬嘅博士,喺呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這裡,最可敬的博士,在這裡。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Shylock, there’s thrice thy money offered thee.
passages.vernacular: 夏洛克,有三倍嘅錢提供畀你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夏洛克,有三倍的錢提供給你。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: An oath, an oath!
passages.vernacular: 一個誓言,一個誓言!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個誓言,一個誓言!

passages.original: I have an oath in heaven.
passages.vernacular: 我喺天上有一個誓言。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在天上有一個誓言。

passages.original: Shall I lay perjury upon my soul?
passages.vernacular: 我該讓偽誓加喺我嘅靈魂上嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我該讓偽誓加在我的靈魂上嗎?

passages.original: No, not for Venice.
passages.vernacular: 不,為了整個威尼斯都不。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,為了整個威尼斯也不。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Why, this bond is forfeit, And lawfully by this the Jew may claim A pound of flesh, to be by him cut off Nearest the merchant’s heart.
passages.vernacular: 哎,呢契約已違約,依法猶太人可以索取一磅肉,由佢喺最靠近商人心臟嘅地方割下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎,這契約已違約,依法猶太人可以索取一磅肉,由他在最靠近商人心臟的地方割下。

passages.original: Be merciful, Take thrice thy money; bid me tear the bond.
passages.vernacular: 發發慈悲,攞三倍嘅錢;叫我撕咗契約。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 發發慈悲,拿三倍的錢;叫我撕了契約。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: When it is paid according to the tenour.
passages.vernacular: 要等按條款付清。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要等按條款付清。

passages.original: It doth appear you are a worthy judge; You know the law;
passages.vernacular: 你顯然係個稱職嘅法官;你懂法律;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你顯然是個稱職的法官;你懂法律;

passages.original: your exposition Hath been most sound.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅解釋好有理。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的解釋非常有理。

passages.original: I charge you by the law, Whereof you are a well-deserving pillar, Proceed to judgment.
passages.vernacular: 我以法律嘅名義命令你,你係法律值得稱道嘅支柱,宣布判決。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我以法律的名義命令你,你是法律值得稱道的支柱,宣布判決。

passages.original: By my soul I swear There is no power in the tongue of man To alter me.
passages.vernacular: 憑我嘅靈魂我發誓,人嘅舌頭冇力量能改變我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑我的靈魂我發誓,人的舌頭沒有力量能改變我。

passages.original: I stay here on my bond.
passages.vernacular: 我堅持我嘅契約。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我堅持我的契約。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: Most heartily I do beseech the court To give the judgment.
passages.vernacular: 我衷心懇求法庭作出判決。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我衷心懇求法庭作出判決。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Why then, thus it is: You must prepare your bosom for his knife.
passages.vernacular: 好,咁係咁樣:你必須準備好你嘅胸膛接受佢嘅刀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,那麼是這樣:你必須準備好你的胸膛接受他的刀。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: O noble judge!
passages.vernacular: 啊高貴嘅法官!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊高貴的法官!

passages.original: O excellent young man!
passages.vernacular: 啊傑出嘅年輕人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊傑出的年輕人!

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: For the intent and purpose of the law Hath full relation to the penalty, Which here appeareth due upon the bond.
passages.vernacular: 因為法律嘅意圖同目的同刑罰完全相關,呢度契約上顯示係應得嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為法律的意圖和目的與刑罰完全相關,這裡契約上顯示是應得的。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: ’Tis very true.
passages.vernacular: 好真確。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 非常真確。

passages.original: O wise and upright judge, How much more elder art thou than thy looks!
passages.vernacular: 啊聰明正直嘅法官,你比你嘅外貌老得多!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊聰明正直的法官,你比你的外貌老得多!

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Therefore lay bare your bosom.
passages.vernacular: 所以袒露你嘅胸膛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以袒露你的胸膛。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: Ay, his breast So says the bond, doth it not, noble judge?
passages.vernacular: 對,佢嘅胸膛,契約上咁講,唔係嗎,高貴嘅法官?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,他的胸膛,契約上這麼說,不是嗎,高貴的法官?

passages.original: “Nearest his heart”: those are the very words.
passages.vernacular: 「最靠近佢嘅心」:嗰個就係原話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 「最靠近他的心」:那就是原話。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: It is so.
passages.vernacular: 係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是這樣。

passages.original: Are there balance here to weigh The flesh?
passages.vernacular: 呢度有秤嚟稱肉嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡有秤來稱肉嗎?

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: I have them ready.
passages.vernacular: 我已備好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我已備好。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Have by some surgeon, Shylock, on your charge, To stop his wounds, lest he do bleed to death.
passages.vernacular: 夏洛克,你出錢請個外科醫生喺旁邊,堵住佢嘅傷口,免得佢流血而死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夏洛克,你出錢請個外科醫生在旁邊,堵住他的傷口,免得他流血而死。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: Is it so nominated in the bond?
passages.vernacular: 契約上有咁樣規定嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 契約上有這樣規定嗎?

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: It is not so express’d, but what of that?
passages.vernacular: 冇咁樣表明,但嗰又點樣?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有這樣表明,但那又怎樣?

passages.original: ’Twere good you do so much for charity.
passages.vernacular: 你出於慈善做咁啲係好嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你出於慈善做這麼一點是好的。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: I cannot find it; ’tis not in the bond.
passages.vernacular: 我找唔到;契約上冇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我找不到;契約上沒有。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: You, merchant, have you anything to say?
passages.vernacular: 你,商人,你有乜嘢要講嘅嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你,商人,你有什麼要說的嗎?

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: But little.
passages.vernacular: 好少。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 很少。

passages.original: I am arm’d and well prepar’d.
passages.vernacular: 我已武裝好,準備充分。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我已武裝好,準備充分。

passages.original: Give me your hand, Bassanio.
passages.vernacular: 把你嘅手畀我,巴薩尼奧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把你的手給我,巴薩尼奧。

passages.original: Fare you well, Grieve not that I am fallen to this for you, For herein Fortune shows herself more kind Than is her custom:
passages.vernacular: 再會,唔好為我為你落到呢地步而悲傷,因為喺呢件事上命運顯得比佢平常更仁慈:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再會,不要為我為你落到這地步而悲傷,因為在這件事上命運顯得比她平常更仁慈:

passages.original: it is still her use To let the wretched man outlive his wealth, To view with hollow eye and wrinkled brow An age of poverty, from which ling’ring penance Of such misery doth she cut me off.
passages.vernacular: 佢一向嘅習慣係讓不幸嘅人活過佢嘅財富,用空洞嘅眼睛同滿係皺紋嘅額頭睇一個貧窮嘅老年,而呢種緩慢嘅悲慘折磨佢為我剪斷喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她一向的習慣是讓不幸的人活過他的財富,用空洞的眼睛和滿是皺紋的額頭看一個貧窮的老年,而這種緩慢的悲慘折磨她為我剪斷了。

passages.original: Commend me to your honourable wife, Tell her the process of Antonio’s end, Say how I lov’d you, speak me fair in death.
passages.vernacular: 代我向你可敬嘅夫人問候,告訴佢安東尼奧結局嘅經過,講我幾咁愛你,喺我死後替我講好話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 代我向你可敬的夫人問候,告訴她安東尼奧結局的經過,說我多麼愛你,在我死後替我說好話。

passages.original: And when the tale is told, bid her be judge Whether Bassanio had not once a love.
passages.vernacular: 等故事講完,叫佢評判一下,巴薩尼奧係咪曾有過一位朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等故事講完,叫她評判一下,巴薩尼奧是否曾有過一位朋友。

passages.original: Repent but you that you shall lose your friend And he repents not that he pays your debt.
passages.vernacular: 你只要後悔你將失去你嘅朋友,佢不後悔為你還債。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你只要後悔你將失去你的朋友,他不後悔為你還債。

passages.original: For if the Jew do cut but deep enough, I’ll pay it instantly with all my heart.
passages.vernacular: 因為如果猶太人割得夠深,我會即刻衷心償還。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為如果猶太人割得夠深,我會立刻衷心償還。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Antonio, I am married to a wife Which is as dear to me as life itself, But life itself, my wife, and all the world, Are not with me esteem’d above thy life.
passages.vernacular: 安東尼奧,我娶咗一位妻子,佢對我同生命一樣珍貴,但生命本身、我嘅妻子同全世界,喺我心中都不比你嘅生命更貴重。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安東尼奧,我娶了一位妻子,她對我和生命一樣珍貴,但生命本身、我的妻子和全世界,在我心中都不比你的生命更貴重。

passages.original: I would lose all, ay, sacrifice them all Here to this devil, to deliver you.
passages.vernacular: 我願失去一切,對,把佢哋全部獻畀呢度嘅魔鬼,嚟救你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我願失去一切,對,把它們全部獻給這裡的魔鬼,來救你。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Your wife would give you little thanks for that If she were by to hear you make the offer.
passages.vernacular: 你妻子若喺旁邊聽見你咁樣提議,唔會太感謝你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你妻子若在旁邊聽見你這樣提議,不會太感謝你。

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: I have a wife who I protest I love.
passages.vernacular: 我有個妻子,我發誓我愛佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有個妻子,我發誓我愛她。

passages.original: I would she were in heaven, so she could Entreat some power to change this currish Jew.
passages.vernacular: 我但願佢喺天堂,咁樣佢可以懇求某種力量改變呢條狗般嘅猶太人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我但願她在天堂,這樣她可以懇求某種力量改變這條狗般的猶太人。

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: ’Tis well you offer it behind her back, The wish would make else an unquiet house.
passages.vernacular: 你係喺佢背後提議嘅,呢個好好,否則呢個願望會使家裡唔得安寧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是在她背後提議的,這很好,否則這個願望會使家裡不得安寧。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: These be the Christian husbands!
passages.vernacular: 呢啲就係基督徒嘅丈夫!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些就是基督徒的丈夫!

passages.original: I have a daughter— Would any of the stock of Barabbas Had been her husband, rather than a Christian!
passages.vernacular: 我有一個女兒——但願佢嫁嘅係巴拉巴嘅後代,而唔係基督徒!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我有一個女兒——但願她嫁的是巴拉巴的後代,而不是基督徒!

passages.original: We trifle time, I pray thee, pursue sentence.
passages.vernacular: 我哋喺浪費時間,請你宣布判決。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們在浪費時間,請你宣布判決。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: A pound of that same merchant’s flesh is thine, The court awards it and the law doth give it.
passages.vernacular: 嗰商人嘅一磅肉係你嘅,法庭判畀你,法律畀予你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那商人的一磅肉是你的,法庭判給你,法律給予你。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: Most rightful judge!
passages.vernacular: 最公正嘅法官!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最公正的法官!

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: And you must cut this flesh from off his breast.
passages.vernacular: 你必須從佢胸膛上割下呢塊肉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你必須從他胸膛上割下這塊肉。

passages.original: The law allows it and the court awards it.
passages.vernacular: 法律允許,法庭判畀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 法律允許,法庭判給。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: Most learned judge! A sentence!
passages.vernacular: 最博學嘅法官!一個判決!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最博學的法官!一個判決!

passages.original: Come, prepare.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,準備。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,準備。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Tarry a little, there is something else.
passages.vernacular: 稍等,仲有別嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 稍等,還有別的。

passages.original: This bond doth give thee here no jot of blood.
passages.vernacular: 呢契約喺呢度不畀你一絲血。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這契約在這裡不給你一絲血。

passages.original: The words expressly are “a pound of flesh”: Take then thy bond, take thou thy pound of flesh, But in the cutting it, if thou dost shed One drop of Christian blood, thy lands and goods Are, by the laws of Venice, confiscate Unto the state of Venice.
passages.vernacular: 話語明確係「一磅肉」:咁攞你嘅契約,攞你嘅一磅肉,但割嘅時候,如果你流出一滴基督徒嘅血,你嘅土地同財產,依威尼斯嘅法律,將被沒收歸威尼斯國家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 話語明確是「一磅肉」:那麼拿你的契約,拿你的一磅肉,但割的時候,如果你流出一滴基督徒的血,你的土地和財產,依威尼斯的法律,將被沒收歸威尼斯國家。

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: O upright judge! Mark, Jew.
passages.vernacular: 啊正直嘅法官!注意,猶太人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊正直的法官!注意,猶太人。

passages.original: O learned judge!
passages.vernacular: 啊博學嘅法官!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊博學的法官!

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: Is that the law?
passages.vernacular: 呢個係法律嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是法律嗎?

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Thyself shalt see the act.
passages.vernacular: 你自己將睇到呢條文。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你自己將看到這條文。

passages.original: For, as thou urgest justice, be assur’d Thou shalt have justice more than thou desir’st.
passages.vernacular: 因為,你既然要求公正,你要確信,你得到嘅公正比你所希望嘅更多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為,你既然要求公正,你要確信,你得到的公正比你所希望的更多。

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: O learned judge!
passages.vernacular: 啊博學嘅法官!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊博學的法官!

passages.original: Mark, Jew, a learned judge!
passages.vernacular: 注意,猶太人,一位博學嘅法官!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 注意,猶太人,一位博學的法官!

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: I take this offer then.
passages.vernacular: 嗰我接受呢個提議。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那我接受這個提議。

passages.original: Pay the bond thrice And let the Christian go.
passages.vernacular: 付三倍契約嘅錢,放呢基督徒走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 付三倍契約的錢,放這基督徒走。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Here is the money.
passages.vernacular: 錢喺呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 錢在這裡。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Soft!
passages.vernacular: 慢住!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 慢著!

passages.original: The Jew shall have all justice. Soft! no haste!
passages.vernacular: 猶太人將得到全部公正。慢住!別急!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 猶太人將得到全部公正。慢著!別急!

passages.original: He shall have nothing but the penalty.
passages.vernacular: 佢只能得到刑罰。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他只能得到刑罰。

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: O Jew, an upright judge, a learned judge!
passages.vernacular: 啊猶太人,一位正直嘅法官,一位博學嘅法官!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊猶太人,一位正直的法官,一位博學的法官!

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Therefore prepare thee to cut off the flesh.
passages.vernacular: 所以準備好割下嗰塊肉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以準備好割下那塊肉。

passages.original: Shed thou no blood, nor cut thou less nor more, But just a pound of flesh:
passages.vernacular: 不許流血,割嘅不多不少,恰好一磅肉:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不許流血,割的不多不少,恰好一磅肉:

passages.original: if thou tak’st more Or less than a just pound, be it but so much As makes it light or heavy in the substance, Or the division of the twentieth part Of one poor scruple, nay, if the scale do turn But in the estimation of a hair, Thou diest, and all thy goods are confiscate.
passages.vernacular: 如果你割得多啲或少啲,即使只差到使佢喺重量上輕啲或重啲,或差到一個小錢嘅二十分之一嘅分量,不,如果秤只偏咗一根頭髮嘅估量,你就死,你所有財產被沒收。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你割得多一點或少一點,即使只差到使它在重量上輕一點或重一點,或差到一個小錢的二十分之一的分量,不,如果秤只偏了一根頭髮的估量,你就死,你所有財產被沒收。

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: A second Daniel, a Daniel, Jew!
passages.vernacular: 第二位但以理,一位但以理,猶太人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 第二位但以理,一位但以理,猶太人!

passages.original: Now, infidel, I have you on the hip.
passages.vernacular: 而家,異教徒,我抓住你嘅把柄喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,異教徒,我抓住你的把柄了。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Why doth the Jew pause?
passages.vernacular: 猶太人點解停下?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 猶太人為什麼停下?

passages.original: Take thy forfeiture.
passages.vernacular: 攞你嘅罰金吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拿你的罰金吧。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: Give me my principal, and let me go.
passages.vernacular: 把我嘅本金畀我,讓我走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把我的本金給我,讓我走。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: I have it ready for thee. Here it is.
passages.vernacular: 我為你備好喇。喺呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我為你備好了。在這裡。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: He hath refus’d it in the open court, He shall have merely justice and his bond.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺公開法庭上拒絕喇,佢只能得到純粹嘅公正同佢嘅契約。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他在公開法庭上拒絕了,他只能得到純粹的公正和他的契約。

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: A Daniel still say I, a second Daniel!
passages.vernacular: 我仍講一位但以理,第二位但以理!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我仍說一位但以理,第二位但以理!

passages.original: I thank thee, Jew, for teaching me that word.
passages.vernacular: 猶太人,我謝謝你教我呢個詞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 猶太人,我謝謝你教我這個詞。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: Shall I not have barely my principal?
passages.vernacular: 我難道連本金都攞唔到嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我難道連本金都拿不到嗎?

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Thou shalt have nothing but the forfeiture To be so taken at thy peril, Jew.
passages.vernacular: 你乜嘢都攞唔到,只有罰金,而且要冒你嘅風險去取,猶太人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你什麼也拿不到,只有罰金,而且要冒你的風險去取,猶太人。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: Why, then the devil give him good of it!
passages.vernacular: 哎,咁讓魔鬼賜佢好處吧!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎,那麼讓魔鬼賜他好處吧!

passages.original: I’ll stay no longer question.
passages.vernacular: 我唔再留下追問喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不再留下追問了。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Tarry, Jew.
passages.vernacular: 等一等,猶太人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等一等,猶太人。

passages.original: The law hath yet another hold on you.
passages.vernacular: 法律對你仲有另一個抓手。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 法律對你還有另一個抓手。

passages.original: It is enacted in the laws of Venice, If it be proved against an alien That by direct or indirect attempts He seek the life of any citizen, The party ’gainst the which he doth contrive Shall seize one half his goods;
passages.vernacular: 威尼斯嘅法律規定,如果證明一個外邦人以直接或間接嘅企圖謀害任何公民嘅性命,被佢謀算嘅一方將奪取佢一半財產;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 威尼斯的法律規定,如果證明一個外邦人以直接或間接的企圖謀害任何公民的性命,被他謀算的一方將奪取他一半財產;

passages.original: the other half Comes to the privy coffer of the state, And the offender’s life lies in the mercy Of the Duke only, ’gainst all other voice.
passages.vernacular: 另一半歸國家嘅私庫,而犯人嘅性命只憑公爵嘅憐憫,不聽其他任何聲音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 另一半歸國家的私庫,而犯人的性命只憑公爵的憐憫,不聽其他任何聲音。

passages.original: In which predicament I say thou stand’st; For it appears by manifest proceeding That indirectly, and directly too, Thou hast contrived against the very life Of the defendant;
passages.vernacular: 我講你就處喺呢種境地;因為從明顯嘅訴訟過程睇來,你間接地、都直接地,謀算被告嘅性命;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說你就處在這種境地;因為從明顯的訴訟過程看來,你間接地、也直接地,謀算被告的性命;

passages.original: and thou hast incurr’d The danger formerly by me rehears’d.
passages.vernacular: 你已招致我先前所講嘅危險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你已招致我先前所說的危險。

passages.original: Down, therefore, and beg mercy of the Duke.
passages.vernacular: 所以,跪下,向公爵乞求憐憫。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以,跪下,向公爵乞求憐憫。

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: Beg that thou mayst have leave to hang thyself, And yet, thy wealth being forfeit to the state, Thou hast not left the value of a cord;
passages.vernacular: 乞求你得以自縊,然而你嘅財產已被國家沒收,你連一根繩子嘅價值都冇剩下;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 乞求你得以自縊,然而你的財產已被國家沒收,你連一根繩子的價值都沒剩下;

passages.original: Therefore thou must be hang’d at the state’s charge.
passages.vernacular: 所以你必須由國家出錢被吊死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以你必須由國家出錢被吊死。

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: That thou shalt see the difference of our spirit, I pardon thee thy life before thou ask it.
passages.vernacular: 為了讓你睇到我哋精神嘅不同,我喺你開口前就赦免你嘅性命。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了讓你看到我們精神的不同,我在你開口前就赦免你的性命。

passages.original: For half thy wealth, it is Antonio’s; The other half comes to the general state, Which humbleness may drive unto a fine.
passages.vernacular: 至於你嘅一半財產,歸安東尼奧;另一半歸國家,謙卑可以使佢減為罰款。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 至於你的一半財產,歸安東尼奧;另一半歸國家,謙卑可以使它減為罰款。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Ay, for the state, not for Antonio.
passages.vernacular: 對,歸國家,不歸安東尼奧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,歸國家,不歸安東尼奧。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: Nay, take my life and all, pardon not that.
passages.vernacular: 不,把我嘅命同一切都攞去,唔好赦免嗰個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,把我的命和一切都拿去,不要赦免那個。

passages.original: You take my house when you do take the prop That doth sustain my house;
passages.vernacular: 你哋攞走支撐我房子嘅支柱,就係攞走我嘅房子;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們拿走支撐我房子的支柱,就是拿走我的房子;

passages.original: you take my life When you do take the means whereby I live.
passages.vernacular: 你哋攞走我賴以生活嘅手段,就係攞走我嘅命。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們拿走我賴以生活的手段,就是拿走我的命。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: What mercy can you render him, Antonio?
passages.vernacular: 安東尼奧,你能對佢施乜嘢慈悲?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安東尼奧,你能對他施什麼慈悲?

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: A halter gratis, nothing else, for God’s sake!
passages.vernacular: 一條白畀嘅絞索,別嘅冇,睇喺上帝嘅份上!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一條白給的絞索,別的沒有,看在上帝的份上!

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: So please my lord the Duke and all the court To quit the fine for one half of his goods, I am content, so he will let me have The other half in use, to render it Upon his death unto the gentleman That lately stole his daughter.
passages.vernacular: 如果公爵大人同全體法庭同意免去佢一半財產嘅罰款,我樂意,只要佢讓我用另一半,喺佢死後轉交畀最近偷走佢女兒嘅嗰位紳士。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果公爵大人和全體法庭同意免去他一半財產的罰款,我樂意,只要他讓我用另一半,在他死後轉交給最近偷走他女兒的那位紳士。

passages.original: Two things provided more, that for this favour, He presently become a Christian;
passages.vernacular: 另外兩個條件,為了呢份恩惠,佢即刻成為基督徒;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 另外兩個條件,為了這份恩惠,他立刻成為基督徒;

passages.original: The other, that he do record a gift, Here in the court, of all he dies possess’d Unto his son Lorenzo and his daughter.
passages.vernacular: 另一個係,佢喺法庭上立下遺贈契約,把佢死時所擁有嘅一切留畀佢兒子羅倫佐同佢女兒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 另一個是,他在法庭上立下遺贈契約,把他死時所擁有的一切留給他兒子羅倫佐和他女兒。

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: He shall do this, or else I do recant The pardon that I late pronounced here.
passages.vernacular: 佢必須咁樣做,否則我撤回我頭先宣布嘅赦免。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他必須這樣做,否則我撤回我剛才宣布的赦免。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Art thou contented, Jew?
passages.vernacular: 你滿意嗎,猶太人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你滿意嗎,猶太人?

passages.original: What dost thou say?
passages.vernacular: 你講乜嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說什麼?

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: I am content.
passages.vernacular: 我滿意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我滿意。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Clerk, draw a deed of gift.
passages.vernacular: 書記,起草一份贈同契約。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 書記,起草一份贈與契約。

passages.title: Shylock 夏洛克
passages.original: I pray you give me leave to go from hence; I am not well;
passages.vernacular: 請准許我離開呢度;我不舒服;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請准許我離開這裡;我不舒服;

passages.original: send the deed after me And I will sign it.
passages.vernacular: 把契約送到我後面,我會簽字。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把契約送到我後面,我會簽字。

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: Get thee gone, but do it.
passages.vernacular: 去吧,但要辦到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去吧,但要辦到。

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: In christ’ning shalt thou have two god-fathers.
passages.vernacular: 受洗時你將有兩個教父。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 受洗時你將有兩個教父。

passages.original: Had I been judge, thou shouldst have had ten more, To bring thee to the gallows, not to the font.
passages.vernacular: 若係我當法官,你會多得十個,帶你上絞架,而唔係洗禮盆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 若是我當法官,你會多得十個,帶你上絞架,而不是洗禮盆。

passages.original: [Exit Shylock.]
passages.vernacular: [夏洛克下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [夏洛克下。]

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: Sir, I entreat you home with me to dinner.
passages.vernacular: 先生,我懇請你隨我回家食飯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生,我懇請你隨我回家吃飯。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: I humbly do desire your Grace of pardon, I must away this night toward Padua, And it is meet I presently set forth.
passages.vernacular: 我謙卑地請大人原諒,我今晚必須前往帕多瓦,我應該即刻出發。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我謙卑地請大人原諒,我今晚必須前往帕多瓦,我應該馬上出發。

passages.title: Duke 公爵
passages.original: I am sorry that your leisure serves you not.
passages.vernacular: 我好遺憾您冇空閒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我很遺憾您沒有空閒。

passages.original: Antonio, gratify this gentleman, For in my mind you are much bound to him.
passages.vernacular: 安東尼奧,酬謝呢位紳士,因為依我睇你欠佢好多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安東尼奧,酬謝這位紳士,因為依我看你欠他很多。

passages.original: [Exeunt Duke and his train.]
passages.vernacular: [公爵及其侍從下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [公爵及其侍從下。]

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Most worthy gentleman, I and my friend Have by your wisdom been this day acquitted Of grievous penalties, in lieu whereof, Three thousand ducats due unto the Jew We freely cope your courteous pains withal.
passages.vernacular: 最可敬嘅紳士,我同我嘅朋友今日靠你嘅智慧免於可怕嘅刑罰,為此,應畀猶太人嘅三千杜卡特,我哋自願用嚟酬謝你嘅禮貌辛勞。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最可敬的紳士,我和我的朋友今日靠你的智慧免於可怕的刑罰,為此,應給猶太人的三千杜卡特,我們自願用來酬謝你的禮貌辛勞。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: And stand indebted, over and above In love and service to you evermore.
passages.vernacular: 而且我哋永遠喺愛同服務上對你負有更多嘅債。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而且我們永遠在愛和服務上對你負有更多的債。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: He is well paid that is well satisfied, And I delivering you, am satisfied, And therein do account myself well paid, My mind was never yet more mercenary.
passages.vernacular: 得到滿足嘅人就得到咗好報,我解救咗你哋,我就滿足,並因此認為自己得到好報,我嘅心從來冇更貪財過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 得到滿足的人就得到了好報,我解救了你們,我就滿足,並因此認為自己得到好報,我的心從來沒有更貪財過。

passages.original: I pray you know me when we meet again, I wish you well, and so I take my leave.
passages.vernacular: 請你下次見面時認得我,我祝你哋安好,就此告辭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你下次見面時認得我,我祝你們安好,就此告辭。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Dear sir, of force I must attempt you further.
passages.vernacular: 親愛嘅先生,我必須再勉強你一下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 親愛的先生,我必須再勉強你一下。

passages.original: Take some remembrance of us as a tribute, Not as fee.
passages.vernacular: 收下啲紀念,作為敬意,唔係酬金。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 收下一點紀念,作為敬意,不是酬金。

passages.original: Grant me two things, I pray you, Not to deny me, and to pardon me.
passages.vernacular: 請答應我兩件事,別拒絕我,並原諒我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請答應我兩件事,別拒絕我,並原諒我。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: You press me far, and therefore I will yield.
passages.vernacular: 你逼我太緊,所以我讓步。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你逼我太緊,所以我讓步。

passages.original: [To Antonio.]
passages.vernacular: [對安東尼奧。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對安東尼奧。]

passages.original: Give me your gloves, I’ll wear them for your sake.
passages.vernacular: 把你嘅手套畀我,我為了你戴佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把你的手套給我,我為了你戴它。

passages.original: [To Bassanio.]
passages.vernacular: [對巴薩尼奧。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對巴薩尼奧。]

passages.original: And, for your love, I’ll take this ring from you.
passages.vernacular: 而為了你嘅愛,我要攞你呢枚戒指。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而為了你的愛,我要拿你這枚戒指。

passages.original: Do not draw back your hand; I’ll take no more, And you in love shall not deny me this.
passages.vernacular: 唔好縮回你嘅手;我不多要,你出於愛不該拒絕我呢個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要縮回你的手;我不多要,你出於愛不該拒絕我這個。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: This ring, good sir?
passages.vernacular: 呢枚戒指,好先生?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這枚戒指,好先生?

passages.original: Alas, it is a trifle, I will not shame myself to give you this.
passages.vernacular: 唉,呢個係小嘢,我唔會羞辱自己把呢個畀你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 唉,這是小東西,我不會羞辱自己把這個給你。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: I will have nothing else but only this, And now methinks I have a mind to it.
passages.vernacular: 除咗呢個我乜嘢都唔好,而且而家我覺得我想要佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除了這個我什麼都不要,而且現在我覺得我想要它。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: There’s more depends on this than on the value.
passages.vernacular: 呢個比價值更重要。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個比價值更重要。

passages.original: The dearest ring in Venice will I give you, And find it out by proclamation, Only for this I pray you pardon me.
passages.vernacular: 我會畀你威尼斯最貴重嘅戒指,並用公告把佢找出嚟,只有呢個,我請你原諒我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會給你威尼斯最貴重的戒指,並用公告把它找出來,只有這個,我請你原諒我。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: I see, sir, you are liberal in offers.
passages.vernacular: 我明白喇,先生,你喺提供上好慷慨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我明白了,先生,你在提供上很慷慨。

passages.original: You taught me first to beg, and now methinks You teach me how a beggar should be answer’d.
passages.vernacular: 你先教我乞求,而家我想你喺教我一個乞丐該得到點樣嘅回答。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你先教我乞求,現在我想你在教我一個乞丐該得到怎樣的回答。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Good sir, this ring was given me by my wife, And when she put it on, she made me vow That I should neither sell, nor give, nor lose it.
passages.vernacular: 好先生,呢枚戒指係我妻子畀我嘅,佢畀我戴上時,要我發誓不賣、不送、不丟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好先生,這枚戒指是我妻子給我的,她給我戴上時,要我發誓不賣、不送、不丟。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: That ’scuse serves many men to save their gifts.
passages.vernacular: 呢藉口許多人用嚟保住佢哋嘅禮物。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這藉口許多人用來保住他們的禮物。

passages.original: And if your wife be not a mad-woman, And know how well I have deserv’d this ring, She would not hold out enemy for ever For giving it to me.
passages.vernacular: 而如果你嘅妻子唔係瘋女人,而且知道我幾咁配得呢枚戒指,佢唔會永遠為你把佢畀我而同你為敵。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而如果你的妻子不是瘋女人,而且知道我多麼配得這枚戒指,她不會永遠為你把它給我而與你為敵。

passages.original: Well, peace be with you!
passages.vernacular: 好吧,願平安同你哋同喺!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好吧,願平安與你們同在!

passages.original: [Exeunt Portia and Nerissa.]
passages.vernacular: [鮑西婭同尼莉莎下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [鮑西婭與尼莉莎下。]

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: My Lord Bassanio, let him have the ring.
passages.vernacular: 巴薩尼奧大人,把戒指畀佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴薩尼奧大人,把戒指給他。

passages.original: Let his deservings and my love withal Be valued ’gainst your wife’s commandment.
passages.vernacular: 讓佢嘅功勞同我嘅愛一起,抵過你妻子嘅命令。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓他的功勞和我的愛一起,抵過你妻子的命令。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Go, Gratiano, run and overtake him; Give him the ring, and bring him if thou canst Unto Antonio’s house.
passages.vernacular: 去,葛拉蒂安諾,跑去追上佢;把戒指畀佢,如果你能嘅話,帶佢到安東尼奧家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去,葛拉蒂安諾,跑去追上他;把戒指給他,如果你能的話,帶他到安東尼奧家。

passages.original: Away, make haste.
passages.vernacular: 快去,趕緊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 快去,趕緊。

passages.original: [Exit Gratiano.]
passages.vernacular: [葛拉蒂安諾下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [葛拉蒂安諾下。]

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Come, you and I will thither presently, And in the morning early will we both Fly toward Belmont.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,你同我即刻去嗰度,明早我哋倆一起飛往貝爾蒙特。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,你和我馬上去那裡,明早我們倆一起飛往貝爾蒙特。

passages.original: Come, Antonio.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,安東尼奧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,安東尼奧。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act IV, Scene II — A Street 第四幕第二場:街道

passages.original: Enter Portia and Nerissa.
passages.vernacular: [鮑西婭同尼莉莎上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [鮑西婭與尼莉莎上。]

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Inquire the Jew’s house out, give him this deed, And let him sign it, we’ll away tonight, And be a day before our husbands home.
passages.vernacular: 打聽出猶太人嘅房子,把呢份契約畀佢,讓佢簽字,我哋今晚就走,趕喺我哋丈夫回家前一天到家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 打聽出猶太人的房子,把這份契約給他,讓他簽字,我們今晚就走,趕在我們丈夫回家前一天到家。

passages.original: This deed will be well welcome to Lorenzo.
passages.vernacular: 呢份契約會好受羅倫佐歡迎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這份契約會很受羅倫佐歡迎。

passages.original: Enter Gratiano.
passages.vernacular: [葛拉蒂安諾上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [葛拉蒂安諾上。]

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: Fair sir, you are well o’erta’en.
passages.vernacular: 好先生,終於追上你喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好先生,終於追上你了。

passages.original: My Lord Bassanio upon more advice, Hath sent you here this ring, and doth entreat Your company at dinner.
passages.vernacular: 巴薩尼奧大人經再三考慮,派我把呢枚戒指送畀你,並懇請你一起食晚飯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴薩尼奧大人經再三考慮,派我把這枚戒指送給你,並懇請你一起吃晚飯。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: That cannot be; His ring I do accept most thankfully, And so I pray you tell him.
passages.vernacular: 呢唔可能;佢嘅戒指我萬分感激地接受,請你咁樣告訴佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這不可能;他的戒指我萬分感激地接受,請你這樣告訴他。

passages.original: Furthermore, I pray you show my youth old Shylock’s house.
passages.vernacular: 此外,請你帶我嘅書記去老夏洛克嘅房子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 此外,請你帶我的書記去老夏洛克的房子。

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: That will I do.
passages.vernacular: 我會嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我會的。

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: Sir, I would speak with you.
passages.vernacular: 先生,我想跟你講句話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生,我想跟你說句話。

passages.original: [Aside to Portia.]
passages.vernacular: [對鮑西婭旁白。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對鮑西婭旁白。]

passages.original: I’ll see if I can get my husband’s ring, Which I did make him swear to keep for ever.
passages.vernacular: 我嚟睇睇能唔能夠攞到我丈夫嘅戒指,嗰個係我讓佢發誓永遠保留嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我來看看能不能拿到我丈夫的戒指,那是我讓他發誓永遠保留的。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: [To Nerissa.]
passages.vernacular: [對尼莉莎。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對尼莉莎。]

passages.original: Thou mayst, I warrant.
passages.vernacular: 你可以,我保證。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你可以,我保證。

passages.original: We shall have old swearing That they did give the rings away to men;
passages.vernacular: 我哋會聽到老一套嘅發誓,講佢哋把戒指送畀咗男人;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們會聽到老一套的發誓,說他們把戒指送給了男人;

passages.original: But we’ll outface them, and outswear them too. Away! make haste!
passages.vernacular: 但我哋要用厚臉皮頂回去,發更毒嘅誓。走!快點!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我們要用厚臉皮頂回去,發更毒的誓。走!快點!

passages.original: Thou know’st where I will tarry.
passages.vernacular: 你知道我會喺邊度等你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你知道我會在哪裡等你。

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: Come, good sir, will you show me to this house?
passages.vernacular: 嚟,好先生,你能帶我到呢所房子去嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,好先生,你能帶我到這所房子去嗎?

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act V, Scene I — Belmont. The Avenue to Portia’s House 第五幕第一場:貝爾蒙特,通往鮑西婭家的林蔭道

passages.original: Enter Lorenzo and Jessica.
passages.vernacular: [羅倫佐同潔西卡上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [羅倫佐與潔西卡上。]

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: The moon shines bright.
passages.vernacular: 月亮明亮地照耀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 月亮明亮地照耀。

passages.original: In such a night as this, When the sweet wind did gently kiss the trees, And they did make no noise, in such a night, Troilus methinks mounted the Trojan walls, And sigh’d his soul toward the Grecian tents Where Cressid lay that night.
passages.vernacular: 喺咁樣嘅夜晚,當溫柔嘅風輕輕吻住樹,樹無聲響,喺咁樣嘅夜晚,我想特洛伊羅斯爬上特洛伊城牆,向希臘人帳篷嘆息佢嘅靈魂,嗰夜克瑞西達就躺喺嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這樣的夜晚,當溫柔的風輕輕吻著樹,樹無聲響,在這樣的夜晚,我想特洛伊羅斯爬上特洛伊城牆,向希臘人帳篷嘆息他的靈魂,那夜克瑞西達就躺在那裡。

passages.title: Jessica 潔西卡
passages.original: In such a night Did Thisbe fearfully o’ertrip the dew, And saw the lion’s shadow ere himself, And ran dismay’d away.
passages.vernacular: 喺咁樣嘅夜晚,提斯柏膽怯地踩過露水,先睇到獅子嘅影子,然後才睇到獅子本身,驚慌地逃走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這樣的夜晚,提斯柏膽怯地踩過露水,先看到獅子的影子,然後才看到獅子本身,驚慌地逃走。

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: In such a night Stood Dido with a willow in her hand Upon the wild sea-banks, and waft her love To come again to Carthage.
passages.vernacular: 喺咁樣嘅夜晚,狄多手持柳枝站喺荒涼嘅海岸上,招手讓佢嘅愛人回到迦太基。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這樣的夜晚,狄多手持柳枝站在荒涼的海岸上,招手讓她的愛人回到迦太基。

passages.title: Jessica 潔西卡
passages.original: In such a night Medea gathered the enchanted herbs That did renew old Æson.
passages.vernacular: 喺咁樣嘅夜晚,美狄亞採集咗使老埃宋返老仲童嘅魔草。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這樣的夜晚,美狄亞採集了使老埃宋返老還童的魔草。

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: In such a night Did Jessica steal from the wealthy Jew, And with an unthrift love did run from Venice As far as Belmont.
passages.vernacular: 喺咁樣嘅夜晚,潔西卡從富有嘅猶太人嗰度偷走,懷住輕率嘅愛,從威尼斯一直跑到貝爾蒙特。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這樣的夜晚,潔西卡從富有的猶太人那裡偷走,懷著輕率的愛,從威尼斯一直跑到貝爾蒙特。

passages.title: Jessica 潔西卡
passages.original: In such a night Did young Lorenzo swear he loved her well, Stealing her soul with many vows of faith, And ne’er a true one.
passages.vernacular: 喺咁樣嘅夜晚,年輕嘅羅倫佐發誓佢深愛佢,用許多信誓偷走佢嘅靈魂,卻冇一句係真嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這樣的夜晚,年輕的羅倫佐發誓他深愛她,用許多信誓偷走她的靈魂,卻沒有一句是真的。

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: In such a night Did pretty Jessica, like a little shrew, Slander her love, and he forgave it her.
passages.vernacular: 喺咁樣嘅夜晚,可愛嘅潔西卡像個小潑婦,誹謗佢嘅愛人,佢原諒咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這樣的夜晚,可愛的潔西卡像個小潑婦,誹謗她的愛人,他原諒了她。

passages.title: Jessica 潔西卡
passages.original: I would out-night you did no body come; But hark, I hear the footing of a man.
passages.vernacular: 若冇人嚟,我會講得比你多過呢啲夜晚;不過聽,我聽到有人嘅腳步聲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 若沒有人來,我會說得比你多過這些夜晚;不過聽,我聽到有人的腳步聲。

passages.original: Enter Stephano.
passages.vernacular: [斯特凡諾上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [斯特凡諾上。]

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: Who comes so fast in silence of the night?
passages.vernacular: 係邊個喺夜晚嘅寂靜中咁樣急忙地嚟?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是誰在夜晚的寂靜中這樣急忙地來?

passages.title: Stephano 斯特凡諾
passages.original: A friend.
passages.vernacular: 一個朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個朋友。

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: A friend!
passages.vernacular: 一個朋友!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個朋友!

passages.original: What friend?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢朋友?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼朋友?

passages.original: Your name, I pray you, friend?
passages.vernacular: 請問你嘅名字,朋友?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請問你的名字,朋友?

passages.title: Stephano 斯特凡諾
passages.original: Stephano is my name, and I bring word My mistress will before the break of day Be here at Belmont.
passages.vernacular: 我名叫斯特凡諾,我帶嚟消息,我嘅女主人喺天亮前會到貝爾蒙特呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我名叫斯特凡諾,我帶來消息,我的女主人在天亮前會到貝爾蒙特這裡。

passages.original: She doth stray about By holy crosses where she kneels and prays For happy wedlock hours.
passages.vernacular: 佢喺神聖嘅十字架旁徘徊,跪下為幸福嘅婚姻時光祈禱。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她在神聖的十字架旁徘徊,跪下為幸福的婚姻時光祈禱。

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: Who comes with her?
passages.vernacular: 邊個同佢嚟?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰同她來?

passages.title: Stephano 斯特凡諾
passages.original: None but a holy hermit and her maid.
passages.vernacular: 除咗一位聖潔嘅隱修士同佢嘅侍女,冇別人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 除了一位聖潔的隱修士和她的侍女,沒有別人。

passages.original: I pray you is my master yet return’d?
passages.vernacular: 請問我嘅主人回嚟咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請問我的主人回來了嗎?

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: He is not, nor we have not heard from him.
passages.vernacular: 冇,我哋都冇聽到佢嘅消息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有,我們也沒聽到他的消息。

passages.original: But go we in, I pray thee, Jessica, And ceremoniously let us prepare Some welcome for the mistress of the house.
passages.vernacular: 但我哋進去吧,請你,潔西卡,讓我哋隆重地準備啲歡迎呢家女主人嘅禮節。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但我們進去吧,請你,潔西卡,讓我們隆重地準備一些歡迎這家女主人的禮節。

passages.original: Enter Launcelet.
passages.vernacular: [朗斯洛特上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [朗斯洛特上。]

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: Sola, sola! wo ha, ho! sola, sola!
passages.vernacular: 嗬,嗬!喂,哈,嗬!嗬,嗬!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗬,嗬!喂,哈,嗬!嗬,嗬!

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: Who calls?
passages.vernacular: 邊個喺叫?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 誰在叫?

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: Sola!
passages.vernacular: 嗬!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗬!

passages.original: Did you see Master Lorenzo?
passages.vernacular: 你見過羅倫佐少爺嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你見過羅倫佐少爺嗎?

passages.original: Master Lorenzo! Sola, sola!
passages.vernacular: 羅倫佐少爺!嗬,嗬!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 羅倫佐少爺!嗬,嗬!

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: Leave holloaing, man. Here!
passages.vernacular: 別喊喇,老兄。呢度!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別喊了,老兄。這裡!

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: Sola!
passages.vernacular: 嗬!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嗬!

passages.original: Where, where?
passages.vernacular: 邊度,邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哪裡,哪裡?

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: Here!
passages.vernacular: 呢度!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡!

passages.title: Launcelot 朗斯洛特
passages.original: Tell him there’s a post come from my master with his horn full of good news.
passages.vernacular: 告訴佢,有一位信使從我主人嗰度嚟,號角裡滿係好消息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 告訴他,有一位信使從我主人那裡來,號角裡滿是好消息。

passages.original: My master will be here ere morning.
passages.vernacular: 我主人天亮前會到呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我主人天亮前會到這裡。

passages.original: [Exit.]

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: Sweet soul, let’s in, and there expect their coming.
passages.vernacular: 親愛嘅靈魂,我哋進去,喺嗰度等佢哋嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 親愛的靈魂,我們進去,在那裡等他們來。

passages.original: And yet no matter; why should we go in?
passages.vernacular: 不過都無妨;我哋點解要進去?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不過也無妨;我們為什麼要進去?

passages.original: My friend Stephano, signify, I pray you, Within the house, your mistress is at hand, And bring your music forth into the air.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅朋友斯特凡諾,請你喺屋內通知,你嘅女主人快到喇,並把你嘅音樂帶到戶外。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的朋友斯特凡諾,請你在屋內通知,你的女主人快到了,並把你的音樂帶到戶外。

passages.original: [Exit Stephano.]
passages.vernacular: [斯特凡諾下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [斯特凡諾下。]

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: How sweet the moonlight sleeps upon this bank!
passages.vernacular: 月光幾咁甜美地瞓喺呢河岸上!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 月光多麼甜美地睡在這河岸上!

passages.original: Here will we sit and let the sounds of music Creep in our ears;
passages.vernacular: 我哋坐喺呢度,讓音樂嘅聲音悄悄鑽進我哋嘅耳朵;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們坐在這裡,讓音樂的聲音悄悄鑽進我們的耳朵;

passages.original: soft stillness and the night Become the touches of sweet harmony.
passages.vernacular: 柔和嘅寂靜同夜晚適合甜美同聲嘅觸動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 柔和的寂靜與夜晚適合甜美和聲的觸動。

passages.original: Sit, Jessica.
passages.vernacular: 坐下,潔西卡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 坐下,潔西卡。

passages.original: Look how the floor of heaven Is thick inlaid with patens of bright gold.
passages.vernacular: 睇天空嘅地面鑲嵌住多密嘅明亮金盤。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 看天空的地面鑲嵌著多密的明亮金盤。

passages.original: There’s not the smallest orb which thou behold’st But in his motion like an angel sings, Still quiring to the young-eyed cherubins;
passages.vernacular: 你睇到嘅最小嘅天體,運行時都像天使般歌唱,永遠同眼睛年輕嘅小天使哋合唱;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你看到的最小的天體,運行時也像天使般歌唱,永遠與眼睛年輕的小天使們合唱;

passages.original: Such harmony is in immortal souls, But whilst this muddy vesture of decay Doth grossly close it in, we cannot hear it.
passages.vernacular: 咁樣嘅和諧存在於不朽嘅靈魂中,但只要呢泥濘腐朽嘅外衣粗重地把佢包住,我哋就聽唔到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這樣的和諧存在於不朽的靈魂中,但只要這泥濘腐朽的外衣粗重地把它包住,我們就聽不到。

passages.original: Enter Musicians.
passages.vernacular: [樂師哋上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [樂師們上。]

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: Come, ho!
passages.vernacular: 嚟,喂!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,喂!

passages.original: and wake Diana with a hymn.
passages.vernacular: 用讚美詩喚醒狄安娜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 用讚美詩喚醒狄安娜。

passages.original: With sweetest touches pierce your mistress’ ear, And draw her home with music.
passages.vernacular: 用最甜美嘅觸動刺進你哋女主人嘅耳朵,用音樂把佢引回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 用最甜美的觸動刺進你們女主人的耳朵,用音樂把她引回家。

passages.original: [Music.]
passages.vernacular: [奏樂。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [奏樂。]

passages.title: Jessica 潔西卡
passages.original: I am never merry when I hear sweet music.
passages.vernacular: 我聽到甜美嘅音樂時從不快樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽到甜美的音樂時從不快樂。

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: The reason is, your spirits are attentive.
passages.vernacular: 原因係你嘅精神係專注嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 原因是你的精神是專注的。

passages.original: For do but note a wild and wanton herd Or race of youthful and unhandled colts, Fetching mad bounds, bellowing and neighing loud, Which is the hot condition of their blood, If they but hear perchance a trumpet sound, Or any air of music touch their ears, You shall perceive them make a mutual stand, Their savage eyes turn’d to a modest gaze By the sweet power of music:
passages.vernacular: 因為只要注意一群野性放縱嘅牲口或一群年輕未馴嘅小馬,發瘋般地蹦跳、咆哮、嘶鳴,嗰個係佢哋血液嘅熱性,如果佢哋偶然聽到號角聲,或任何音樂嘅調子觸到佢哋嘅耳朵,你會睇到佢哋一起站住,佢哋野性嘅眼睛因音樂甜美嘅力量變成溫順嘅凝視:
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為只要注意一群野性放縱的牲口或一群年輕未馴的小馬,發瘋般地蹦跳、咆哮、嘶鳴,那是它們血液的熱性,如果它們偶然聽到號角聲,或任何音樂的調子觸到它們的耳朵,你會看到它們一起站住,它們野性的眼睛因音樂甜美的力量變成溫順的凝視:

passages.original: therefore the poet Did feign that Orpheus drew trees, stones, and floods, Since naught so stockish, hard, and full of rage, But music for the time doth change his nature.
passages.vernacular: 所以詩人虛構講俄耳甫斯能吸引樹木、石頭同江河,因為冇乜嘢咁遲鈍、堅硬、滿係怒氣,音樂唔能夠喺一時改變佢嘅性質。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以詩人虛構說俄耳甫斯能吸引樹木、石頭和江河,因為沒有什麼這麼遲鈍、堅硬、滿是怒氣,音樂不能在一時改變它的性質。

passages.original: The man that hath no music in himself, Nor is not mov’d with concord of sweet sounds, Is fit for treasons, stratagems, and spoils;
passages.vernacular: 心中冇音樂、不被甜美聲音嘅和諧所感動嘅人,適合做叛國、陰謀同掠奪嘅事;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 心中沒有音樂、不被甜美聲音的和諧所感動的人,適合做叛國、陰謀和掠奪的事;

passages.original: The motions of his spirit are dull as night, And his affections dark as Erebus.
passages.vernacular: 佢精神嘅運動像夜一樣遲鈍,佢嘅感情像厄瑞玻斯一樣黑暗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他精神的運動像夜一樣遲鈍,他的感情像厄瑞玻斯一樣黑暗。

passages.original: Let no such man be trusted.
passages.vernacular: 唔好信任咁樣嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要信任這樣的人。

passages.original: Mark the music.
passages.vernacular: 注意聽音樂。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 注意聽音樂。

passages.original: Enter Portia and Nerissa.
passages.vernacular: [鮑西婭同尼莉莎上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [鮑西婭與尼莉莎上。]

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: That light we see is burning in my hall.
passages.vernacular: 我哋睇到嘅嗰光係喺我嘅大廳裡燃燒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們看到的那光是在我的大廳裡燃燒。

passages.original: How far that little candle throws his beams!
passages.vernacular: 嗰小蠟燭嘅光線能射多遠!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那小蠟燭的光線能射多遠!

passages.original: So shines a good deed in a naughty world.
passages.vernacular: 一件善行喺邪惡嘅世界裡就咁樣照耀。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一件善行在邪惡的世界裡就這樣照耀。

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: When the moon shone we did not see the candle.
passages.vernacular: 月亮照耀時我哋睇唔見蠟燭。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 月亮照耀時我們看不見蠟燭。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: So doth the greater glory dim the less.
passages.vernacular: 更大嘅光輝就咁樣使較小嘅黯然。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 更大的光輝就這樣使較小的黯然。

passages.original: A substitute shines brightly as a king Until a king be by, and then his state Empties itself, as doth an inland brook Into the main of waters. Music! hark!
passages.vernacular: 一個代理人像國王一樣明亮,直到國王在場,嗰時佢嘅威儀就像內陸小溪流入大海一樣流盡。音樂!聽!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個代理人像國王一樣明亮,直到國王在場,那時他的威儀就像內陸小溪流入大海一樣流盡。音樂!聽!

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: It is your music, madam, of the house.
passages.vernacular: 係您家嘅音樂,夫人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是您家的音樂,夫人。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Nothing is good, I see, without respect.
passages.vernacular: 我睇冇乜嘢嘢係好嘅,若冇相應嘅背景。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我看沒有什麼東西是好的,若沒有相應的背景。

passages.original: Methinks it sounds much sweeter than by day.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得佢聽起嚟比白天甜美得多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得它聽起來比白天甜美得多。

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: Silence bestows that virtue on it, madam.
passages.vernacular: 夫人,係寂靜賦予佢呢種美好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夫人,是寂靜賦予它這種美好。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: The crow doth sing as sweetly as the lark When neither is attended;
passages.vernacular: 烏鴉喺冇人注意時,唱得同雲雀一樣甜美;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 烏鴉在沒有人注意時,唱得和雲雀一樣甜美;

passages.original: and I think The nightingale, if she should sing by day When every goose is cackling, would be thought No better a musician than the wren.
passages.vernacular: 我想夜鶯如果白天唱歌,當每隻鵝都喺咯咯叫時,會被認為不比鷦鷯更好嘅音樂家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我想夜鶯如果白天唱歌,當每隻鵝都在咯咯叫時,會被認為不比鷦鷯更好的音樂家。

passages.original: How many things by season season’d are To their right praise and true perfection! Peace!
passages.vernacular: 多少事物因時節嘅調味而得到佢哋應有嘅稱讚同真正嘅完美!安靜!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 多少事物因時節的調味而得到它們應有的稱讚和真正的完美!安靜!

passages.original: How the moon sleeps with Endymion, And would not be awak’d!
passages.vernacular: 月亮點樣同恩底彌翁瞓喺一起,唔肯被喚醒!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 月亮怎樣與恩底彌翁睡在一起,不肯被喚醒!

passages.original: [Music ceases.]
passages.vernacular: [音樂停止。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [音樂停止。]

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: That is the voice, Or I am much deceiv’d, of Portia.
passages.vernacular: 嗰個係鮑西婭嘅聲音,如果我冇被騙嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那是鮑西婭的聲音,如果我沒有被騙的話。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: He knows me as the blind man knows the cuckoo, By the bad voice.
passages.vernacular: 佢認得我,就像瞎子認得杜鵑,憑嗰難聽嘅聲音。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他認得我,就像瞎子認得杜鵑,憑那難聽的聲音。

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: Dear lady, welcome home.
passages.vernacular: 親愛嘅夫人,歡迎回家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 親愛的夫人,歡迎回家。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: We have been praying for our husbands’ welfare, Which speed, we hope, the better for our words.
passages.vernacular: 我哋一直喺為丈夫哋嘅平安祈禱,希望憑我哋嘅話,佢哋能走得更順利。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們一直在為丈夫們的平安祈禱,希望憑我們的話,他們能走得更順利。

passages.original: Are they return’d?
passages.vernacular: 佢哋回嚟咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們回來了嗎?

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: Madam, they are not yet; But there is come a messenger before To signify their coming.
passages.vernacular: 夫人,仲冇;但有一位信使先嚟,通報佢哋嘅到來。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 夫人,還沒有;但有一位信使先來,通報他們的到來。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Go in, Nerissa.
passages.vernacular: 進去,尼莉莎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 進去,尼莉莎。

passages.original: Give order to my servants, that they take No note at all of our being absent hence, Nor you, Lorenzo; Jessica, nor you.
passages.vernacular: 吩咐我嘅僕人,對我哋離開呢度嘅事啲都唔好提起,你都唔好,羅倫佐;潔西卡,你都唔好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吩咐我的僕人,對我們離開這裡的事一點也不要提起,你也不要,羅倫佐;潔西卡,你也不要。

passages.original: [A tucket sounds.]
passages.vernacular: [吹號角。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [吹號角。]

passages.title: Lorenzo 羅倫佐
passages.original: Your husband is at hand, I hear his trumpet.
passages.vernacular: 你丈夫快到喇,我聽到佢嘅號角。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你丈夫快到了,我聽到他的號角。

passages.original: We are no tell-tales, madam, fear you not.
passages.vernacular: 我哋唔係多嘴嘅人,夫人,唔使怕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們不是多嘴的人,夫人,不用怕。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: This night methinks is but the daylight sick, It looks a little paler.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得呢夜晚只係生病嘅白天,佢睇起嚟稍微蒼白啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得這夜晚只是生病的白天,它看起來稍微蒼白一些。

passages.original: ’Tis a day Such as the day is when the sun is hid.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係太陽被遮住時白天嘅嗰種樣子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是太陽被遮住時白天的那種樣子。

passages.original: Enter Bassanio, Antonio, Gratiano and their Followers.
passages.vernacular: [巴薩尼奧、安東尼奧、葛拉蒂安諾及其隨從上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [巴薩尼奧、安東尼奧、葛拉蒂安諾及其隨從上。]

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: We should hold day with the Antipodes, If you would walk in absence of the sun.
passages.vernacular: 如果你喺太陽不喺時走動,我哋就能同對蹠地嘅人共享白天。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你在太陽不在時走動,我們就能與對蹠地的人共享白天。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Let me give light, but let me not be light, For a light wife doth make a heavy husband, And never be Bassanio so for me.
passages.vernacular: 讓我發光,但唔好讓我輕浮,因為輕浮嘅妻子使丈夫沉重,但願巴薩尼奧永遠唔會因我而咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我發光,但不要讓我輕浮,因為輕浮的妻子使丈夫沉重,但願巴薩尼奧永遠不會因我而這樣。

passages.original: But God sort all!
passages.vernacular: 但願上帝安排一切!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但願上帝安排一切!

passages.original: You are welcome home, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 歡迎回家,我嘅大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 歡迎回家,我的大人。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: I thank you, madam.
passages.vernacular: 謝謝你,夫人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 謝謝你,夫人。

passages.original: Give welcome to my friend.
passages.vernacular: 歡迎我嘅朋友。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 歡迎我的朋友。

passages.original: This is the man, this is Antonio, To whom I am so infinitely bound.
passages.vernacular: 呢個就係嗰位,呢個就係安東尼奧,我對佢有無限嘅債。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這就是那位,這就是安東尼奧,我對他有無限的債。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: You should in all sense be much bound to him, For, as I hear, he was much bound for you.
passages.vernacular: 按理你喺各方面都該對佢負好多債,因為,我聽講,佢為你負咗好多債(受咗好多約束)。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 按理你在各方面都該對他負很多債,因為,我聽說,他為你負了很多債(受了很多約束)。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: No more than I am well acquitted of.
passages.vernacular: 不比我已清償嘅更多。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不比我已清償的更多。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Sir, you are very welcome to our house.
passages.vernacular: 先生,好歡迎你到我哋家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生,非常歡迎你到我們家。

passages.original: It must appear in other ways than words, Therefore I scant this breathing courtesy.
passages.vernacular: 呢要喺言語之外嘅方式上顯現,所以我省略呢口頭嘅禮貌。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這要在言語之外的方式上顯現,所以我省略這口頭的禮貌。

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: [To Nerissa.]
passages.vernacular: [對尼莉莎。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [對尼莉莎。]

passages.original: By yonder moon I swear you do me wrong, In faith, I gave it to the judge’s clerk.
passages.vernacular: 憑嗰邊嘅月亮我發誓你冤枉我,講真嘅,我把佢畀咗法官嘅書記。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑那邊的月亮我發誓你冤枉我,說真的,我把它給了法官的書記。

passages.original: Would he were gelt that had it, for my part, Since you do take it, love, so much at heart.
passages.vernacular: 但願得到佢嘅人被閹喇,就我而言,既然你,愛人,咁放喺心上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但願得到它的人被閹了,就我而言,既然你,愛人,這麼放在心上。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: A quarrel, ho, already!
passages.vernacular: 吵架喇,喂,已經!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 吵架了,喂,已經!

passages.original: What’s the matter?
passages.vernacular: 點回事?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼回事?

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: About a hoop of gold, a paltry ring That she did give me, whose posy was For all the world like cutlers’ poetry Upon a knife, “Love me, and leave me not.”
passages.vernacular: 為了一個金環,一枚廉價嘅戒指,佢畀我嘅,上面嘅詩銘就像刀匠刻喺刀上嘅詩:「愛我,別離開我。」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為了一個金環,一枚廉價的戒指,她給我的,上面的詩銘就像刀匠刻在刀上的詩:「愛我,別離開我。」

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: What talk you of the posy, or the value?
passages.vernacular: 你講乜嘢詩銘,或價值?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說什麼詩銘,或價值?

passages.original: You swore to me when I did give it you, That you would wear it till your hour of death, And that it should lie with you in your grave.
passages.vernacular: 我畀你戒指時你向我發誓,你會戴到死嘅嗰一刻,佢會同你一起躺喺墳墓裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我給你戒指時你向我發誓,你會戴到死的那一刻,它會同你一起躺在墳墓裡。

passages.original: Though not for me, yet for your vehement oaths, You should have been respective and have kept it.
passages.vernacular: 即使不為我,都為你激烈嘅誓言,你該重視並好好保存。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 即使不為我,也為你激烈的誓言,你該重視並好好保存。

passages.original: Gave it a judge’s clerk!
passages.vernacular: 把佢畀咗法官嘅書記!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把它給了法官的書記!

passages.original: No, God’s my judge, The clerk will ne’er wear hair on’s face that had it.
passages.vernacular: 不,上帝係我嘅審判官,得到佢嘅嗰個書記臉上永遠唔會長毛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,上帝是我的審判官,得到它的那個書記臉上永遠不會長毛。

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: He will, and if he live to be a man.
passages.vernacular: 佢會嘅,如果佢活到成為男人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他會的,如果他活到成為男人。

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: Ay, if a woman live to be a man.
passages.vernacular: 對,如果女人活到成為男人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,如果女人活到成為男人。

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: Now, by this hand, I gave it to a youth, A kind of boy, a little scrubbed boy, No higher than thyself, the judge’s clerk, A prating boy that begg’d it as a fee, I could not for my heart deny it him.
passages.vernacular: 而家,憑呢隻手,我把佢畀咗一個年輕人,一個男孩,一個小小嘅瘦男孩,不比你高,法官嘅書記,一個多嘴嘅男孩,佢作為酬金懇求佢,我心裡實在唔能夠拒絕佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,憑這隻手,我把它給了一個年輕人,一個男孩,一個小小的瘦男孩,不比你高,法官的書記,一個多嘴的男孩,他作為酬金懇求它,我心裡實在不能拒絕他。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: You were to blame,—I must be plain with you,— To part so slightly with your wife’s first gift, A thing stuck on with oaths upon your finger, And so riveted with faith unto your flesh.
passages.vernacular: 你有錯,——我必須對你直講,——咁隨便地把你妻子第一份禮物送出去,一件用誓言貼喺你手指上嘅嘢,用信義鉚喺你肉裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你有錯,——我必須對你直說,——這麼隨便地把你妻子第一份禮物送出去,一件用誓言貼在你手指上的東西,用信義鉚在你肉裡。

passages.original: I gave my love a ring, and made him swear Never to part with it, and here he stands.
passages.vernacular: 我畀咗我嘅愛人一枚戒指,讓佢發誓永遠不離開佢,佢就站喺呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我給了我的愛人一枚戒指,讓他發誓永遠不離開它,他就站在這裡。

passages.original: I dare be sworn for him he would not leave it Nor pluck it from his finger for the wealth That the world masters.
passages.vernacular: 我敢為佢起誓,佢唔會離開佢,都唔會為世界所擁有嘅財富把佢從手指上拔下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我敢為他起誓,他不會離開它,也不會為世界所擁有的財富把它從手指上拔下來。

passages.original: Now, in faith, Gratiano, You give your wife too unkind a cause of grief, An ’twere to me I should be mad at it.
passages.vernacular: 而家,講真嘅,葛拉蒂安諾,你畀你妻子嘅悲傷理由太不友善,如果係我,我會為此發瘋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,說真的,葛拉蒂安諾,你給你妻子的悲傷理由太不友善,如果是我,我會為此發瘋。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: [Aside.]
passages.vernacular: [旁白。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [旁白。]

passages.original: Why, I were best to cut my left hand off, And swear I lost the ring defending it.
passages.vernacular: 哎,我最好把我嘅左手砍掉,發誓講我為了保護佢而丟咗戒指。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎,我最好把我的左手砍掉,發誓說我為了保護它而丟了戒指。

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: My Lord Bassanio gave his ring away Unto the judge that begg’d it, and indeed Deserv’d it too.
passages.vernacular: 巴薩尼奧大人把佢嘅戒指畀咗懇求佢嘅法官,而且佢確實都配得到。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 巴薩尼奧大人把他的戒指給了懇求它的法官,而且他確實也配得到。

passages.original: And then the boy, his clerk, That took some pains in writing, he begg’d mine, And neither man nor master would take aught But the two rings.
passages.vernacular: 然後嗰細路,佢嘅書記,寫字仲花咗些力氣,佢懇求我嘅,而佢同佢主人除咗呢兩枚戒指乜嘢都唔肯要。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 然後那孩子,他的書記,寫字還花了些力氣,他懇求我的,而他和他主人除了這兩枚戒指什麼都不肯要。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: What ring gave you, my lord?
passages.vernacular: 大人,你畀咗乜嘢戒指?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,你給了什麼戒指?

passages.original: Not that, I hope, which you receiv’d of me.
passages.vernacular: 我希望唔係你從我呢度得到嘅嗰枚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我希望不是你從我這裡得到的那枚。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: If I could add a lie unto a fault, I would deny it, but you see my finger Hath not the ring upon it, it is gone.
passages.vernacular: 如果我能喺過錯上再添一個謊,我就否認,但你睇我嘅手指上冇戒指,佢冇喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果我能在過錯上再添一個謊,我就否認,但你看我的手指上沒有戒指,它沒有了。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Even so void is your false heart of truth.
passages.vernacular: 你虛假嘅心都正是咁樣空空冇真實。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你虛假的心也正是這樣空空沒有真實。

passages.original: By heaven, I will ne’er come in your bed Until I see the ring.
passages.vernacular: 憑上天,我唔會上你嘅床,直到我睇到嗰枚戒指。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑上天,我不會上你的床,直到我看到那枚戒指。

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: Nor I in yours Till I again see mine!
passages.vernacular: 我都不上你嘅,直到我再睇見我嘅!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也不上你的,直到我再看見我的!

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Sweet Portia, If you did know to whom I gave the ring, If you did know for whom I gave the ring, And would conceive for what I gave the ring, And how unwillingly I left the ring, When nought would be accepted but the ring, You would abate the strength of your displeasure.
passages.vernacular: 親愛嘅鮑西婭,如果你知道我把戒指畀咗邊個,如果你知道我為邊個畀咗戒指,並能想到我點解畀咗戒指,我點樣不情願地離開戒指,當除咗戒指乜嘢都不被接受時,你就會減輕你不悅嘅力度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 親愛的鮑西婭,如果你知道我把戒指給了誰,如果你知道我為誰給了戒指,並能想到我為什麼給了戒指,我怎樣不情願地離開戒指,當除了戒指什麼都不被接受時,你就會減輕你不悅的力度。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: If you had known the virtue of the ring, Or half her worthiness that gave the ring, Or your own honour to contain the ring, You would not then have parted with the ring.
passages.vernacular: 如果你知道戒指嘅價值,或畀你戒指嗰位嘅一半價值,或你保住戒指嘅自身榮譽,你就唔會同戒指分離。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你知道戒指的價值,或給你戒指那位的一半價值,或你保住戒指的自身榮譽,你就不會與戒指分離。

passages.original: What man is there so much unreasonable, If you had pleas’d to have defended it With any terms of zeal, wanted the modesty To urge the thing held as a ceremony?
passages.vernacular: 有邊個人咁樣不講理,如果你樂意以任何熱誠嘅措辭保護佢,會冇羞恥心去強求呢被視為儀式嘅嘢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 有哪個人這樣不講理,如果你樂意以任何熱誠的措辭保護它,會沒有羞恥心去強求這被視為儀式的東西?

passages.original: Nerissa teaches me what to believe: I’ll die for’t but some woman had the ring.
passages.vernacular: 尼莉莎教我該相信乜嘢:我敢以性命打賭,有個女人得到咗戒指。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 尼莉莎教我該相信什麼:我敢以性命打賭,有個女人得到了戒指。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: No, by my honour, madam, by my soul, No woman had it, but a civil doctor, Which did refuse three thousand ducats of me, And begg’d the ring, the which I did deny him, And suffer’d him to go displeas’d away, Even he that had held up the very life Of my dear friend.
passages.vernacular: 不,憑我嘅榮譽,夫人,憑我嘅靈魂,冇女人得到佢,而係一位有禮嘅博士,佢拒絕咗我三千杜卡特,卻懇求戒指,我拒絕咗佢,讓佢不悅地離開,就係佢,保住咗我親愛朋友嘅性命。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,憑我的榮譽,夫人,憑我的靈魂,沒有女人得到它,而是一位有禮的博士,他拒絕了我三千杜卡特,卻懇求戒指,我拒絕了他,讓他不悅地離開,就是他,保住了我親愛朋友的性命。

passages.original: What should I say, sweet lady?
passages.vernacular: 我該講乜嘢,親愛嘅夫人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我該說什麼,親愛的夫人?

passages.original: I was enforc’d to send it after him.
passages.vernacular: 我被迫把佢送去追上佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我被迫把它送去追上他。

passages.original: I was beset with shame and courtesy.
passages.vernacular: 我被羞愧同禮貌包圍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我被羞愧和禮貌包圍。

passages.original: My honour would not let ingratitude So much besmear it.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅榮譽唔容忘恩負義咁樣玷污佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的榮譽不容忘恩負義這樣玷污它。

passages.original: Pardon me, good lady; For by these blessed candles of the night, Had you been there, I think you would have begg’d The ring of me to give the worthy doctor.
passages.vernacular: 原諒我,好夫人;因為憑呢夜嘅神聖蠟燭,如果你當時在場,我想你都會向我懇求嗰枚戒指,送畀嗰位可敬嘅博士。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 原諒我,好夫人;因為憑這夜的神聖蠟燭,如果你當時在場,我想你也會向我懇求那枚戒指,送給那位可敬的博士。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Let not that doctor e’er come near my house, Since he hath got the jewel that I loved, And that which you did swear to keep for me, I will become as liberal as you, I’ll not deny him anything I have, No, not my body, nor my husband’s bed.
passages.vernacular: 唔好畀嗰位博士靠近我嘅家,既然佢得到咗我所愛嘅珠寶,你曾向我發誓為我保存嘅,我都要像你一樣慷慨,我乜嘢都唔會拒絕佢,對,連我嘅身體、我丈夫嘅床都不拒絕。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別讓那位博士靠近我的家,既然他得到了我所愛的珠寶,你曾向我發誓為我保存的,我也要像你一樣慷慨,我什麼都不會拒絕他,對,連我的身體、我丈夫的床都不拒絕。

passages.original: Know him I shall, I am well sure of it.
passages.vernacular: 我一定會認得佢,我好確定。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我一定會認得他,我很確定。

passages.original: Lie not a night from home.
passages.vernacular: 一夜唔好離家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一夜不要離家。

passages.original: Watch me like Argus, If you do not, if I be left alone, Now by mine honour which is yet mine own, I’ll have that doctor for mine bedfellow.
passages.vernacular: 像阿耳戈斯嗰樣睇住我,如果你不,如果我被獨自留下,憑我仍屬於我自己嘅榮譽,我要嗰位博士做我嘅床伴。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 像阿耳戈斯那樣看住我,如果你不,如果我被獨自留下,憑我仍屬於我自己的榮譽,我要那位博士做我的床伴。

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: And I his clerk.
passages.vernacular: 而我要佢嘅書記。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 而我要他的書記。

passages.original: Therefore be well advis’d How you do leave me to mine own protection.
passages.vernacular: 所以要小心,你點樣把我留下由我自己保護。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 所以要小心,你怎樣把我留下由我自己保護。

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: Well, do you so.
passages.vernacular: 好,你就咁樣做吧。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,你就這樣做吧。

passages.original: Let not me take him then, For if I do, I’ll mar the young clerk’s pen.
passages.vernacular: 嗰就唔好畀我抓到佢,因為如果我抓到,我要毀掉嗰年輕書記嘅筆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那就別讓我抓到他,因為如果我抓到,我要毀掉那年輕書記的筆。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: I am th’ unhappy subject of these quarrels.
passages.vernacular: 我係呢啲爭吵嘅不幸主角。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是這些爭吵的不幸主角。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Sir, grieve not you.
passages.vernacular: 先生,您唔使悲傷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生,您不必悲傷。

passages.original: You are welcome notwithstanding.
passages.vernacular: 儘管如此,您仍然受歡迎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 儘管如此,您仍然受歡迎。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Portia, forgive me this enforced wrong, And in the hearing of these many friends I swear to thee, even by thine own fair eyes, Wherein I see myself—
passages.vernacular: 鮑西婭,原諒我呢被迫嘅過錯,當住呢許多朋友嘅面,我向你發誓,憑你自己美麗嘅眼睛,我喺其中睇見自己——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 鮑西婭,原諒我這被迫的過錯,當著這許多朋友的面,我向你發誓,憑你自己美麗的眼睛,我在其中看見自己——

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Mark you but that!
passages.vernacular: 注意呢個!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 注意這個!

passages.original: In both my eyes he doubly sees himself, In each eye one.
passages.vernacular: 喺我兩隻眼睛裡佢睇見雙重嘅自己,每隻眼裡一個。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在我兩隻眼睛裡他看見雙重的自己,每隻眼裡一個。

passages.original: Swear by your double self, And there’s an oath of credit.
passages.vernacular: 憑你嘅雙重自己發誓吧,嗰才係可信嘅誓言。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑你的雙重自己發誓吧,那才是可信的誓言。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: Nay, but hear me.
passages.vernacular: 不,聽我講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,聽我說。

passages.original: Pardon this fault, and by my soul I swear I never more will break an oath with thee.
passages.vernacular: 原諒呢個過錯,憑我嘅靈魂我發誓,我再都不對你違背誓言。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 原諒這個過錯,憑我的靈魂我發誓,我再也不對你違背誓言。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: I once did lend my body for his wealth, Which but for him that had your husband’s ring Had quite miscarried.
passages.vernacular: 我曾為佢嘅財富借出我嘅身體,若唔係嗰得到你丈夫戒指嘅人,佢早就完喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我曾為他的財富借出我的身體,若不是那得到你丈夫戒指的人,它早就完了。

passages.original: I dare be bound again, My soul upon the forfeit, that your lord Will never more break faith advisedly.
passages.vernacular: 我敢再次擔保,以我嘅靈魂作罰金,你丈夫再都唔會故意違背信義。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我敢再次擔保,以我的靈魂作罰金,你丈夫再也不會故意違背信義。

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Then you shall be his surety.
passages.vernacular: 嗰你就做佢嘅擔保人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那你就做他的擔保人。

passages.original: Give him this, And bid him keep it better than the other.
passages.vernacular: 把呢個畀佢,叫佢比對嗰一枚更好地保存。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把這個給他,叫他比對那一枚更好地保存。

passages.title: Antonio 安東尼奧
passages.original: Here, Lord Bassanio, swear to keep this ring.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢度,巴薩尼奧大人,發誓保存呢枚戒指。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這裡,巴薩尼奧大人,發誓保存這枚戒指。

passages.title: Bassanio 巴薩尼奧
passages.original: By heaven, it is the same I gave the doctor!
passages.vernacular: 憑上天,呢個就係我畀博士嘅嗰枚!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 憑上天,這就是我給博士的那枚!

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: I had it of him: pardon me, Bassanio, For by this ring, the doctor lay with me.
passages.vernacular: 我係從佢嗰度得到嘅:原諒我,巴薩尼奧,因為憑呢枚戒指,博士同我同瞓過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是從他那裡得到的:原諒我,巴薩尼奧,因為憑這枚戒指,博士與我同睡過。

passages.title: Nerissa 尼莉莎
passages.original: And pardon me, my gentle Gratiano, For that same scrubbed boy, the doctor’s clerk, In lieu of this, last night did lie with me.
passages.vernacular: 都原諒我,我溫和嘅葛拉蒂安諾,因為嗰個瘦男孩,博士嘅書記,為了呢個,琴晚同我同瞓過。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也原諒我,我溫和的葛拉蒂安諾,因為那個瘦男孩,博士的書記,為了這個,昨晚與我同睡過。

passages.title: Gratiano 葛拉蒂安諾
passages.original: Why, this is like the mending of highways In summer, where the ways are fair enough.
passages.vernacular: 哎,呢就像夏天修路,路明明已經夠好喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎,這就像夏天修路,路明明已經夠好了。

passages.original: What, are we cuckolds ere we have deserv’d it?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,我哋喺仲冇應得之前就戴綠帽子喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,我們在還沒應得之前就戴綠帽子了?

passages.title: Portia 鮑西婭
passages.original: Speak not so grossly.
passages.vernacular: 唔好講得咁粗俗。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別說得這麼粗俗。

passages.original: You are all amaz’d.
passages.vernacular: 你哋都驚呆喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們都驚呆了。

passages.original: Here is a letter; read it at your leisure.
passages.vernacular: 呢度有一封信;請喺空閒時讀佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡有一封信;請在空閒時讀它。

passages.original: It comes from Padua from Bellario.
passages.vernacular: 佢從帕多瓦嘅貝拉里奧嗰度嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 它從帕多瓦的貝拉里奧那裡來。

passages.original: There you shall find that Portia was the doctor, Nerissa there, her clerk.
